His favorite was the paper roast dosa with mushrooms and water chestnuts and he's South Indian so I trust his opinion on dosa!

Wow! Indian accent was not what I expected in all the best ways possible. My local friend Tiffany recommended this place to us. The staff was incredibly attentive and receptive. They gave fabulous recommendations on eats and drinks based on our tastes and everything was superb. They knew we had a show to get to, and were attentive to the length of our dinner to get us there on time. I appreciate every detail they put into the service and experience from beginning to end. Also what is that coconut stuff they served at the beginning!? Oh my goodness can someone ship that to me!!? It was so unbelievably unexpected and absolutely delicious. Thank you Indian accent for being awesome!!!

Excellent food. Fresh ingredients and really nice flavors in every dish. The staff was very friendly and attentive.  Dishes were very delicious and presentation very interesting. I highly recommend the chef's menu, which delights with flavors from all over India.

Really good food and amazing service. We went with the $90 choice of 4 items. Yes that does mean you can go with 4 entrees but don't do that. Choose one dish from each section to get a feel of different textures. Between my husband and I we got 8 different items and every single one was outstanding. For the dessert the doda barfi was so amazing. The servers are very attentive and polite. The ambiance is great as well- it's not snooty or snobbish in anyway - it has a warm vibe.

The food is just OK not bad but not great either - quantity is small and price is high. Expectations should go up too. But then how can we understand why people like this place? They have not been to a better place. I would recommend Tamarind - far far better - both food and service. They goofed up on my bill - did not match and luckily I had a pic of the "Restaurant copy" but the manager Cristiano was unapologetic about their mistake which i would consider sacrilegious - changing the amount the customer signs off on should be a no-no. But I am not upset because I don't expect much out of this place - there are better places in NYC.

As I write this 5-star review of Indian Accent, I almost want to go back to all of the 5-star reviews I have written for other businesses, and knock them down a star. Few, if any, of them quite match Indian Accent with respect to the joys of dining I have experienced here. 

One thing I order on every visit is the bone marrow nihari with pathar kabab. These two dishes (nihari and pathar kabab) are traditionally served separately. For as far back into my youth as I can remember, I have ordered and eaten them together because they just tasted so good together; I have always thought of these two different delicacies as a match made in food heaven. Imagine my delight to finally discover a restaurant that shares this sentiment, and serves these items as a single, combined dish! 

For dessert, I'm always torn between the makhan malaai and the doda barfi treacle tart. 

Service is courteous and professional, and I believe reservations are required (I've never shown up without one; just didn't want to risk getting turned away and not getting my nihari/kabab fix!).

The food was average (some things excellent and others not good), but the killer here is the service. If you want to check it out, order appetizers (decent but aesthetically A++) and dessert (SO GOOD). Just don't expect the staff to be helpful or polite. Oh, and the drinks weren't anything special.

Some items on the menu were very good, including the soft shell crab, appetizers, and the conical dosa. Other items made it feel like the kitchen is still experimenting to solidify their menu. Their breaded paneer dish left something to desired, and there's really only so many ways to make some of the basic lentil dishes / palak / saag...

My main complaint was that our server was not polite, which is really unacceptable at this price point. After contacting management they partially comp'ed my meal (~50%) but with a gift card so I guess I'm forced to go back... meh

Ok.  Besides one of the dishes in our tasting menu, we enjoyed everything else including the wine pairings!  Also, presentation was beautiful and the Service was wonderful too.  We just left all too full - and might opt for a smaller tasting menu or a la carte next time.  A friend brought me here for my bday and I thought it was great.  Great place for a special evening or occasion!

Are there some solid dishes here? Yes. But does it justify the price or make you want to trade in your favorite Indian joint? Not even close. We did the four course menu and our dishes ranged from decent to good, but never spectacular. The biggest letdown was the wine pairings. Most were way too sweet and didn't do much for the food it came with. I would suggest passing on the pairings and following your own palette.

Always a pleasure to be here. 
But please take care of cold dishes to the table.
Also, when it's sent back, please do not reheat n send the same thing back. 
It really threw us off!!!

We came here on New Year's Eve and did the pre fixe with wine pairing. It was pricey, the meal with gratuity ($125 dinner, $70 wine pairing and tips) was about $250 per person...but it was so worth it. There was a LOT of food. My personal favorites were the puchka shots, the appetizers, butter chicken naan and the sarson ka saag..everything was splendid. Would definitely come back here!

Can't review the food bc we were never able to order. This is on the service and experience. Walked in and sat at the bar. Only a couple of guests were in the restaurant. The bartender was AT the bar. Literally behind the bar, but if still took her 10-15 minutes to greet us. Then poured water. No order. She eventually asked what we wanted. I got a beer. She poured it. My date ordered a glass of wine. The bartender poured a sample, then walked away. She didn't come back for 5 mins. She eventually came back and finished the pour and left again. Guess we can't order food. She was not blatantly rude, but extremely pretentious and dismissive. We were going to order good but why bother. We drank or beverage, paid and went down the street the Bengal Tiger (which was amazing BTW). Can't comment on the food but this still leaves a bad taste in my mouth. No thanks. Change your staff and/or attitude.

My review is solely for the dessert I had and the impeccable service I received. I came in rather late on a weekday night, very close to closing time but they were happy to accommodate me for dessert at the bar. I had the makkhan malai which is quite possibly one of the lightest Indian desserts I've ever had. I'm honestly not a huge indian dessert fan so this says a LOT. If I had more time in NYC I'd definitely try all of their desserts- especially that kheer, and a round 2 of makhan malai wouldn't disappoint either!

Service 5 stars. Value for money - can't ask for much given it's supposed to be high end. Ambiance - average. Food quality - mediocre at best. We had the chef tasting menu. Every dish except the fenugreek tart was OK (far from spectacular though). The fenugreek tart filled with spinach curry that really lacked in flavour. Not very impressed.

Had such a wonderful time at Indian Accent today! As a first time diner, I was not disappointed. Two friends of mine decided to stop in for lunch and boy are we glad we did. The lovely hostess, Karishma, took our coats and bags and brought us to the bar. Manny, our bartender took great care of us while also making great recommendations and keeping light conversation. 

The food was to die for. It started out with some amuse, and some pumpkin coconut shorba. Can someone get me a recipe for this?! I could eat this all day! Next I had the sweet pickles rib, it was marinated beautifully and melted in your mouth. My friends also got the sweet potato and ribs as well. We also tried the pulled jackfruit phulka. Who would've thought jackfruit tasted so good. It was almost like a little taco that was bursting at the seems with flavor. Our next course we shared dosa, prawns, black dairy dal, an aloo kulcha and naan. All tasted wonderfully, but I especially loved the scallops and prawns! We also tried the soy keema. Though the best part of the meal was the dessert, the doda barfi was simply exceptional. Coming in a close second was the meethe chawal! Overall, brilliant ideas and food.

Huge shoutout to our bartender Manny, who took care of us with all of our needs and food accommodations (one of us is vegan). Also the managers Mark and Richard both stopped by to see how we were enjoying our meal and made polite conversation. As we were leaving we thanked the chef who came up to see how we enjoyed everything. 

In the end, Karishma helped us assemble our things and thanked us all for coming. She has such a great personality and really topped off our meal. She asked for highlights of our meal and asked our overall comments on the experience. I had nothing but amazing things to say! I will certainly be back in the future! Thanks, Indian Accent!
Food and cocktails were both great. I especially enjoyed the saffron dessert. I think it's overpriced though, and service was rather slow.
One of the finest dining experiences I've had in New York. Ambiance is both warm and energetic. The food....and service.... outstanding! I'll be back for sure.
After an afternoon shopping @ 5th, we ended up in this great restaurant. A great experience & the best indian restaurant I ever visited.

An incredible tasting experience with lovely servers inside a beautifully-adorned interior. Highly, highly recommend not just as a meal but as a thorough gastronomic adventure into artfully altered Indian classics. 

As a New Year's Day treat, my family and I set off into exploring the dinner menu. We had so much fun picking apart the flavors as no dish had too much or too little complexity - just the right amount to prompt a 'there's something unusually great added to this!' Sharing our courses between us, we tried:

Appetizers
Yogurt and goat cheese kebab, pickled beet - highly recommend for the veg eaters at the table; 
Potato sphere chaat, white pea mash 
Crab claws, butter-pepper-garlic, cauliflower
Bheja fry, goat brains, khasta roti - my first time trying goat brains, and though skeptical to start, I was pleasantly surprised 

Between the apps and mains, Indian Accent includes "mid-courses," my favorite of which was the soy keema, quail egg, lime leaf butter pao combination served in a small clay pot. 

For the mains, I loved the winter vegetables, punjabi kadhi (and I have very high standards for kadhi), but the sea bass shone as the category winner.

Having tasted the most authentic Indian desserts of Amritsar, Mumbai, and Delhi, we almost ignored the dessert section entirely before being convinced by our server that we might be missing out - and he was right. The meethe chawal was unlike anything we'd tried before, finishing off our evening with another classic reinvention. 

The cocktails were incredible too, in case you opt out of the wine pairings!

Small note, my main course was served cold, but they quickly brought out a new dish once alerted.

For this much money, I expect the flavors to blow me away. Everything was good, nothing was great. Dining room is beautiful, presentation is spectacular, and service is impeccable, but I eat for the taste. 
At this price point, I expect more.

It was time to choose a fine dining,  special occasion venue for our Anniversary and usually we pick a Japanese restaurant however this time we decided to think outside the culinary box and to try something different. A quick Yelp  search for ' Best Indian fine dining restaurant ' threw up Indian Accent as the main contender. The reviews were mainly very positive so off we went .
Before arriving at the restaurant  I have to admit I conjured up images of food served in gold platters in a grand palatial  hall dimly lit  with opulent furnishings . The truth could not have been more different. The restaurant was decorated in a very modern style with a very bright light fixtures piercing down at the diners. Although we arrived 30 mins past our reservation due to the unreliability of the weekend NYC subway system , the manager gave our hostess the nod to seat us. Truth be told I was  ready to burst out in melodramatic display of emotion - the sort that might garner an Academy award had we been turned away from the restaurant. Perhaps it was just as well for the sake of the finely dressed diners who really seemed to be enjoying the food and company. 
We noticed many Indian families consisting of dad, mom and young adult children and considered that as always to be a good sign. 
Our menus arrived and my husband picked the vegetarian 8 course meal  and I went for the 8 course  meat version. The food while superb was minuscule and left us wanting for more. We felt the restaurant was well named as the food was fusion with a mere Indian accent. For example : they served little pita bites with a teaspoon of butter chicken which resembled pizza bites. One dessert was a  ( mini ) treacle tart.   
Would we return? Probably  not but as we headed out for pizza we unanimously agreed that we had a fun experience and a great albeit tiny anniversary meal.

We had reservations to celebrate a birthday. While we waited for our table we ordered drinks at bar. They had creative cocktails such as a Moscow mule with a twist and the Upsy Desi drink which was unique as well as "mocktails" such as a rose almond milk type of drink. Both were really great. We decided on the 3 course tasting menu. They brought out complimentary Chef's Tasting of roasted pumpkin shorba and blue cheese stuffed naan. Both were excellent. We ordered a bunch of vegetarian items. Our favorites were the pulled jackfruit on top of a layered bread, winter root veggies tart, lentil stew (kichdi) and the stuffed paneer makhani naan. The mushroom dosa was interesting as well as the sweet potato sphere chaat. At the end they served a tray of digestives. For dessert they put a candle on our makhan malai since we specified during reservations that we were celebrating a birthday. The staff and management were so professional and courteous. While they weren't Indian they knew the history behind the cuisine which was impressing. I highly recommend this restaurant and can't wait to come back for another special occasion.
Great food and fantastic cocktails! The food tastes very authentic. The presentation is very western. The service was good. We tried the chefs tasting menu.
I first went to the one in New Colony, Delhi and then NYC. So delicious! Order the tasting menu to sample all of the flavors. Cocktails and mocktails are amazing...

The loveliest dining experience I have had, at some moments I truly felty the food was too pretty to eat! We were asked several times if our food was okay. The server was so attentive. The chef also sent out blue cheese stuffed naan that made everything wonderful. The food was creatively presented, perfectly spiced, and just the right portion size to make it through the whole meal. I would recommend to anyone on a special occasion, it was the best way to kick off our adventure weekend.
This is one of the best Indian restaurants on east coast. Food, that makes you crave for more. Very authentic. We went for chef's menu which is worth every cent. Service was amazing as well.

Was looking for something different for a special night recently and stumbled across this restaurant listed on Zagat.

1/ It was awesome
2/ Although pricey it was nice to have a dinner in a restaurant and actually be able to hear my date and have a regular volume conversation (eg tables are nicely spread out and the height of the room means volume is nicely hushed).

We had the "tasting menu" lol have no idea how many actual courses with the various little tasting tidbits (13? 15?) but by the end we were waving the white flag and saying we surrender. Although each bite is quite small they were amazingly tasty and unique from course to course.

Out of every course they only 'missed' on two of them (eg 'duck pancake' and the 'sticky date pudding') but every other dish I'd very willingly come back for - including some that I'm coming back to particularly try.

Highly recommend.

This place is a gastronomical delight. Great quality of service, innovative food essentially Indian but served in a way that feels western. I tried the bheja fry as an appetizer as well as chicken kofta and Kadi for the main course. The cocktails are different so I will not have them again and stay with flavors I am familiar with. I'd recommend his place despite the price. You guys need to open a place in San Francisco too.

This place is a gem - great, interesting food and attentive, informed service. We enjoyed our meal, drinks and service. Last night was my 3rd trip for dinner, and it did not disappoint. The flavors are amazing, the presentation is top notch, and the ambiance is casual elegance. Dishes are complex and vary from adventurous like goat brains (delicious) to black dairy dal to beef tenderloin - but not the usual chicken tikka or lamb biryani. Highly recommend.
An amazing experience from beginning to end!  Each course more delicious than the next we will be sure to come back our next visit to NYC.

Came here for dinner. So as a non Indian these are my opinions. I enjoyed the high end ambience, and a different flavor style. They have very different dishes so if you come here be ready to experiment and to enjoy some spice- everything is very spicy. I would recommend this place to someone looking at dishes and just ready to jump in and try something different, the chef is very creative. The downside to this place is the 20 mins between courses, they are very slow bringing out food.

Went for Valentine's, a set menu, but everything given was a taste of heaven and unique. My Valentine who accompanied me to dinner loved it herself and some items reminded her of food she's had in the past. It was the 2nd time I've tried Indian Food in my life. The first being at a coworkers Indian Wedding but I much younger. We had a 5 course meal of appetizers, entrees, drinks and desserts. A nice setting in the heart of Manhattan. Service was excellent and our table was ready before the reservation. A bar is located in the place in the dining room area, with a pretty decent selection of wine to choose. Would recommend on a special day like Valentine's. Two other locations exist , one being in the capital  of India; New Dehli and one in London.

Food: 5
Vibe: 5
Staff/wait time: 5

This is the best Indian restaurant in Manhattan. Their establishment is beautiful, and there is a good amount of space.

The food was excellent. Opted for the three course option. Everything we had was excellent. Things that stood out:

1. Jackfruit tacos: well balanced and flavorful
2. Potato sphere chaat - was initially skeptical but this really came through 
3. Black dal - simple but just the right amount of flavor.
4. Kheer - perfect

Overall recommend! Skip Junoon and Tamarind, this place is the spot.

Pretentious, finicky and overpriced, this restaurant is like a Wes Anderson version of Indian food, from the overly precious waitstaff to the impenetrable menu to the carefully constructed, lifeless dishes.  And the prices are utterly ridiculous.  To add insult to injury, we were charged $9 for a (microscopic) substitute side order of vegetables, without being warned (though they did take it off the bill when questioned.  Overall, an exercise in frustration.  With so many great Indian places in NYC, it's an expensive shame to waste a dinner here.
So amazing that I ordered everything on the menu and threw up the next morning, was very sad that it escaped my body.. :( will be coming back again!

TLDR version - Good food. good service. Great experience. 

Food - 4.5* ( I liked pretty much everything I tasted)
Ambiance - 4.5*
Service - 5* (this was true of every person who touched us that day, and the only other place I've gotten service that good was Alinea, a Michelin 3-star in Chicago). 

We were celebrating our anniversary with a nice dinner and the experience didn't let us down. We started with cocktails and my 'smoke and spice' came with a large chunk of ice that the restaurant cuts each day with a marigold emblazoned on top - good start.. 

From there, things only got better - our server was friendly, attentive and helpful. Guiding us towards what to order and how much to order. We compulsively photographed each dish before we ate it (because they all looked so good). 

there's may other photos so I'll pause here with a quick nod to Kristiano and an invitation to come and open a new restaurant in SF (maybe a pop-up one for 3-months)... 

Looking forward to visiting their newest branch that opened in London when I am there in a few weeks.

A long awaited visit to this restaurant turned out to stand upto my expectations. I went with a group of friends and opted for al-a-carte instead of the two-course lunch. The menu here is seasonal and exclusive. It is sweet and short with equal vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. we tried to taste as many vegetarian dishes as possible but the desserts blew us away.

We started with a complementary serving of BLUE STUFFED MINI NAAN and PUMPKIN SHORBA. In spite of these being tiny in size they were full of flavor. Not that you dont expect that from Indian food. 

Without any delay we went on to our First course, we had sweet potato shakarkandi and Yogurt and Goat cheese kebab as our firsts. Both the dishes were so good you would definitely go for seconds! The sweet potato shakkarkandi was sweet potatoes on a bed of radishes, topped with crunchy okra and some greens. quite good balance of sweet and spice. 

for seconds we ordered paper roast dosa, wild mushrooms, water chestnuts but replaced mushrooms with paneer and vegetables. This dish was pretty good as well. Also ordered winter root vegetables, sarson ka saag, fenugreek tart. I liked this better than the dosa. Flavor wise both are equally good but I would recommend getting the latter if you have to choose. We also got the black dairy daal which was rich and yumm! The paneer makhani kulcha was out of the world. Stuffing paneer in kulcha is pretty traditional but is always a good idea. 

The best part of the meal for anyone with a sweet tooth were the desserts. We had three desserts makhan malai, doda barfi treacle tart and kheer. The Makhan malai was amazingly light, with rich flavor of saffron and milk. Kheer was pretty good as well but I am personally not a fan of sweet rice but if you are thats your to go dessert. The best of all was the Doda barfi, it was a milk cake with pecan like base which was crispy and nutty. My favorite part of the meal was the doda barfi.

Overall, definitely visit once!

Best meal I've ever had.  Each bite starting with the sipping soup appetizer was an experience in itself. The service was outstanding which deserves it's own 5 star evaluation. Vegetarian tasting was out of this world and if I could eat like this every day I would consider myself rich.
Vegan's will love this place because the chief has gone above and beyond to create a special experience.

Bootlegging at fine dining prices !!


Horrible valentines experience where they took over 2 and half hours to serve the second course , messed up our bill , disregarded a bday request and continued to try and ply us with drinks all through to keep their billing up.

I wrote to their management ( email below) to which I got a standard response of them forwarding my concerns to their chef Manish Malhotra and nothing beyond. 

My email to Indian Accent Managemnt :

This is to provide you feedback on our dinner experience last evening for Valentine's Day. I had booked your restaurant three weeks ago and got a 9 pm slot for dinner for two which I had booked to celebrate my partners birthday which happens to be on Valentine's Day. 

We were first told to wait at the bar and get a drink while waiting to be seated...finally seated at 9 30 pm.

To start on a positive  note with the cocktail that was well made and presented ( Moghul Fortification) though the one we wanted Smokey something  was not available ( funny for an Indian restaurant where the flavor for a whisky based drink would be the highest amongst its patron demographic  ).

The meal was painfully slow and given that dinner was a prefixed menu where the first Course of Puchka ( pre fried flour balls with pre made chutneys  ) is not something one has to prep or cook - was served 25 mins post being seated. The portions were even smaller than a fine dining French restaurant though the prices clearly for your Valentine's Day were not in the same range as peer NYC dining establishments.
I still did not have a problem given it was a super special occasion but what really got us was the deliberate delay of each course and the trained and constant nudge to have another drink/ cocktail/ wine. The second course was finally served at 11. 18 pm ( two hours after being seated ) and that's after we had mentioned the delay twice to the staff. The dessert was again served after the customary 20 - 33 mins wait and despite instructions to have something special written on the dessert plate ( happy birthday !!) .. it was served quite perfunctorily. This is after I had gotten up and even reminded them before they served the desserts. 

Finally without embarrassing my dinner date and the birthday boy .. I got up and told the staff about the complete disregard of my request and the delay ... to which they come back with the check. On reviewing my invoice I find that I was charged for a beverage that the table next to us had !! 

The staff then comes back with the revised invoice and tells me he has given us two drink OFF for the error and offers us two glasses of complimentary prosecco at 11 55 pm !! Whilst the gesture is appreciated ... it's was nearly midnight on a weeknight and the whole reason we were still stuck there was due to the problem in the first place of the food being served in a strategically planned manner to ply the alcohol agenda to hungry customers !!

Absolutely under par and disappointing for a restaurant of your caliber !!

Thought you should get this feedback firsthand from us so that hopefully other expectant guests don't have a similar dining experience.

Their response : Thank you for your candid feedback. My sincere apologies about your experience. I am forwarding your email to Chef Manish Mehrotra as well as our General Manager Neil Mendoza. We will look into this immediately. 

Apologies once again. 

Warm regards 
Mukta Kapoor
A really wonderful experience. Amazing food, service and atmosphere. Would come back anytime!!!

Superb.  If you're looking for a "fine dining" experience but don't want yet more wine country food, consider this.  Also, if you're looking for just deliciousness of any sort, consider this.  I came with in a group of four and we were all alternating between being impressed, delighted, and blissed out on the food.

Instead of focusing on all the good things, let me focus on the weak things, because they were few:

- the yogurt and goat cheese kebab: a bit dry, and while not bad at all, it was not as delicious as just about everything else.
- the kulchas: these are just stuffed naan you can order as accompaniment.  Very good stuffed naan, but, I preferred the dal makhani (here called "black dairy dal", because... fanciness?), which was exquisite and also came with its own little naan.
- the desserts: meh.  I see many others love them, but, if you're stuffed from over-ordering everything else, and you're on the fence for dessert, it's okay, you may skip without missing out too much.

Now, the good things:

- Everything.

Okay more seriously:

- Everything.

Okay okay, just a few of many highlights:

- The baked sea bass with berry pulao is maybe the best or among the best fish dishes I've ever had.  It's a mix of flavors and textures, bit sweet, bit savory, creamy, crispy, flaky, buttery.  I want more, now, please.
- The ghee roast lamb, the sphere chaat--enthusiastically enjoyed by the people who ordered them, and delicious from the tastes I got.  
- The soy keema was really good, basically just a flavorfully spicy chili, but made of soy and quail egg.  
- The winter root vegetables was like a tart or a crown, beautifully constructed surprisingly flavored and delicious.  Really liked it.
- The "black dairy dal" I mentioned above, which may be ordered as accompaniment.  I think this is one of the few things on the menu that is recognizable as typical restaurant Indian food.  It's just dal makhani, but, richly flavored and probably as good as dal makhani gets.  Which is very very good.

Service was very good.  Setting is pleasantly generic upscale.  Price is high.
First time in NY and this was our first meal! Kind, attentive staff with great recommendations!!! Enjoying ourselves very much!!

I used to be a regular here, probably have been here 40+ times since it opened, but now the service has gone to the dogs. The way they treated us on Thursday at dinner was beyond shocking. I had 2 guests, one visiting from abroad and experiencing the restaurant for the first time. Way to make an impression, Indian Accent! 
 
We ordered the 4-course meal, a total of 12 dishes + 3 accompaniments that we were all going to share plus drinks for the table. The menu hasn't changed much in 2 years though a few dishes like the crab claws and ghee roast lamb are still classics (that's where the good news ends). They had overbooked the restaurant and clearly wanted to hurry us out, so they brought the dishes all together in 2 batches instead of the four. Needless to say the food got cold at the table and was not as enjoyable. Then it just got worse. Daniel (who I believe, is the Sommelier and was the host/floor manager for the night) made my party get up midway through the meal before dessert was served (we had ordered it as part of our prix fixe menu) under the pretext of seating us elsewhere. I thought they needed the table for a larger party and would accommodate us elsewhere in the restaurant but they headed us to the bar, which had standing room only. 

One of the other managers thought we had finished our meal and were leaving, so he started escorting us to the door even as one of the waiters was trying to set up our desserts at the bar for us. Is that what you expect at a Michelin-starred or a top restaurant in NYC? At this point, I had had enough and refused to eat dessert standing at the bar. BTW other parties were leaving by now and those waiting at the door were shaking their heads in disbelief at the way we were being treated. We asked for the check (it took us 15 more minutes standing by the hostess to get it), paid and left. 

Daniel was so arrogant that one of my guests openly questioned whether he would have treated us differently if we were of a different color. I apologized to my guests and took them to Landmarc for drinks and dessert to make up for the horrible experience. The hostess was equally shocked and asked me to contact Mark Shay (the GM) as we left. 

Cristiano Azevedo (you are the best) and Mark Shay, it was a great ride while it lasted. Thanks for the good old days but if this is the way your staff is going to treat your customers, you can kiss us all goodbye. 

To Manish Mehrotra (the chef-owner, who I met during his early days here): I have seen a steady decline in service after 2 years, accelerated even further after your Mayfair, London location opened late last year and the reservation hotline for NY was offshored. All I can say is that the current strategy and service may fill tables in the short term but not for long. It is time to listen to your most loyal customers and take action if you want to sustain your early success, though some, like me, may not ever be coming back.

My bf surprised me here last night and I loved it! This dessert definitely caught my eye. The Makhan Malai was out of this world and the best I have ever had. It's was smooth, just the right amount of sweetness and crunch. I will be back :)

Throw out all of your preconceived notions around Indian food. Indian Accent proves the cuisine can reach well beyond take away curries. Chef Mehrotra harnesses bold flavors with finesse and nuance. Spice was deftly handled, nothing was too jarring but you did get a good sense of lingering heat on the finish of most dishes. Surroundings are modern and upscale, again not your stereotypical Indian venture. For a while, Indian Accent has been rumored to be in contention for Michelin star. In my opinion, it's not too far off the mark; the food certainly delivers, although service is not quite there yet. Absolutely worth a try - we plan to return.

Atmosphere
- Modern and upscale, but surprisingly comfortable with plush seating and not too much formality.
- Decent spacing of tables, including for two tops.
- Cool looking bar area at front.

Food
One can select among a 9-course tasting menu or 3-4 course prix fixe. We ordered four courses ($90), which also includes one accompaniment. Have to say, we really enjoyed most everything. Four courses includes a fair amount of food, just short of too much. Desserts were gigantic, and could probably be cut in half. We sampled:
      
- potato sphere chaat, white pea mash: Deeply flavorful, but pea mash really refreshening. Recommend.     
- mathri trio: smoked eggplant bharta; duck khurchan; methi murgh: Nice little bites to start, on smaller side, but good flavor.
    
- phulka chili pork: Delicious deep flavors with wonderful spice. Recommend.
- pathar beef kebab, bone marrow nihari: Enjoyed the kebab as well as the sauce, but found the bone marrow to be far too much/rich. Could use some refinement.

- chicken kofta, punjabi kadhi, onion pakora: Excellent, highly recommend, beautiful flavors and refined presentation. 
- beef tenderloin, bakarkhani, potato and fenugreek cheela: Lacked creativity in flavor and presentation. Not that it tasted bad, just no where near level of other dishes.

- butter chicken kulcha: Addictive, must order! Butter chicken filling is so succulent.
- black dairy dal with lachha naan: Enjoyed the dal very much, naan was nice but perhaps a touch greasy. Recommend.

- makhan malai, saffron milk, rose petal jaggery brittle, almonds: Quite interesting and not too heavy, but large in size.
- kheer, crispy seviyan, coconut and jaggery ice cream, strawberries: Ordered on waiters recommendation, very nice. Highly recommend.   

Beverage
We enjoyed the 2013 St. Innocent Freedom Hill Vineyard Pinot Noir ($105). Though it wasn't the bottle we ordered. Wish I had noticed the offered wine pairings at the very bottom of the food menu, as $58 for four courses is quite reasonable. Would do that on a future visit. Overall the wine list leans heavily toward Rieslings, Gruner Veltliner, etc. that typically pair well with Indian cuisine and bottle prices are on average ~$100-150.

Had a mishap on our bottle order. In spite of the waiter confirming our selection twice (returning once to the table to do so), the wrong bottle was brought out. They have three various versions and vintages of the same vineyard. It didn't register to me until after they opened (my fault), but in the end we were charged for the original bottle. If you have a preference or are into wine, pay attention.

To conclude, the after dinner drinks list contains a number of off-the-run options, pretty cool. The Pedro Ximenez 'Gran Barquero' Montilla-Morilles, Spain NV ($20) was excellent.

Service
- Fine, if unexceptional; overall could use some more polish. Our waiter did have generally good suggestions on what to order, however.
- Wine service needs some tweaking (see above).

Loved this place! Took my fiancé for his 28 birthday since he loves Indian food and we loved the different kinds of foods we were given, the textures, flavors and spices were amazing! Christiano one of the hosts gave us a complimentary dessert. Get the mustard infused tequila for all the tequila lovers!

Fine dining Indian food-- who knew? I love Indian food, it's probably my favorite cuisine. However, fine dining, for my taste, is too expensive for what it is. Though this wasn't the best Indian food I've had (ranks maybe second), it's the best fine dining I've had. Of course, it's very popular-- so popular that you have to make a reservation months in advance. We got the pre-theater course (2 of any dishes you like with an accompaniment, be it two mains, an app and a main, a main and a dessert, etc.). Before our orders, we got cute little hors d'oeuvres of pumpkin-coconut milk soup with little puffs of blue-cheese stuffed naan. It was perfect (but hot). 
- Bengal rice khichdi, crispy lentils, smoked papad
(More lentil soup with some sauces, good but not as good as the khichdi from Vatan, which is more rice-like)
- Mathri trio: smoked eggplant bharta; duck khurchan; methi murgh 
(Three super tiny flatbread cones; one had eggplant curry, one with duck curry, and one with chicken curry. They're not super discernible from each other). 
- Seared scallops, prawn koliwada malvani dried shrimp pulao 
(A scallop dish with delicious fried shrimp and shrimp biryani, though I think the seafood is not as good as the truly Indian dishes). 
- Accompaniment: butter chicken kulcha 
(Delicious tiny naan stuffed with butter chicken).
- Baked sea bass, patrani butter, berry pulao
(A super tender bass with a similar biryani). 
- Ghee roast lamb, roomali roti pancakes
(Cute set up of a tiny pot with goat curry, tiny rotis, and little containers of sauces and chopped cucumbers and daikon-- if you wrap up the goat in the roti with tamarind sauce and the vegetables, it's a perfect combination of sweet and savory. It's my favorite main of the three and reminded me of one of my favorite dishes: peking duck.)
- Accompaniment: black dairy dal with lachha naan 
(Even better than the kulcha, it was a nice flaky naan with a butter chicken-like sauce, without the chicken. It goes well with the ghee lamb). 
- Doda barfi treacle tart vanilla bean ice cream
(Tasted like a very sweet chocolate cake topped with ice cream, though there's no chocolate. It was one of the delicious highlights--I'm a sweet tooth.)
- Kheer, crispy seviyan, coconut and jaggery ice cream, strawberries 
(Rice pudding with fried vermicelli noodles, ice cream and fruit. It was also good, I always appreciate good rice pudding, but it's not as good as the doda.)
To top it all off, they gave us little sweet indian snacks, like peanut brittle and sesame things at the end. 

Yes, this was good Indian food, but better than a hole in the wall place, or a good family restaurant like Saravana Bhavan? Maybe. (Yet, I'm still partial to Vatan). But still not worth the hundreds of dollars it costs. But if you're willing to spend, this is the most worth-it fine dining I've had.

4.5 stars. I had high expectations for Indian Accent. I generally find Indian restaurants in NYC to be unimaginative and average. Indian Accent does a great job breaking the mold. There are several interesting options on the menu. We're vegetarian and we got the 4 course menu. 
Amuse bouche: Pumpkin soup (delicious) and tiny naan with blue cheese (loved the tiny naan presentation but I'm not a fan of blue cheese--be careful when biting into it...it's warm and the cheese squirts out)
Starter: Shakarkandi (chaat style, tasty, I liked the added fried okra and use of sweet potatos). My husband got the potato sphere chaat which was closer to more traditional chaat
Mid-course: Soy keema. Tasty, very filling, unique. I was stuffed at the end of this meal. If I had to eliminate one dish, it would be this one... it was good but too much quantity (I got tired of it towards the end); My husband got the Bengal Rice Khichadi which he liked but it was probably the most boring menu item we ordered. 
Main: Winter root vegetables (we both LOVED this). I thought it was extremely unique, tasty and well presented. Highly recommended especially if you're vegetarian. It was suitable for those with nut allergies. They made an error for my husband and brought this plus a dosa with paneer (an option to substitute mushrooms). The winter root vegetable was so much better than the dosa. 
Dessert: Doda burfi treacle tart... must get! so amazing! if you have a nut allergy (like my husband) get the Makhan Malai without almonds. The Makhan Malai is very light and airy.
Cocktails: I LOVED the trancendental medication. Perfect cocktail. Not too sweet, very tasty, amazing honey granules around the rim. My husband's Mughal Fortification was great if you like Bourbon. 
The negatives (why I docked 0.5 stars): the service was too fast/rushed. We would've liked some time to breathe between courses. The vegetarian menu was the same price as the regular menu. There's no way veggies cost as much as meat... it always feels like you're getting a little ripped off when you pay the same price. Also, menu doesn't seem to change much. It would be nice to go back if they offer some new things every once in a while. They should expand their vegetarian offerings and put it all on a separate menu.

This place takes indian food to the next level! Such great service, a very relaxed and romantic ambiance, and a menu with unique selections that you will not find anywhere else. This completed our experience at NYC! The chef Manish Malhotra has done an incredible job using the indian spices to make fusion dishes that is nothing short of incredible. They serve complimentary mini naan filled with blue cheese with a side of pumpkin coconut chorba. It was so good that we asked for seconds. The bheja fry on khasta rotti was my favorite dish! We finished with the makhan malaai which was like eating air! What an interesting experience. it's texture is hard to describe, it is whipped milk infused with saffron and topped with candied almonds, rose petals and pure gold! It was exquisite!

Incredible, there's not words to describe how amazing is the food at this place. The explosion of flavors in my mouth were unforgettable. We arrived and David was our server, he decided 4 courses for us and he chose the best of the best, he was very nice and explained everything. The other servers were kinda as well. Obsessed with this place, will come back!!!

Went there with 6 people for a work anniversary. The ambience is nice, place is very modern and clean feel to it. 

Drinks: they took some time to get the drinks. But after we tried them we were all amazing how well crafted the drinks where. The flavors stand out and you will remember them. I had the transcendental medication which is gin based!

Food: is on the next level, flavors are well matched up. To be honest you don't need supplemental spice /heat which I have a habit of asking for at restaurants. I didn't use any additional spice. Tastes for each appetizer and mains we ordered were unique and not the same. The table had tried ribs, sweet potatoes with okra app, tuna salmon bhel, goat cheese kebabs, pulled pork phulka and again all where amazed. For mains we had chicken, scallops, poha and wild rice veg medley supplemented with naan and many "little" stuffed Kulchas. All brilliantly prepared with amazing taste profiles.

Only issue: portions are very small! And slightly $$$$.  Portions are small!

That said I will probably go back again with my better half for a special occasion!

Amazing, high-end Indian restaurant. Ate alone at the very nice bar. Had a glass of the Ott "Am Berg" Gruner Veltliner and a main dish: seared scallops, prawn koliwada, malvani dried shrimp pulao. When I said I like it spicy, he said they had a green sauce he would put on the side. Compliments of chef was two tiny naan w blue cheese inside, which were delicious. Also, tiny little soup. Everything was so flavorful, although portion size is small. Not cheap, but I would come again.

There are no words to describe this indian dining experience! The ambience, the staff and the location are great but the food! Impeccable blend of flavors to satisfy any palette! Absolutely impressed! Keep up the great work!
Bad service.  Good food.  I will not be back.   They are not nice to customers generally.  I did not like the overall experience.

There were issues settling in. Made to wait despite reservation and gave 3 of us a small table ( good for 2 people only). Portions are small and taste is average. Ordered Mathri trio, ghee toast lamb and kheer. The dessert is probably the best of all courses. I went with a lot of expectations but honestly speaking, the restaurant is over rated.

Good. Not great 

Pros: beautifully plated modern Indian. Creative. 
Good cocktails. 
Friendly staff. 
Nice interior. 
Excellent dhal
Nice overall experience 
Well run restaurant 

Cons: actual flavors don't always match the impressive plating. If you close your eyes, flavors are pretty ordinary, such as the yam salad. Basically a curry potato salad. 

The ribs, which we were told people come back for were ok, and then we realized they're basically Général Tsos glazed ribs. So a little meh. 

The ghee lamb was salty and a little greasy with very monotone flavors. 

While the staff is friendly, every 3-5 minutes someone came to ask us if we were enjoying our meal. It was too much attention.

This is hands down one of the best food experiences I've had. It is definitely the best Indian food I've yet to experience. 

My husband and I did the 9 courses for our anniversary dinner last weekend. I randomly saw this place in a YouTube video for the London location and upon looking it up, saw there was one in NYC, and made a reservation for the weekend we would be in town. 

The service from the phone to in person was 5 stars. We had Kenneth help us at this location and he was a delight to interact with, he was friendly and made our experience about more than just the meal we were eating. We had a great time talking to him about the dishes and the flavors. 


The food is amazing. I don't want it give it away but I would 100% recommend the chefs tasting. 

The ambiance was nice but in my opinion could be a bit more luxe. This was the only thing 'missing' for me. 

We had an absolutely memorable time! I will make it a point to try the other locations on Delhi and London!

Indian accent is a fun Spin - or accent as it were on Indian food.  We figured that out when we asked for Indian beers and were told they don't have any. I felt under dressed in jeans as it was the fine dining experience as advertised! Their version of Naan is delicious stuffed with mushrooms chicken or bacon,and the Seabass was spectacular. The servers (many) are very professional.  It's a multi course long ordeal so just be prepared to make it a night.

Hi yelp can we  hv option of no star..this restaurant goes for 0 star as of my point of view.why I am saying that cos ther is no taste and flavor in any of the food items, and food quantity was very very less  prices as compare to other good fine dining restaurant is very very high and when u don't get good taste and in the end whn check comes, u feel lik someone robbed you ..menu is v confusing ..we ordered 4 and three course meals and can u believe I m still hungry and i had food at home after coming form there.anyway let's not talk about quantity let's talk about taste ..I feel chef main concentration was making everything crispy..and he used same sauces Nd chuttnies in all the food .as complimentary we got Som sort of drink and blue chees nan ..drink was ok nan taste like medicine then appetizer came which was ok ..thn khichdi which was again spoiler and thn main course where I ordered sarson ka saag and kulcha..I even dnt remember how was the taste..thn desert which was ok so overall one of the worst restaurant I visited so far ..where ntn was tasty ..go for good service nice ambiance.

WOW I had friends recommend #INDIANaccent and true to their word... this HAS TO BE THE BEST UNIQUE INDIAN FOOD RESTAURANT in NYC! Looove the butter chicken accompaniment( I could have had 4 orders of that!) .. but thankfully waited for the $75 prefix3 course .. so delicious ... ask for SMITHA as your waitress SHE IS AMAZING with full service and truly knows how to take care of clients ! Mark the manager totally took care of us and the bartender SHAWN is to die for!

Food: v. Good
Service: over pretentious/ ostentatious 
Ambience: bit noisy.
Overall it's a high end Indian restaurant!
Amazing food and amazing hospitality. We tried almost everything on the menu and it was all delicious

My coworker recommended this place after she had her amazing dinner at Indian Accent. I made a reservation for Saturday dinner. My husband and I usually go to new American or french restaurants for fine dining, so this was a new experience for us. The place radiated very classy and modern vibes. We got seated towards the inner end of the restaurant. We decided to do the three course dinner. The menu was a little difficult for us to understand as there were many Indian terms that did not have English description, but our server was very friendly and patient with us at explaining and answering all of our questions. We got blue cheese naan and coconut pumpkin soup/yogurt (?) as our amuse bouche.
My three choices were sweet pickle rib, ghee roast lamb, and meethe chawal (dessert), and bacon Kulcha for accompaniment. My husband got mathri trio, scallop, makhan malai (dessert), and kulcha stuffed with duck.  My marinated pork rib was delicious but I didn't feel like I was eating Indian food. Kulcha was similar to fried stuffed naan. Scallop dish was my favorite (although it was one of my husband's choices). The lamb dish was also good and reminded a lot of the sloppy jo. All the presentation for the food was excellent, and the portion was also very filling. I think my tastebuds are not quite accustomed to the some of the tastes of the food, but I was happy to have tried something different from our usual restaurant choices.

Absolutly amazing food!! We had the 3 courses meal, and each course was better then the last. We also paired it with the wine tasting and we couldn't be happier with what we got. The service was very attentive and took time to explain what the dishes were like so we didn't have any doubts.  I HIGHLY recommend this place for dates and special occasions!

I went here with my family after my sister's college graduation and we all loved it. Two of us got the four course and the other two got the three course (both do a pretty good job of filling you up with delight). It was definitely a new experience for all of us, trying dishes we have never had before (even though we are Indian). The drinks were also a new taste. I remember the goat and duck being my favorites from all that we were given, but honestly, it's all really good. Will definitely plan on going again when I come back to New York City. I rarely give 5 stars, but this place has earned it!

It's taken me a few trips to NY to finally make it in here, but man I am glad we finally did.  I started with a Barbary Coast which had a ton of flavor with the chili infused aperol (but I'd recommend finishing it before you start into the food!)

The potato chaat was fantastic--great flavors and textures.  For a main, I had the sea bass and smoked bacon Kulcha.  The bass was cooked perfectly and had amazing flavor.  The Kulcha was a bit spicy and absolutely delicious.  

We had to run so couldn't enjoy dessert but we are looking forward to our next visit.

Amy thanks for a wonderful service and best ever indian food I have had in NYC. Anand has to be proud to have such a great indian restaurant being run by you and your team. 

I recommend the lamb and sea bass. Fantastic place!!!!

Food is a little bit more hit or miss than I expected, but the highs are truly incredible. I would skip the potato sphere (sounds a lot better than it is.) The beef you get with the beef kebab and bone marrow mid-course is delicious, although there are 3 or 4 tiny bites of meat; the dish is 90% bone marrow. The chicken kofta was rich and simply delicious. The ghee roast lamb is by far the best thing we had and I would go back there just for that. The cocktails were also delicious, particularly the ones with bourbon :)

The food is very good.  It's inventive, this is not your standard curry house, so don't expect any classic dishes.  There are some fan favorites though: the sweet pickled ribs are well worth it.  The kulchas (stuffed naans) were heavenly, the butter chicken one is a standout. 

The wine list is pretty extensive and you can find cheap bottles.  It's a little difficult to pair indian flavours with wine though, our waiter seemed a little clueless but we landed on a good bottle sub-70.

The bar is expensive.  You'll probably wait there a bit before getting your table but I would just wait it out.

We consider ourselves foodies. Indian Accent (IA) has become our most desired place for creative/inventive Indian cuisine. Today we tasted the season's new brunch menu at IA and the master chef Manish Mehrotra himself flew from Delhi to host this experience. Our taste buds were in cloud nine and so were we and we are not easy to please! Great food, great service and rich with Indian hospitality! A must visit for those who demand only the best! DP

Came here post day-long conference of lip service meets and needed a place to unwind with delicious food. Always look for quality indian in NYC and the issue with Indian food is always portion control - they overserve and you overeat loving every minute when it goes down but hating yourself after with a belly of guilt! 

Indian Accent does a prixe fixed which at first was different but it was the perfect balance and size - we had the mushroom dosa (awesome, they should add a truffle option for $$ extra), traditional Chaat, the kulcha was over buttered but since it was so small it was just fine! paneer was terrific. 

Presentation, service all were excellent. Decor was like a find american restaurant. Highly recommend, good place for Indian people with White friends who want "good Indian food"

We came here for lunch. The amuse-bouche was a great start with a tasty spicy soup served in a small cup and mini pita bread filled with goat cheese. I'm not a fan of goat cheese but I really liked it. For app, I had the famous sweet pickled rib.  OMG this was one of the best ribs I've eaten across all cuisines and would have been happy to have a plate full of them instead of just 2 ribs as an app. For main I had the ghee roast lamb.  It was very good, but not the best I've had, and it was nice to eat with the mini roti pancakes.  It was accompanied by cucumber with a few sauces. I had this with the butter chicken kulcha - excellent.  To finish I had the doda tart. First, I like the name and it was very good and you need the vanilla ice cream to balance the sweetness.  Service is excellent and atmosphere is upscale. Will be back.

Good food and ambience !!
Very delicious appetizers , different from regular Indian food !

The lunch A La Carte and service deserves a 5/5 HOWEVER When I came back for the lunch tasting menu both my mother and I agreed that the A La Carte was far better and that the tasting menu was not worth the money.  Don't get the tasting menu BUT DO eat here.  It would be 5 stars if not for the tasting menu.

We had gone with too much expectations and even agreed to book late evening 9 PM reservation as it was the earliest reservation available. Reached there at exactly 9 PM after day long activities, the person at reception desk told that they would require couple of minutes to prepare our table. We waited patiently with our restless kid for 10 mins and asked again. The same person tells that the previous guests have not left the seat and they can't ask them to leave- which is altogether different from earlier story of preparing table. They let us stand for exactly 30 mins despite reservation and had let in few other people who came after us. I even pointed to vacant tables but were brushed aside, treated coldly and ignored at multiple occasions! They kept telling us couple of mins to wait and never seemed to make any effort to expedite the process.This is ridiculously bad treatment one can expect at such fine dining place inspite of the reservation and double confirmation over phone.

Later raised the same issue with a manager there and she profusely apologised after spoiling our mood. The lady who was taking our order was good and nice to talk with, however our beer order was missed which we never bothered to check again. 

They added extra course charges on our bill which we never ordered and got it corrected.

Overall not a good experience even though food was fabulous and creatively presented.
Service was impeccable from the hostess, to the bartender, and server. The food was AMAZING (I included descriptions with my pictures below).

This is worst restaurant of New York. I would suggest to all Indian visiting New York, Do not waste your time to go their.   I was their in evening 6.30 pm at June 21st and waste my time and money. Very luxuries look and duffer services.

Probably the best high-end Indian restaurant I've ever been to.  I had some expectations when we arrived...it had a nice NYC vibe to the decor and ambiance and was pretty full when we came.

We started with drinks: I had the "Proper Copper" which was Kaffir LIme Leaf vodka, honey and rose blossom water.  While I didn't love my drink, my husband did.  He had a tito's soda to start with.

The drink menu had some clever names to their cocktails, such as bandit queen, mughal fortification and Mumbai's the word. 

We chose the 3 course menu (you could do all four courses if you would like as well), at $75 each.  I thought the price was fair.  There was also a more limited chef's tasting menu. 

Our amuse bouche was a spicy tomato soup and stuffed naan. So good and a good start for what was yet to come. You could choose a lot of different combinations for your tasting menu. 

I chose the mid-courses, mains and desserts. My husband did 2 mid courses and a main. So you can get creative. 

I had teh pulled jackfruit phulka, the baked sea bass and makhan malai, with a saag paneer kulcha accompaniment. My husband did the sweet pickle ribs, pork dumplings and chicken malai tikka with the black dairy dal.

He said his ribs were amazing. They fell off the bone so he was super happy about that.  My jackfruit was like a mix of a taco and flat bread. I ate the jackfruit, which was well marinated with a fork and I loved the mini phulka that was provided. the dumplings  (in a savory broth) were something he wanted to order another round.
My sea bass was a good portion and came with a side of pulao rice with berries. So good! We both did the wine pairings with our dishes and they enhanced the food nicely.

The kulcha was really different and I loved the inventive spin on putting my favorite Indian dish inside the kulcha since I eat it that way most often.

The makhan malai was a standout.  It looks dense but is really airy and the rose flavor was incredible.  A lot of tables were ordering this dish and I could see why. My husband ended the night with a couple of old fashioneds and thought these were some of the best he's had. 

I never felt rushed and had a fantastic experience at Indian Accent.  The food is so creative and filling--you get a decent portion for each course. I'm really glad we came here for dinner.

I came here for lunch and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. As you would expect, this isn't your traditional Indian restaurant but the flavors were still very true to the cuisine. The service and ambiance were also very nice. 

There were three of us and we all went with the two course lunch for $35. The awesome thing about this two course was that you could literally choose any combination of the two items that you wanted. You could have an appetizer and main or two appetizers, or even two mains. I went with the two mains of course. 

I ordered the softshell crab to start with the ghee lamb for entree. My friends ordered the ribs, dumplings, and salmon. We also had the hoisin duck naan. 

Everything was delicious and it was just the right amount of food. I didn't leave hungry nor did I leave uncomfortably full. I would definitely come back for lunch and maybe even dinner next time.

Five stars just for the dessert! Must try the Makhan Malai which will melt in your mouth. 

Nice ambience, bright and cheerful. Inventive dishes on the menu, quite a few vegetarian options. Started off with the complimentary coconut flavored soup which was good and the blue cheese naan which was messy to eat. 

Got the sweet pickle ribs , melt in the mouth tender just the right amount of spice and sweet. The shrimp kolivada dish was just amazing , tasted like the homemade shrimp rava fry, elevated!

Wife got the Bengali kichidi and the fenugreek palak tart which she loved. Great flavor and creative presentation.

Dessert - both the makhan malai and the kheer was fantastic. Great textures in each, well balanced and not too sweet. The kheer dessert had perfectly cooked rice kheer, crispy sevaiyan and juicy berries along with two wonderful ice creams- brilliant combination. The makhan malai was light and airy , with crunchy bits and nuts and a hint of rose, easily the best dessert in a long time! 

Wanted to eat at the Indian Accent in Delhi to try the daulat ki chaat , didn't happen due to time constraints. Came here for a memorable lunch while in New York for the Memorial Day weekend.

Amazing food, amazing experience!

We did the chef's tasting menu for dinner, it was outstanding.
The whole experience lasted a good 4 hours. 

Very decently priced for a 9 course dinner; the presentation of the food was beautiful, modern and elegant; a very nice twist on Indian cuisine.

The langoustine is one of the best things I've ever tasted, the cod was so buttery and flaky, and the dessert was out of this world; each dish is small but packs a nice punch.

The ambience was nice and modern, it could work for a business meeting as well as a date.
The best high quality Indian places in all of NYC! The fried soft shell crab had great texture and was so tasteful! A must try in NYC!

We sat at the bar and ordered a la carte. 

It was great; the cocktails were amazing (I ordered the one with bourbon and saffron / coriander) and the food was wonderful. 

We got the ghee lamb, the spinach kofta, and the butter chicken kulcha. The kulcha was great with the chutneys that came with the lamb, the lamb was spiced perfectly, and the kofta was soft and tender. 

Strongly recommend you spend way too much money at this tasty establishment ;)

I recently went for dinner and did the chef's tasting menu. The food was not only beautifully prepared, but amazingly delicious as well. Indian Accent's progressive take on traditional Indian plates was refreshing. Although there were hints of modern taste and texture, each plate held true to its authentic origin. In addition to the food, the cocktails were also just as good (try the Transcendental Medication)! The experience lasted about 2 hours and was worth every penny.

For a great upscale Indian meal, Indian Accent is perfect. A small restaurant inside, it manages to be upscale without being pretentious. The cocktails are delicious with an Indian flare of flavor. The food is exquisitely tasty with a punch of flavor and a nice balance of different textures and tastes. The service is top notch too and incredibly attentive. It's a great spot for a special occasion, or just for something different.

This is based on my dinner experience. Loved the ambience the food and the service. Everything had a distinct flavor unlike a lot of Indian fusion restaurants. 
It's Indian fine dining at its best. Def a stop next time I am in NYC.

I came here for brunch, and it was nothing short of 'meh'.

The great thing about this place at brunch is that it's relatively empty, and not loud at all. It's definitely for families or friends trying to have a nice New York city brunch where you can actually hear each other. The food also comes out relatively quickly, so there's no waiting around. We were in and out in an hour.

The sad part is that the food is just.so.meh. Everything looks really good but tastes all too similar to the inspiration.

To start, I had the wasabi and yogurt batata puri. It tasted just like the original, with a slight afterburn of the wasabi which was nice, but again, not outstanding. 

For my entree, I had the parsi "salli per eedu". Now you tell me, what kind of New York city brunch entree with egg for $22 has JUST ONE EGG?! I got this entree and was overwhelmed with the "ARE YOU KIDDING ME" feeling. The dish itself was tasty, but again, nothing worth hauling ass to midtown and paying serious $ for.

My friend and I split a wild mushroom kulcha which was the smallest kulcha of all time. It was tasty but super, super, super small.

We split the bill, and the total came out to around $50 each. I just paid $50 for meh food, y'all, and certainly not doing it again. I'd liken this experience to paying for a Lamborghini, but getting a nicely painted Volvo with a Lamborghini hood ornament. I love Volvos, but dressing one up really nicely doesn't make it a Lamborghini. When you pay for Lambo, you want a Lambo.

Faultless service, innovative drinks and delicious inventively plated food come together in this unpretentious Indian restaurant.

Four of us went for dinner on a Friday night and had a lovely evening. We started with cocktails off the menu and were all happy with our choices.

We did the 4 course prix fixe menu. Everything was flavorful and delicious with interesting plating.

I must admit I was a bit skeptical before coming to Indian Accent, as I have not often had successes with Indian cuisine in Midtown. But given it's part of a franchise with a successful location in Delhi, I thought it was worth a shot.

I'm glad I took the risk, as the food was excellent. The soy keema pao was a great way to start the meal, and even caused the meat eaters at my table to regret their selections once they tried my appetizer. The innovative kulchas, including one filled with mushrooms, are also a must-have.

I usually have a drink at the bar and read! Extremely comfortable seats and great cocktails! Fresh ingredients and just very different flavors! I would love to come back just for the cocktails and the nice relaxing bar where you can read and unwind after a long meal! Another pro-tip: The bartenders are pretty friendly!

Surrender yourself to the chef and you won't be disappointed! 
Incredible tasting menu and they are always innovating. You might be disappointed that something you ate last time has been churned on the menu but trust me the replacement is even better. I almost think the midtown location is better than the original in New Delhi, India. Chef Manish and his team goes above and beyond to create an experience for the soul with modern twists to classic Indian dishes and street food. Ending the meal with daulat ki chaat is like taking a bite out of the clouds

This place was absolutely exceptional! And was worth every single penny it was actually a very fun experience in the food was absolutely amazing! If you are a lover of Indian food or even someone that may be on the fence about Indian food this place will definitely win you over I can't even express how positive experience wise! There's definitely nothing else out there quite like it! I highly recommend the stuffed butter chicken naan!!

Went for a team lunch recently. I read the reviews and expected a lot.

1. SMALL portions. (of course fine dining implies small portions, but if you're  hungry when you entered, you're going to be hungry by the time you leave). Watching a  teammate eat two spoons of salmon was painful haha.

Tip: While ordering, ask the waiter for food options that have a lot of quantity :P
For veg: Order the idly and dosa combo 2 course combo.

2. Everything tasted good, but it wasn't SPECTACULAR. I could've had this at most decent Indian restaurants.

3. I had inquired vegan/vegetarian options and was misinformed that they had a separate vegan menu. However, the waiter just pointed at a few recipes and said he could make them vegan by removing half the stuff.  That was disappointing. The waiter missed informing that idlies (which I love) was vegan/vegetarian -  I should've guessed but I didn't want to assume  - which I completely missed and only found out later. I wasn't informed that we can order 2 dishes from main courses instead of an appetizer and a main course. Would've picked other options but I thought I had to order from each.

Advice to the management: Do not tell people you have a separate vegan/vegetarian menu. Having symbols next to dishes might us to  identify these options without having to depend on anyone else.

Indian Haute Cuisine!! It's a shame that this is such a selling point to me, but not many of these types of places exist in the world. Service was definitely accommodating, while knowing there place and when to interrupt.  

The mini bleu cheese kulchas were fucking fantastic. I could have ate a barrel of those. Fluffy bread, creamy bleu cheese, and the char on the edges from the tandoor put an exclamation point on it all! A great start to the meal for damn sure. 

The Kashmiri morels were a delicious mushroom, spiced with a great zest that rings long after the last bite. The texture of the crispy Parmesan papad is Quite helpful as the mushroom is obviously spongy. The walnut powder didn't make much of a difference (or at least from what I could tell) 

The duck khurchan were not as good as I thought they were gonna be. The duck is there, and they top it with foie gras, but there's nothing that explodes with orgasmic flavor. They aren't terrible, but they were certainly a let down with my high expectations. 

The cod amritsari was a dish that took cod to new heights I never dreamed. The entire filet was jam packed moist with a delicious buttery feel and flavor. Never did it fade or disappear while eating. The boondi on top gave a much welcomed texture that gave my teeth some fun little toys to crunch and destroy. The spices they pepper on top zip in and out on the forefront, leaving a wonderful aftertaste. 

The lobster with coconut curry was good, but I wish the lobster had a more pronounced fish flavor. Otherwise, it was cooked just right. The coconut curry didn't explode in my mouth at first, but it did have me coming back for more. By the end, I was scraping the bowl clean with my spoon. Rich, creamy, with a Creeper spice that leaves a great zest on the tongue 

The tiger prawns are simple, yet the sauce is what really carries them. Nutty, spicy, and creamy in all the right ways. 

The sweet pickle ribs were a delight that I didn't even expect. The chef figured if I wanted to try the best off the menu, that he would throw one on there. The charred candy bits were the highlight of that dish. If you don't do the tasting menu, I highly recommend you order this.  

The kulchas kinda remind me of pizza. Especially with the masala filling. The tandoor charred edges of course made it better. But black dal was great, but the mustard caper raita was the show stopper! It came out tasting like a horseradish cream, which is not something raita normally tastes like. I spooned globs of that stuff on my kulchas and enjoyed every minute of it.  

The chicken malai was not what I expected, but it's still a good dish. It definitely feels like east meets West in this dish. I'm surprised the sugar snap peas didn't bother me. The texture of the meat reminded me of meatballs. They packed it was a great spice though. It was quite creamy with the sauce they added on top and all around the plate.  

The digestive pomegranate sorbet sat in some mango lassi tasting sauce that was quite bright and fruity. It was a great way to prepare my taste buds for some dessert.  

The mahkan? malai was quite a treat! The saffron milk looked like ice cream, scooped like mousse, yet dissolved quickly into air in my mouth. It almost felt like I was breathing it in! All the toppings sit nice on the mouth once the mousse disappeared with the almonds and rose petals. The gold flakes seemed unnecessary, but they added to the jewelry like presentation of the meal. 

This place has quite the charm to me. Its conservative enough to bring the family, but it offers items I would never find elsewhere in america. I was quite happy with what they served here. Not everything was a show stopper, but its worth a visit (if you have plenty of time in New York. If you only have a few days, then wait till next time.)
Great food and ambiance! Not your typical Indian restaurant in any manner but definitely lived up to all the hype!

Excellent choice for a modern take on Indian cuisine in a sumptuous modern restaurant.

- beautiful, tasteful modern decor
- excellent service, many wait staff so you're always taken care of. 
- food was very good, I would say the portions are definitely on the smaller side 

Definitely recommend

If you're feeling a light meal, skip the prix fixe/ tasting menu and grab a seat at the bar, where you can get most of the popular bites and get drinks.

The proper copper is an excellent refreshing drink, while the wine selection leaves a bit to be desired. 

The sweet potato shakarkandi is a great way to start your meal (after the pumpkin soup they brought us on the house that is). The black dairy dal was a creamy version of the Indian staple but was very good with a lachha naan. We also got the lamb pancakes which was a good light dish but required a bit more bread. All in, the meal was light and a good way to have Indian food without it being too heavy. The portions are on the small size so keep that in mind while deciding your order :)
This place has some of the best non-traditional Indian food I've had. Especially the sea bass and doda barfi.

It's OK not great. 
Service might have been the worst part of the experience. My husband and I usually set next to each other at restaurants. We sat at a table w lots of space but they didn't allow any seat changes. Wasn't elegant as I expected. The server made a passive aggressive comment about us putting the water glass on the table and how it might ruin their "beautiful new tables". the waiter was so unhelpful when we were asking about the menu. After we decided what we wanted he THEN tell us that if one person wanted the chef menu everyone should get it. Didn't bother saying that 20 min ago and save everyone's time. 
Food: was not consistently good some were meh somewhere enjoyable. We didn't have dishes that were "oh my god I have to come back" kinda dishes. The cod was good. But strangely it was served with rice that was good but the same rice was served with 2 more dishes. Same flavor and everything. 
Cocktails were EXCELLENT. Wine menus is also great with many exotic options. 
Unfortunately we didn't enjoy the experience. I don't think I would recommend it.

Having tried other top Indian restaurants in NYC, I came to Indian Accent with high hopes and mostly positive reviews but I was very disappointed. 

We were a very large group so we ordered almost everything on the menu (the portions are quite small). Except for a couple of items, most of them were not very enjoyable. 

I felt like they tried too hard to be creative, which is great except when your creations lack excitement or flavour.
Great Food. Very Well Made. The Soft Shell Crab, Butter Chicken Kulcha, and Ghee Roast Lamb are Amazing!
The food here is amazing. So many interesting flavors and the presentation is beautiful. Would love to come back!

I do not wish to repeat my review of Indian Accent in the Trip Advisor on the Yelp site. But I would urge you to visit Trip Advisor and see my full review headlined ALL HYPE, NO SUBSTANCE. THIS IS NEW YORK AND WE ARE NOT CULINARY MORONS. 

Here is the bottom line. The restaurant service staff is polite and obliging but totally lack fine dining service etiquette. The restaurant of this caliber should have a trained Sommelier. The service etiquette is crude and does not match the pricing. 

My main, roast lamb was served on a very narrow width rectangular wooden tray. The main was served with julienned daikon and cucumber surrounded by 4 sauces including Tamarind sauce. What were these sauces doing was not explained to me. The menu stated that my main would be served with Roomali Roti. Totally false. There was no Roomali Roti. The 2" or 2.5" Tortillas were housed in a cane box. They were dry, hard and chewy. If the Chef wants to experiment let him do so but not destroy the soul of the proclaimed offering. 

The roast lamb was loaded with ghee or oil and the taste of the lamb was sacrificed at the altar of the floating oil. I did not eat the main and neither the maitre'd came by to enquire the reason I abstained from consuming it. I was with some guests and did not want to subject them to my complaint. 

The restaurant offers only two varieties of Vodka I.e Ketel and Tito's. Better and high end brands like Belvedere and Grey Goose are not on the menu. I believe when a restaurant offers only limited and not too popular brands and charges top prices does so to improve margins at the cost of customer care. Perhaps lucrative promotional monies are given to keep other brands out.

This restaurant is all about gouging customers and not paying attention to service etiquette, quality of food and customer concerns. Pretty looking and innovative presentations only do not serve business interests longer term. 

All hype and no substance. New York has sophisticated diners and not culinary morons.

Nope. Not impressed with this place at all. It's expensive and not worth the hefty price tag for the quality and taste. The ambiance is also lacking for a place that should be classier. The original Delhi location has amazing food in a gorgeous space, but I guess restaurants can get away with a lot less in Manhattan based solely on reputation or perceived quality.

This was my 2nd time visiting Indian accent. We asked for a table for 6 but requested addition of 2 friends who wanted to dine with us last time. The staff were extremely accommodating with all of our requests. Everyone at the table ordered from the 3-4 course menu. The portions were generous and absolutely delightful. The seabass and the paper dosa were fantastic. The best I've ever had. This is one restaurant in NYC that we highly recommend. Absolutely worth it.

I had such a huge expectations before visiting Indian Accent, and it all crushed as soon as the first dishes came out.
Feels like yet another american restaurant, the Indian flavours were not there. Food was really disappointing, even returned one main course since it felt like I am eating just cooked spinach. Prices are extreamly high and definatrly dont worth it.
And to finish the experience I was served a cold latte (cold, not just not hot enough, cold, is if it was waiting for 30 minutes before I had it).
The service is amazing but the food is really bad. We ordered 9 items and the only thing that we ate was the naan. Even the naam was below average. Would not recommend this place!

We went for the Sunday brunch and had the two-person sharing "feast". It was definitely a feast - so much food we were ready to burst by the end.
