Everything was excellent and also quite varied albeit with a focus on eggs and carbs (natural for brunch). The proper copper drink was one of the best I've had - superbly tart, with a really strong kaffir like flavor. The standout dishes to me were the batata puri, the salli boti, the beef dabba gosht, the saag paneer kulcha, and both desserts - the makhan malai deserves a special mention, but the deconstructed sevaiyon ki kheer was also superb. Overall my only critique would be that it was a bit heavy - could have done with some more "fresh" or "bright" tastes, perhaps through some palate cleansers (am imagining a tamarind granita with rock salt!). Overall superb. Will be back.

Not a big fan of indian food but this  wonderful Indian restaurant met my expectations! I loved every bite I've had. Every dish was beautifully presented, the portions were small but flavorful and filling. 

First we started with amuse. 
Pumpkin soup. It was delicious! And small bites of naan stuffed with blue cheese! And that was excellent as well.

Ghee roast lamb, roomali roti. Was very tasty! I usually don't like lamb due to the strong flavor it has, but this one was excellent! Wouldn't think it's lamb if I didn't know. Spinach stuffed naan was great, mango dessert was good as well and few more dishes that I don't remember... overall everything tasted delicious! 

Excellent service! every dish was explained to us and the servers were attentive!

Beautiful presentation, great taste and high class service. 
The food is fantastic. The staff is very knowledgeable. 
You have a nice big menu to choose your course from. 
And all the dishes are made to order but they don't keep you waiting. So plus point there.
Of course it's expensive give the class. 

Amazing place to take your date to or to make your date 


The only thing missing is the ambiance. For such upscale place, they can do a little better. Private dining/ better lighting etc ..

In NYC for just a couple of days.  Stumbled across this restaurant while searching for Indian food, which we love.   Can't find enough accolades to express our delight at every dish.   What they do to coconut!   The saffron infused dish was a delight.  Every bite was different from all other Indian food, and spectacular.  When we ordered two desserts, but not the owner's favorite, he had it made for us anyway.   It was outrageous.  We were pretty lucky we had long walks to and from our hotel as we were more than full.  And happy.  We will be back, every time we come to NYC.

Overpriced food with very small portions! I was still hungry after spending over $150 on a three course dinner! The food was mediocre at best! Will never go back! The waiter kept coming to our face every few minutes even after telling him several times that we were not ready. Then the manager comes to intimidate us to hurry up and place the order. We were waiting for a friend to arrive and didn't want to order ahead of him. He was only 15 minutes late! Ridiculous!

Love coming here. The food is incredible and constantly finds a way to alter my perception of Indian food, always in the best way. My favorite part is always the starter that they give you. The soup and blue cheese nan is delicious. The wine is amazing, I'm currently enjoying an amazing Gruner that is refreshing and delicious. The staff is always what truly makes the experience for me though. The hostesses are friendly and warm, and I always feel like they are genuinely happy to see me. The one in the glasses (Alyssa I think?) is always super cute and bubbly. My last server Kevin showed my guest and I a great time, and was very attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. I've never had a bad experience here. The quality of everything is what keeps me coming back! Plus they have such a great lunch deal that is incredibly hard to pass up for a 5 Star restaurant. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone.

This is a wonderful Indian restaurant, transcending the usual North Indian staples for a variety of exotic and delicious contemporary takes on the ancient cuisine.  What's not to love (well, the prices are hard to love.  Ha!).

We visited this restaurant today to celebrate my friend's birthday. we booked in advance for two course brunch buffet, cost for which was $35 each. We made it very clear that we want to go for brunch buffet. When dishes came they were super small in portions and we had waiting time for reordering for our dishes. 
                                                   When we were ready to pay for our buffet, amount was switched to $55 each without giving us any clear explanation. We made it very clear in the beginning that we would like to go for brunch buffet. When asked, server gave us vague explanations such as that dal etc.would be at extra cost, so long story short it was a rip off and they charge you according to their convenience. Brunch buffet did not include bread or rice. How can they think of buffet without bread or rice. We all were really disappointed. I would not recommend this to anyone.

I've only ever had dive-esque indian food, and was hesitant to try an upscale indian experience but I am the most thankful I did. This is one of my favorite meals I have ever had. I had so many things I can't even remember the name of but get the dang pork dumplings and the corn.

Very tasteful and freshly prepared with delicious combinations. One item was not that delicious - the sweet potato appetizer. My lamb dinner was elegantly presented and spiced perfectly. Dessert was a light and delicious rice pudding with crispy kataiffi and coconut ice cream on top. Would recommend highly

Innovative take on Indian cuisine. Vegetarian friendly restaurant with amazing choices for each course. Given it was our first time here - tried out the full tasting menu. Loved every bit of it including the delicious desserts. It was a 3 hour dinner in a beautiful setting being served by courteous hosts. Will be returning for more......
Excellent blend of east and west but I found it to be pricey . The food was plated well as is evident by the photographs!

Just freaking go there!! This place deserves a Michelin star ASAP.

We were really, really looking forward to visiting this place, and read up everything we can find about them. Needless to say, we weren't disappointed. It's difficult to please a seasoned Indian palate with Indian food, and even more difficult to wow them. But Indian Accent did it. People see Indian food as daunting because of its complexities, but Chef Mehrotra has actually managed take out a few ingredients and still retain the taste of each dish. If you're mindful while eating, you can distinguish the flavor of each and every dominant ingredient in the dish.

We had many things there, but here are the highlights:

Pumpkin shorba: served as warm shooters, it was the very first dish. We came in after a long walk in a particularly chilly evening, and LOVED them. Our delight was so visible that the lovely server brought us seconds, then even asked for thirds :p

Sweet-potato chaat: simple yet delicious: sweet potato, chaat masala, fried okra.

Soy keema quail egg with kaffir lime pao: if soy wasn't written in the menu, you'd think this is actual keema.

Ghee roast lamb: served peking duck style, with tiny parathas to wrap the meat with. The meat is cooked tender and exquisitely, with the ghee, black pepper and garam masala flavors in perfect harmony. Served with three chutneys: we especially loved the green chilly... very very spicy!!

Doda barfi treacle tart: served warm, with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. The deep caramelized flavors of doda barfi works so well with the mellow vanilla.

Makkhan malai: Light, fluffy with rose petal chikki for crunch. Probably their signature dish, and is absolutely delicious. All the basic Indian dessert flavors- malai, cardamom, saffron- in perfect balance.

In conclusion, there are many Indian places in NYC that claim to serve 'inventive' or 'modern' food, but this place is the real thing. It's expensive, but totally worth it in my opinion.

I visited Indian Accent for dinner, and I loved it!  The atmosphere is sleek and cool, with dim but not too dim lighting and minimalist decor.  I opted for the four course fixed price dinner.  After a complimentary appetizer, the individual courses included a cute appetizer consisting of several cone shaped shells with assorted fillings, followed by steamed pork dumplings, a main course of sea bass, concluding with a nut tart topped with a scoop of ice cream.  Everything was delicious, light with an accent of Indian spices.  Before getting the check we were brought a small plate of sweets to top off the meal.  One piece of advice - If you want a glass of wine, order it at the table.  If you order at the bar the pour will be measured with a five ounce cup.... for a cool $20.  At the table they just pour.

I came for buttered chicken but I didn't see it available on the lunch menu. There was an option to get first and second course for  a bundled deal. I chose the amazing signature ribs for my first and for the main, scallops. The ribs would not have been enough on their own, they are a starter. The scallops would have provided a light meal. The only naan they offer has blue cheese which I couldn't have and they gave me a cute and flavorful alternative. The bartender did a great job making iced tea on demand-it is made fresh to order but be sure to check out the cool hot tea menu. Nice decor. Excellent service. Soft jazz music could have been turned up just one notch. I'll be back tomorrow for dessert and drinks. Definitely would come back for a meal on a future NYC visit.

Ambience, drinks, and food were all amazing!! They deliver a modern play on The traditional Indian dishes everyone loves, with an innovative twist and innovative plating. Their cocktails are the cherry on top. I recommend trying the "mustard" one. It has that spice kick but compliments your food so nicely!

Where to start? Even if the place weren't lovely - and not deafening, hallelujah!! - the service impeccable and staff completely accommodating yet discrete, the insanely delicious food would still make this a five star. We stayed a ala crate but all seven dishes left us speechless from their excellence. Top notch cocktails and wines by the glass. Not cheap, but worth every penny. I can't remember the last restaurant experience that could top this. My new favorite restaurant in Manhattan.

Wow amazing food and outstanding service, can wait to try more from the menu soon. Best Indian food I ever had, the lamp was amazing. You can select 3 for $75 or 5 for $90 the items, i am not a desert person and went with the 3 main courses.

Wow this place was amazing. So fresh and interesting. You will need the waiter to help u through the menu and all of the staff is great and knowledgeable. Very expensive but worth the money. Every dish was better then the next.  Don't ask me names of dishes but u will enjoy. Such a relax atmosphere and very comfortable seats for a change.  If you want something different this is the place. !

"Oh my god" - these are the words you'd keep repeating while enjoying your amazingly cooked and presented meal at Indian Accent. We had made reservations for a Sunday lunch for noon, and I'd highly recommend making reservations if you plan to come here around 1/1:30 pm as this place did fill up very quickly within 45 mins. and the restaurant was packed by 12:45 pm.

For drinks, I ordered their non-alcoholic beverage "Upsy Desi" and would highly recommend it if you love lime.

We went with the shared brunch feast option, which is priced at $55 per person and would highly recommend this option, because it gives you the opportunity to try some of their best dishes in a single meal. We were 4 of us, so we could pick any 4 items from their menu with an option to repeat one. In terms of servings, you get 2 portions of each dish which you split 4-ways. For the first course, "potato sphere chaat, white pea mash" was a winner. First course gives you 3 options to pick from.

For the 2nd course "parsi "salli per eedu," fried egg, crispy potatoes, chutneys" and "beef chili dabba gosht, baked egg, chappati" are to die for. Definitely order the mushroom, and bacon kulcha.

No options to choose from in the 3rd course, but the 2 options listed on their menu are absolutely delicious i.e. makhan malai, and kesar mangoes.

Service is absolutely spot on and food arrives within 20 mins of placing the order. Is it expensive? - Yes it is... is it worth it? - It absolutely is!

Loved it. Great food, service and ambience!

We tried the following for dinner:

Drinks: Mughal fortification (amazing) and garden reviver with vodka

Appetizers: beet tikki and soy keema

Entrees: Tawa paneer, chicken malai tikka

Accompaniments: Black dal, pulao

Bread: saag paneer kulcha and 2 lacha naans

Loved it all but particularly the chicken and dal. I've never had such tender chicken.

The portions are just the right size (appetizers are really small though) but we were quite full from the above and couldn't indulge in dessert.

Highly recommend going if you haven't already. I'd definitely go back.

My first dinner here was so good, I went back 3 days later! The food was not just delicious but creative, beautiful and participatory (depending on what you order, you will be picking, designing, and/or rolling).  My husband and I sat in a booth in the back room on our first visit and it was very private, quiet and luxe while our second dinner was in the front which is more active, (noisier and friendlier with some conversations taking place across tables which are much closer together).  Different experiences but both great.  The service was impeccable; the servers are extremely well trained and take great care.  Indian Accent is a great experience and I look forward to my next dinner there.

I give 5 stars for excellent food and service! From the moment you walk in until you leave you are treated so well!  Of course we are there to eat but I personally want to be treated well, it's why I spend the money.  We both enjoyed the chefs tasting menu of which every course was perfect.  This restaurant, and its above average price point also attracts a more refined clientele, everyone was well dressed, no one on their cell phones, no one taking pictures of their food....everyone just talking, eating and enjoying their night out.

We went for their prix fixe Thanksgiving dinner this year. 
What a disappointment and overly expensive:
$240 for two, not including the tip.

The appetizers were delicious; especially flavorful were the roast turkey pinwheels.

But the main courses were all strongly redolent of the same curried and cumin spices. And frankly although the ingredients were different everything tasted the same. 

Cumin maple brussels sprouts, tandoori cauliflower, spicy almond kadhai potato and the pumpkin and cranberry kulcha was again indecipherable in taste from one another. 

Also, the deserts were sparse; brought to the table a runny pink rice pudding (terrible) with a fancy name 'saffron pear petha, rice kheer' 
and a tiny piece of treacle tart with vanilla bean ice cream (okay).

Inedible assortment of pecan candy.

Exceeded my expectations!

We started with the complimentary mini pumpkin soup and blue cheese naan. They were so good we asked for seconds! Both were perfect.

My appetizer was the potato chaat. It was meh. Served cold covered in sauce - definitely not something I'd order again. My boyfriend got the crab and really liked it. 

For the second course, I ordered the ribs. They were the perfect balance of sweet and spicy-- and I hate spice so me enjoying them says a lot. The meat melted in my mouth. Need now.

For my entree, I got the bass. It was served next to a big bed of rice. I was shocked by how big the portion was (at least compared to their other portions). Not that it was huge, but it was a hefty filling dish. I loved it and would definitely get it again. My boyfriend got the lamb taco thingy and really enjoyed it. It was a bit too spicy for me but I really like how it is DIY. 

We also ordered garlic naan, which was divine. 


For only $15 more you can get another dish- including the entree sized dishes. That's a pretty good option, do it guys!
Amazing Indian food - innovative without losing track of its roots. Expensive.

Died and went to heaven.  Then came back when the check was delivered!!   But food this insanely delicious is often times blisteringly expensive.  The tandoori lamb chops?   Unreal.  The dumplings I would have passed on.  The crab claws?  Forget about it.  I do thing the lamb roti (for an extra $10) maybe was not as wonderful as the others (and maybe because of the surcharge).   But still...overall the most sublime Indian cuisine anywhere, ever.   Oh yeah...the cocktail "Transcendental Medication"?   Get one of those.

The experience was excellent. I would give it a 4.5 if I could but a gracious round up brings us to a 5 star establishment. Unlike other more common fine dining cuisine, this was my first experience in fine dining Indian food - and it was above expectations. 

Ambiance: The décor is simple and clean - inviting - and not too pretentious. The size and flow of the restaurant are appropriate and the over feel of the establishment is one of understated class. - 5 stars

Service: The service was good. Nothing spectacular.  - 4 stars

Food: my girlfriend and I each did a 3 course (all separate courses) dining experience. We started off with the Asparagus, the pork dumplings and the ribs. The asparagus was very good, the coconut chutney was nice. the pork dumplings had an amazing green chilly broth that really made the dish - this is a must get for those that enjoy subtle spices and flavors. the ribs were good but nothing special - I would skip these. For the main courses we got the lamb and the sea bass. The lamb was great, but the star of that dish was the four chutneys that your presented with. Its a great way to explore different flavors and was worth the $10 up charge. The sea bas was also very good - perfectly cooked. My only complaint is I prefer the skin on fish to be crispy, and they present the fish with soggy skin which may throw some off. for accompaniments we had the pulao and the smoked bacon kulcha - both good but neither special in any way. Lastly - the desert. This was actually the star of the night. We got the  makhan malai. If you have been dining out for a while, its rare you come across something completely new. I have never seen or eaten anything like this before. the best I can describe it is some sort of heavily whipped (very airy) milk mouse cloud with almonds and other toppings sprinkled on it. It was so light and delicious. This is what took the food to a - 5 stars.

Platting: well structured plate design. Its no Michelin star  presentation, but its clean and fits the ambiance and cuisine nicely. See attached pictures to develop your own conclusion - 4 stars. 

All in all, this was an excellent night. I'd recommend to anyone looking to explore the amazing world of Indian cuisine. With a cheaper bottle of wine, two cocktails and 6 courses the bill after tax and tip comes in at $350 for two people.

Overall, a satisfactory place with unique dishes, solid four stars. We did the tasting menu and one or two dishes tasted like something was added as a flavor enhancement and if not, a very generous dose of sodium. The service could be better given the place, we had to wait about ten minutes to get seated even though the restaurant was still fairly empty and we had reservations ahead of time. The waitstaff also forgot a dish we asked to take home since we were getting full (bummed I forgot until I got home!).
Pathetic service, long wait times despite reservations, below average food characterize this overhyped place. Never again!
Thoroughly enjoyed the food, atmosphere and service. An added pleasure is seeing the rooms filled with Indian guests...about 3/4 of so of all other diners. But get ready too spend a small fortune.

On our last night on a recent New York trip, my wife and I chose to dine at Indian Accent which had been reaping some very positive reviews.  
We were not disappointed, Though we were without reservations upon entering the establishment, the management resolved our dilemma rather quickly and we were led to our table.  We enjoyed the service of an exceptionally fine waiter, Timba, who explained all of our questions and offered personal opinions about the quite enticing menu dishes when asked (which were more than a few times).  
We found the wine admirably menu matched and found the food divine.  Everything we ate was cooked in a subtly and flavorsome way we have not yet found in an another Indian restaurant.  While honoring traditional Indian cuisine, the chef here flavors it with inspiration.

As highly rated as this place is, it is way underrated as far as I'm concerned. After living in the city for 16 years and hitting just about every restaurant that made someone's list, I had one of the best meals I've ever had at Indian Accent. I did the 10-course testing menu and was wowed by all but 1 of them, including the first couple "unofficial" courses. I'm shocked that anyone can even get reservations here, but I plan to take advantage of this "glitch" in the matrix for as long as possible.

It takes quite the pull to get me into an Indian restaurant, especially on vacation. However, having had many friends recommend Indian Accent, and catering to bae's excitement to dine here, I booked us a reservation (yes, they take reservations... #winning) for a party of four.
Arriving minutes before our reservation time, we were escorted to the bar as they set our table. I enjoyed just a couple sips of my Proper Copper before we were swiftly seated at our table.
Aspiring to hit Michelin status, our menu was an all-or-none chef's tasting menu. While one member of the group strongly wanted the a la carte menu, we managed to convince him and worked through the chef's tasting menu.
What I loved about the menu here was that they had vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, accommodating both dietary styles. Our server, realizing our confusion, excitement, and desire to try everything, accommodated our curiosity by adding in a little here and there to ensure we tasted a full palate of culinary intricacies.
My favorites from the tasting menu were without a doubt the potato sphere chaat, the baked cod, and a pork dish I can't quite recall the name of.
I would certainly enjoy more Indian restaurants if they were like this! Can certainly see Indian Accent inching towards a star in the future!!
This was one of the best meals I've had. Everything was very exquisite and beautifully executed. I cannot wait to go back. Thank you for a wonderful experience on a special day.

The food here was very unique with amazing fusion blends. My husband and I both did 3 courses which is the perfect amount for tasting. This place is an experience for sure anywhere from the staff to the compliments of the chef to the amazing service. Only complaint is that it lacks decor for such a classy restaurant the decoration inside is pretty dull. I had the upsy desi mocktail it was so good. The pumpkin soup from the chef was another favorite, the bhel and the tandoori lamb chops were also delicious,it's a great experience but not a repeat for me

Best. Meal. Ever.  It's an Indian tasting menu of flavors and spices that are heavenly. 

I started with pumpkin coconut shorba that was so delicious, that I wanted to jump in.  I made such a fuss over it that the GM brought me the recipe (I may name a child after him).  I then had crab claws with flavors I've never had before. And went on to short ribs that were sweet and sour. The meat fell off the bone. The next course was a fried ball of spinach and cheese in a masala sauce. OMG. Each course is better than the last. For dessert, I chose the Maklan Malai based on the other reviews on Yelp. It did not disappoint. It was light and sweet with amazing flavor. 

My new goal in life is to fund them so they can spread beyond NY, India, and London. 

Seriously. Best. Meal. Ever.

Indian Accent offers multi course tasting menus that create the perfect opportunity to explore the excellent tastes coming out of their kitchen. If you want to eat a bit less, reserve a seat at the bar where you can order ala carte.Excellent service. All our courses were delicious-tiger prawns, scallops, lamb and the breads with choice of filling. They turn up their noses at mango chutney and traditional Indian beers in favor of sophisticated sauces, micro brews and an extensive wine list - as a mango chutney lover that was a small disappointment that paled in the context of a great meal overall.

We loved the drinks proper copper drink was really nice twist to maska mules. Also we had Mogal....and  spice scotch drinks were gear. We loved Shawn at the bar. He was explaining all drinks and appetizers to pair with our drinks. We had beets, sweet potato, and Asaragas dosa were great. We enjoyed all.

Amazing. I had really high hopes for this place and it lived up to the hype. 

We went with a group of four and we all did the chef's tasting menu. Among our favorites: the puchkas, the morels (this blew me away), the cod, the shrimp, and the kulchas with butter chicken. That is, essentially, the majority of the menu -- it was all just so good.

If I have any minor complaints, it's that I thought the desserts were just very good (not as incredible  as the rest of the menu), and the total amount of food was basically just right. The latter really isn't a complaint so much as it is a warning that if you want to walk out dying of fullness, this probably isn't the right tasting menu place for you. 

All in all, an amazing experience that I'd love to do again at some point.

I stopped in here expecting the typical Indian fare-- chicken dishes in sauce with rice-- which I love!
However, this is a high concept take on Indian cuisine, which is...AWESOME!! The most unique offerings, the most interesting and vibrant flavors! I can honestly say this is one of the best meals I've ever had. And we all know that's saying a lot!! Go here!!! IMMEDIATELY!!

I did chef's tasting menu. The experience is more than just food but culture...I didn't hear any Indian accent from the waiters, but I definitely tasted Indian accent when "talking" with the chef. 

Food is fantastic. So did the ambience and service. Definitely a five star.

I took my bf here for his birthday recently. Given he and I love Indian food, I looked everywhere for a very good Indian restaurant to take him this year. Its described uniqueness, positive write ups and reviews made me especially curious of this place. It's expensive and more upscale compared to most common Indian restaurants, so it's perfect for those special occasions. Be prepared for Indian cuisine with a tasty contemporary spin.

I appreciated the unique approach to their dishes. For dinner, they offer a few different choices; 3 course with accompaniment, 4 course with accompaniment, or chef's tasting. We opted for the 4 course because we wanted to pick and choose off the menu. You can choose any selection off the menu, and it can be any mix of any items. We shared all our dishes, which included in order --

Amuse bouche for each of us - Pumpkin soup and kulcha with cheese

Appetizers - Sweet potato shakarkandi and potato sphere chaat

Mid courses - Phulka with chili pork and sweet pickle ribs

Mains - Seared scallops, Ghee roast lamb, Spinach kofta, and Chicken malai tikka

Accompaniments - Kulcha with wild mushroom and kulcha with butter chicken

Interestingly, we liked our starter dishes more than our mains. We loved the sweet pickle ribs and the appetizers were pretty great. The phulka is like an Indian taco, delicious but not so easy to share as it's just one portion. I would honestly skip the scallops and the chicken malai next time. They were tasty, but I wasn't super fond of them. The ghee roast lamb is a must. The kulcha was a nice accompaniment. It's like a filled pita pocket. The only annoyance was that our kulcha got cold by the time our second course of mains arrived. We were hoping to enjoy the kulcha with our mains, but we waited too long. 

As for service, our last main dishes were taking some time to arrive. I noticed the service started to slow down as the restaurant filled up. When we arrived, service was definitely more on point. The restaurant was entirely filled up after an hour of arrival. We had different servers come by our table. The only weird thing I noticed is we didn't get a wet towel for the ribs though the table next to us did. As for ambience, the restaurant space is very nice. The seating arrangement was fine. We got a corner table at the very front, and it seemed like the most private seating area. The noise level can get loud depending where you sit. I noticed a line at the door for a table, so I strongly recommend a reservation before coming here.

For a birthday occasion, Indian Accent was a nice choice. We both very much enjoyed the food. It's quite different from your typical Indian restaurant. If you're okay spending a bit more, consider Indian Accent for some unique Indian fine dining.

Shooooooot. What else can I say that no one else has said? I mean, holy freaking wow (and I'm a pastor, so when I say holy, I mean it--like there was the holy spirit gathering right there with her Indian accent and she made sure we were all as happy as happy can be.)

Start to finish. Finish to start--I can go on and on and on. I've been to a couple Michelin star restaurants and I am not quite sure why Indian Accent didn't earn a star. But anyway, one of the best experiences of my eating life. 

It's been 3 weeks and we are still talking about the amuse bouche. Everything else was just as good. And, when I say just as good, I mean I'm dreaming of those scallops and the bread and the fish and, and, and. 

If you are a cocktail-o-phile, this place is like woah. Thank God for immigration. 

Not only was the food just absolutely everything you needed and wanted it to be, the service was stunning. Each person who took care of us acted like we were high rollers. We're not. But, we do tip well--not that they knew that. Anyway, the som suggested a perfect wine. Each staff member knew every detail of everything and was there exactly when we needed. We didn't want for a thing. And, each person added a personal touch that made our evening just that much more magical. Presenting amazing food is one thing, but cultivating a space and people who make you feel both like you're in a castle and in your own livingroom--that's impressive. Out of the million places in NYC, I'll be back to IA. 


My only regret: not getting dessert. I couldn't have eaten another damn thing, but I still wish I'd have tried.

Dining at Indian Accent is a deliciously inspired and elegant fine dining experience. My husband and I chose the vegetarian options on the Chef's Tasting Menu and we were truly impressed with each offering, from the amuse-bouches to the sweets. The chefs, Manish Mehrotra and Chetan Shetty, creatively meld familiar Indian ingredients and spices with some decidedly non-traditional elements, such as in a delectable dish called Kashmiri Morels, which features walnut powder and a parmesan papad. Morels and parmesan on an Indian menu? Well, the synthesis of flavors works and kept us intrigued with each new offering. Every dish is also beautifully constructed and plated in a much more French style than the usual more casual Indian restaurants that I also enjoy. Some of the standout offerings include: the aforementioned morels, the remarkable layered tastes and textures of the Potato Sphere Chaat with white pea mash, and a marvelous Crispy Hearts of Palm served in a mouthwatering, velvety coconut curry. The surprising intermezzo of pomegranate ice was a treat, as were the two desserts that followed: an aerated saffron milk dish called Makhan Malai served with rose petal jaggery brittle and almonds, and to finish, a very satisfying Doda Barfi Treacle Tart accompanied by vanilla bean ice cream with just a hint of chai spice to linger on your palate. The service was very attentive and warm, with the courses arriving in a well-timed succession. The room itself was a fairly blank slate with very minimalist decor while maintaining a very pleasant and airy feel. Perhaps the idea is that the food is the star and the surroundings are therefore kept fairly austere. I think I would have preferred a little more artistry in the room itself, but given how wonderful the entirety of the experience is, that is a small quibble. The restaurant was full, but the noise-level was moderate and conducive to conversation, which is a big plus in my book. We will be visiting the sister restaurant in New Delhi in February and cannot wait to see how it compares to our New York version. In the meantime, we are thrilled we had the pleasure of dining at this Indian Accent and hope to visit again.

Absolutely amazing. I recommend everyone go if you can! Had the lunch tasting menu and everything was delicious. The highlight for me was the rib and the treacle tart dessert. Service was incredibly attentive without being in your face. The atmosphere does kind of feel like a hotel restaurant but it's very classic and spacious

This tasting menu is incredible. I cannot recommend this enough and honestly don't understand why this doesn't have a Michelin star. It's literally insane. It's definitely not a place for cheap grub but, if you're a "tasting menu type," then it's well worth the money.

The food is decent. However the quantity of food you get makes you think they use gold and diamonds in the recipes. This is the most ridiculous example of hype vs. reality. Be prepared to spend $100-150 per person if you do not want to leave hungry due to tiny portions

I have been to Indian Accent to experience the New Year's Eve menu two years in a row, and I don't plan on going anywhere else next year. The way chef Manish Mehrotra reimagines Indian cuisine without compromising its integrity is unlike anything I have ever tasted.
The aloo bonda (served with tomato pickle chutney), which is merely an amuse bouche, is out of this world. This potato ball is so intoxicating that I don't even need wine. (Although I do highly recommend the wine pairing option for $70 ... the sommeliers are generous in knowledge and in pour).

The first course, Calcutta puchkas, is served most exquisitely with different "waters" to be poured inside - pomegranate, tamarind, chutney - and each one is to be eaten in just one bite. The puchkas are arranged in "flight" fashion, so to speak, which not only makes for a conversation piece but allows me and my boyfriend to take our time and enjoy each one before having to surrender our empty plates. 

If I described the rest of the meal, it would be equivalent to spoiling the end of an Oscar-winning film. I recommend you eat there yourself and fill in the blanks.

Midtown pre theater is usually totally forgettable, but what a find! Superb service, terrific and creative cuisine and a dessert that was not too sweet. I don't leave a whole lot of effusive reviews, but this one deserves every accolade I can give. We were going to a show at 7 pm and had dinner at 5 pm keeping in mind that they are 10 blocks from the Broadway scene. They got us out in plenty of time and we comfortably walked getting to our show with time to spare.  Highly recommend.

Contemporary take on Indian cuisine without compromising flavours, which is usually tricky to achieve in (for the lack of better word) 'fusion' food. Totally lived upto my expectations. It was the highlight of my birthday evening.
They have a good selection of dishes, something for everyone Meat,Poultry, Seafood and Vegetarian.

Tried and Recommend:
Appetiser - 
Beetroot Tikki with Goat Cheese Raita (Raita had a nice spicy kick)
Mains - 
Paneer Khurchan with Mini Roomali Rotis (they replenished rotis for us which was sweet!)
Chicken Malai Tikka with Truffle (it is actually not truffle but Kashmiri Morels) but very interesting flavours.
Accompaniment - 
Butter Chicken Kulcha (not the typical sweet tasting butter chicken) it is kulcha (flatbread) with butter chicken stuffing. Liked this one a lot. 
Dessert of course their signature ones -
Makhan Malai (it is famous Daulat ki Chaat from Delhi), it is not a traditionally made one, but a good light airy dessert after a heavy meal and Doda Barfi Treacle Tart (tasted good, although I could not quite taste the Doda Barfi in it). 

Cons - 
Crab Claws with Cauliflower - Crab meat did not have much flavour. Lot of masala was on the outer shell. 
Amuse Bouche - the famous Blue Cheese Naan 
was raw in the centre. Did not like the Pumpkin Shorba very much.

Gave one star less also because, I wish they had the option to order A La Carte instead of 3 or 4 courses. They currently have that option but only if you choose to be seated at the bar/patio (now closed due to winter). 

Extremely generous portions. We could not finish our 3 courses and had to have the dessert to go. Which is why I would prefer A La Carte. 
Impeccably clean and neat place.
Service is very good and prompt. Friendly, warm and very helpful staff.

Took my fiancé here for this 30th Birthday. We both partook in the 3 course meal and wine parings, overall such a great experience. For the food and wine parings, everything complemented each other regardless if the paring was complex or simple. As for the service 5 stars all around. The table hosts were incredibly accommodating and offered great recommendations and input. I'll definitely be coming back again.

Really good food and coming from someone who grew up in India. Did the 3 course pre fix dinner and got the tiger prawns, pickled ribs, and Assamese dumplings. Absolutely loved the shrimp and ribs, but the dumplings were pretty amazing too. For the main course we got the chicken malai tikka, sea bass, and ghee roast lamb. I personally thought the malai chicken was too creamy, but the rest of my party loved it. And for the dessert, I would get the treacle tart. It was the best end to the entire meal. And the kheer wasn't too bad either. Overall, great experience. I would love to try their tasting menu the next time.

Food: 4/5
Service: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 3.5/5
 
I celebrated a nice birthday dinner here. While I wasn't blown away, it was a good meal and the service was great. 

An amuse bouche of soup and blue cheese puff were nice touches to the start of the meal. I loved the sweet pickle ribs (5/5) which literally fell off the bone, and leans on the sweeter tangy side. The crab claws (4/5) are nicely spiced with some lingering heat. Eat the claws with your hands, just like chicken wings - somehow it makes it more satisfying. The tiger prawns (4/5) come 2 to an order under a shower of thin crisps, with a fried "hashbrown" of sorts. Also comes with a kick of spice. For mains, we had the ghee roast lamb (5/5) - their signature dish - which should definitely be on your table. Even though I do not love lamb, the flavors married so well and it wasn't too gamey; plus you get to play with the toppings in a DIY taco format and it's great fun. Try some stuffed in the laccha naan if you order it, and definitely try the butter chicken kulcha (5/5) for a delicious stuffed flatbread experience. I was a bit disappointed by the the paper roast dosa (3.5/5), because it is definitely focused less on the dosa than what was hiding under the dosa. A little bland, a little boring. The tofu masala (3.5/5) was also lackluster, reminding me of a very simple Chinese dish. In fact, it was really hard not to see the ties to Chinese flavors during my meal, which is not necessarily a bad thing but didn't leave me excited. I felt the flavors were toned down too much for the sake of "refined" dining. 

Desserts were a highlight for me. The Makhan malai (5/5) was inventive with much more intensity: saffron, rose, and other spices blended so well into the creamy fluffy souffle. Literally eating a spiced cloud. The treacle tart (5/5) was even better. Gooey but not too sweet, spiced but not too intense, a deep molasses flavor, warm like a hug and cooled down with a simple but perfect vanilla ice cream. The little plate of complimentary dessert bites are... quite interestingly flavored. 

Our waiter was extremely helpful with translating the menu and steered us towards quite a few recommended dishes. There was a bit of a delay bringing out the birthday candle after the desserts already arrived. 

This is a good option for a special occasion meal that's non traditional. The room is nice but I wouldn't say romantic. Worth going for a good meal, but I'm not running back. I crave a little more spice.

We had dinner at Indian accent last night and it was a great experience overall. I would have given it 5 starts as the ambiance, service, and our entrees were exceptional but I was a little disappointed by the appetizers. We ordered a 4 course menu and both of our appetizers - the potato spheres and the beet and peanuts butter balls- were just ok. The entrees on the other hand were out of this world. This is what great food should do to your tastebuds- really push the boundaries of flavor combinations and textures. The crab claw and black rice dumplings with nettle broth were to die for and the mushroom dosa and the chicken malai marke were fantastic. we are excited to try the tasting menu next!
Fantastic food, excellent service. Nicely done. Lamb chops are amazing - the best I have ever had. Highly recommend. Must visit.
Excellent modern indian cuisine with a punch of flavors and spice. We got the 4 course dinner and were stuffed by the 3rd course. Must try the Makhan Malai!

This was by far one of the best meals, presentations and service i've had in some time. Kenneth, our server, was superb. His diner engagement and knowledge of the cuisine as a whole, menu and restaurant was off the chart. It was AN ACTUAL EXPERIENCE. And dining with three Bengali friends, to have two of them my age (30's) and the other a mother who came here from India, ALL have the same superior experience as I did was out of this world. Says a lot for the restaurant. And i'm critical as i've been a chef in NYC for over a decade and now have my own business. So go here. Try it. Enjoy it. Experience it. It's off the chart smart, clean, aromatic, beautifully presented and full of flavor food!

I was traveling to NY for work and was in the mood for some Indian Cuisine. Had not heard of Indian Accent at the time, but the reviews seemed really positive. To be honest, The reviews I read set the bar really, really, high and yet somehow, I left simply in love with this restaurant. 

Since I was eating alone I sat at the bar. The bartenders Shawn and Jesse were incredibly friendly, and in between pouring drinks explained the origin of the restaurant (which in itself was really interesting), and in general were so friendly, I kind of forgot I was eating alone. 

The only issue I had with the restaurant, was that I couldn't stop eating. Well, that and that we don't have anything nearly this amazing where I'm from. They brought out a Pumpkin Shorba and Blue cheese naan to start the night, which while both incredible, I just wanted to swim in the Pumpkin Shorba all night. It was that good. I then ordered the potato sphere chaat which was equal parts sweet and spicy, but overall just amazing. I also ordered the chicken malai tikka with a side of naan. The Chicken tikka was incredible paired with the truffle. 

I was full at this point, not uncomfortably so mind you, just pleasantly full. But I didn't want to stop eating, so I didn't. I ordered the makhan malai for desert (and I very rarely order desert). Maybe because it was so light and airy, or maybe because it was a just plain heavenly blend of saffron, rose and almond, I ate the whole thing. 

I had to call it a night, if for no other reason than I probably could have spent another 2 hours tasting my way through other items on the menu I wanted to try. I half jokingly asked if they would be open for breakfast (they are not, but do brunch on the weekends). I'll definitely be back with my wife to try the chefs tasting. 6 out of 5.
We went for our anniversary lunch to these amazing restaurant.  Awesome food!!! Awesome service!!! Recommend most definitely !!! Loved the experience

We have been coming to Indian Accent to celebrate all our occasions and celebrations for the past few years. In the beginning we loved everything about dining at Indian Accent, the food, service, hospitality everything was amazing.
But during my last visit last week, everything was horrible!!! Completely horrifying! The food is below par, no flavor, bad taste!! My husband and I were so disappointed by the food as well as the service we received. I get it that the restaurant was quiet crowded but we do not expect a bad service any time in a Michelin star restaurant!! I am sad to see Indian Accent loose it's magic from what it was when they opened in NYC.

This place was phenomenal! It was my first experience of a pseudo tasting menu of indian food. I am also very picky with indian food as well. They started us with an amuse bouche of delicious pumpkin coconut soup and bleu cheese naan. I would have never thought that these combinations would fuse well with indian food but it did. It was nice; we had our son with us and they were nice that he ordered only one entree, and he loved it. My husband started with the potato sphere chaat which was good but not as good as my appetizer. I started  with the beet peanut butter tiki with goat cheese raita which was not sweet at all. It was the perfect savory dish. My husbands second dish was the jackfruit pulka which he loved that he ate it so fast, I couldn't even had a bite. Our third course was the spinach kofta and the tawa paneer which was accompanied by palak paneer stuffed naan and rice. It was great. The tawa paneer is similar to all types of typical paneer dish but it was very tasty with great accompaniments including the chutneys. The spinach kofta was different and very tasty. 
At the end of the dinner, we were debating where we wanted dessert and decided we might as well try the desserts, and boy were we happy that we did. We had makhan malai and doda bharfi. They both were delicious. The makhan malai was nice and light and the bharfi balanced it out well with being a bit heavier. 
We were debating if wanted to eat here again during our trip, but there are so many new restaurants that we didn't, but we will definitely be back on our next visit.

We came here for my boyfriend's birthday and got the dinner tasting menu. The tasting menu comes with A LOT of food so we were pretty stuffed by the end of our meal. Every single element and dish served during our night was perfection. The service is very kind and caring and does not have the hoity-toity snobby feel that most upscale high-end restaurants have. Every single server that came to our table was very approachable and welcoming. 

Had a very unique mint yogurt cocktail that left an long-lasting impression.

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC by far and that is something I don't say lightly. 

This is just for the tasting menu though! Highly recommend - it's well priced and gives you a lot of food with great craftmanship, elegance, and fine taste.

By far, this was the best Indian food I've ever eaten. We had a wonderful waiter and we asked that he decide all course choices that he'd recommend. You could see his delight and pride in his reaction. He did not disappoint. The amuse bouche (I know, it's not a French place, but I don't know the phrase in an Indian language) was absolutely magnificent! Pumpkin soup served in a tiny, brown coffee cup along with tiny naan stuffed with blue cheese. The only thing that came to mind was, "More please!" The ghee lamb was outrageously delish, but my favorite dish was the beet encrusted chunky peanut butter. An explosion of warm, silky, crunchy delight.

This place is excellent, offering savory flavors and enhancing the concept of Indian cuisine. The service is excellent, they still send over staff to check on a table, they check your coat by table number and no need for the ticket stress.  They have a nice collection of teas and some great cocktails and an extensive wine list.  We are definitely returning.
This is 1 of the best Indian food I have had in a long time. The flavors are something which Indiana would love, I would recommend this place to anyone.

So I will get the negative out of the way first. We had a 8:45 reservation for 3, got there at 8:50 and were kept waiting for a table standing by the front desk for 35 minutes. We were about to leave and they finally seated us. Best part was we got seated right next to a table of actors! (Robert De Niro and Anupam Kher and other's!!) and now to the food. We were not a fan of the complimentary soup and blue cheese naan. We had the 3 course prix fixe menu. The sweet potato, the ribs, the ghee lamb, the chicken kofta and the dosa were absolutely amazing!! The ribs literally melt in your mouth and the lamb had so much flavor. The mathri trio and the shrimp/ scallop biryani were underwhelming. For dessert we got the Dhoda and the makhan malai. Both were good in their own way. The malai was very light and the dhoda was heavy. All I know was I couldn't breathe after all that food lol. Some maternity pants would have been amazing. It's a good spot overall to have an experience. I still like junoon more though
We waited an hour for a table for a 9:15 pm reservation, the hostess was so rude, they were completely unapologetic, I will never be going here again! This place sucks!

Walked into an empty restaurant at opening time only to be rudely told that the next available time to be seated was 10:00 PM. We asked if they take reservations only, they said no but they're "pretty committed". We continued to stand outside near by waiting for a cab a few of our friends, only to see the restaurant continued to stay empty for the next 30 minutes. It just seems like terrible business to not seat someone when there's no other customers and the restaurant is massive. Hope this changes some day.

The tasting menu is fantastic. Chef's take on traditional recipes from north-south-east & west India is quite fascinating. As I read the menu, I was very intrigued by almost all the dishes and I wished I had the appetite to try them all. I ended up picking the four course menu and chose - potato sphere chat, tiger prawns w/peanut sago vada, spinach kofta with pea salan and chicken tikka kulcha, makhan malai. Everything was delicious! The drinks are innovative as well. Mudra punch is a must try if you are craving for some good old rose flavor. 

The ambiance and service is fantastic. Definitely a treat!

Very good "new indian" food. Atmosphere is nice, service was attentive. I thought it was a bit pricey for the amount of food, but the dishes were beautifully laid out. Appetizers were very good, but my sea bass entree was a bit underwhelming. Overall, a nice pre-theatre meal in midtown

This place is amazing! The service and presentation of the food is off the chart without being pretentious. We tried the 4 course tasting menu which allowed us to try a variety of their dishes. This is not your typical Indian cuisine. I had pulled jackfruit as one of my dishes, it was so good. I've had jackfruit before as a stand alone fruit, and had no idea it could be served as a meat substitute, delicious!! The desserts were also very good, combining several ingredients to create an explosion of flavor. I highly recommend this place while in NYC
What a unique dining experience. My family and I really enjoyed our lunch. We are looking to return for dinner

It's been a while since I've eaten here but Indian Accent is my favorite fine dining restaurant when it comes to Indian food. The staff is great, the food is delicious, and the presentation is awesome. I usually send people here when they're looking for something special that isn't another steakhouse or French restaurant. Never fails.

This place has great traditional food with cool and fresh techniques and has incredible presentation. 
Friendly staff, and amazing ambience! 

Their makai makhan is a MUST try! Will visit again soon :)

Fanciest, most modern Indian restaurant I've been to. Modern, Indian-American cuisine in a refined space. Sat at the bar and sampled a few things, but will need to come back for sit down dinner with a small group. Pork dumplings were incredible. My friend had a chicken dish what I can only describe as meatball-esque which was absolutely delicious.

Amazing food and impeccable service. Definitely a treat, but worth it! We went to celebrate our engagement and were offered a glass of champagne upon seating. We opted for the four course and while the servings were on the smaller side, they packed a burst of flavors! If you're a burbon drinker, try the Mughal Fortification cocktail- it was amazing!

Excellent service and phenomenal food. Did the chef's tasting (10 courses) and they allowed me to substitute one of their dishes so I got to try the sea bass. Cocktails are also fantastic. Service is very attentive--also interesting in that they rotate which people serve you food so you basically get to meet the host etc. Come for a special occasion and you won't regret it
Best Indian food I've had. Get the Paneer. Service was great too. They squeezed us in without a reservation.
I have been to this location twice. At first I was a bit apprehensive, but oh boy did we enjoy the venue. We plan on returning in near future

How if French cuisine is merged into the Indian cuisine? As you know, I love the well-presented, elegant French cuisine, and I also like full of flavor Indian cuisine. So when few years ago, I saw this related post  - it was the news about the Indian food but mixed by French food. 

It keep reminds me always and I wish I can try this fine cuisine once a day. And finally today is coming! It was the best atmosphere experience, fine cuisine in my life to taste Indian, French cuisine. If you are looking for vegan fine food options, attending the important date or business meetings,  Indian Accent in New York would be the great option for you!

I love this place a lot and it's a great place to fit non-Indian Foodies. And it offers many vegan choices. I'll definitely come here again!

Being of Indian descent myself, I wasn't sure if this restaurant was going to live up to the hype but I'm pleased to say it did! We chose to do the vegetarian tasting menu and it was delicious! The chef, Manish Mehrotra, put a modern twist on some classic Indian dishes but not without losing the authenticity, which was great. All in all, I think this is a place my parents (the biggest critics, for good reason) would really enjoy and will plan to bring them back.

This might get a little mushy, but I have nothing but good things to say about this restaurant. It is the best fusion of Indian and modern I have ever experienced! Went for my birthday and I couldn't have asked for a better ambiance to celebrate in. The staff was very accommodating with how much food I wanted and what would be the right choice. My bf and I did the chef's menu. 

The sphere chaat: gives you the perfect mixture of sweet and sour with the green apple slice and sweet chutney. Along with the yogurt chutney, which is the cherry on top 

Soy Keema and pav: so soft and buttery. This dish was airy light with the hint of spice which is not overpowering so you definitely want in every bite.

Paper dosa: this was my personal favorite because the concept of a dosa as a dome and the mushrooms inside was mind blowing to me. Don't be fooled by the picture! The real deal is inside, perfect blend of mushrooms with the crispy covering with a scoop of the chutney

Desserts: makhan malai: was my birthday treat and OMG it melted in my mouth. It is crunchy because of the jaggery brittle, flavorful because of the saffron and rose petals, and smooth because of the malai. What else can you ask for in life? 

Crispy seviyan: this was crispy noodles for dessert with ice cream. An amazing concept that everyone needs to try at least once! My mom makes these noodles at home but the crispy version of them with rice pudding is to die for! 

Recommended? 100%!!!

We were planning were to celebrate our anniversary and I had few options in mind. Being a week day we had to work it out in a given time slot. So here we were in Indian accent 

Started with the cocktails , they all are pretty good .

We decided to go for the 8 course tasting meal which couldn't  be taken by just one person so we both took it . The attendant made few changes on our request .

The fear of whether we will be hungry after the meal as the portions are so small soon faded away after the 4th course , as the food is so rich and you actually enjoy every bite of it .

This place should be visited and really don't think it's a kids place . Because if you want to enjoy every course you need to keep the kids away  Also the question arises what will the kids eat ? So let's keep them with baby sitter and enjoy a romantic peaceful sumptuous meal

I came here because of reviews saying that they could accommodate vegans, and Indian Accent certainly delivered. I got the four course menu with the wine pairing, and I was extremely pleased with everything. First of all, the staff was very knowledgeable about what vegan meant and though the menu wasn't labeled vegan, our server immediately knew what I could eat. This is always way more comforting than being met with confusion and a "let me check with the kitchen" response. The portions were a little big for me, but I know that many people appreciate that. Usually when I do vegan prix fixes or tasting menus at other places the portions are too small because it's usually just the side of a main dish, so I guess I really shouldn't be complaining about them being too big. Everything was really tasty. The wine pairing was also really good and creative. At first our wines were just poured to us with little explanation, but after our sommelier realized I was actually interested in what I was drinking, he opened up and started giving me details about the wines and why they were chosen which I appreciated. By the time we got to the dessert court I thought I couldn't eat any more I was so full, but I kept it together and am proud to say I finished almost all of it. Overall, it was such a nice experience to be able to have a fine dining restaurant that can handle and appreciate their vegan guests!

Get the right dishes and this place is great if you aren't afraid of some spices.

I love the crab claw option. Be warned portions are properly sized so three courses are plenty for a regular customer.

Found this on a lark when we were craving Indian food after a day of walking around New York. Very professional staff from the start to finish. They accommodated us immediately and the wait staff were helpful with choosing from the menu and they 
patiently answered all out questions even though we took a bit longer to find what we were going to eat.

The chef has created a chef's tasting menu which is a four course menu including dessert going for $125 and a bit more with wine pairing. There is also an option to mix and match a 3 or 4 course menu. We choose the latter with a 3 course menu and chose a couple of things from appetizers - sweet potato with okra and a roasted beets with peanut butter - main courses - paper dosa and seared sea bass - and desserts - a cloud of malai and barfi with vanilla ice cream.

They were all absolutely delicious and we were totally stuffed by the end if it. It took a good 10 block walk to walk off the dinner. This was by no means a heavy dinner just that it was delicious and it makes for a good dinner. Hats off to the chefs and the wait staff.

Recommend.

High end, refined environment. and good and really very professional service. Spice-wise, it's seriously toned down, so more of an American/European take on Indian cuisine. I would call it India-influenced but nothing like anything I've had in even high-end places in India. Bartender doesn't know the difference between "up" and "on the rocks". For an occasion, for those unaccustomed to Indian cuisine but accustomed to a high-end environment, this is highly recommended. For those that love Indian cuisine, just be aware what you're not getting into.

Amazing restaurant! Came here to catch up with an old friend. Of course very pricey, but well worth the price. We came for lunch so I think it was a bit cheaper. Very nice setting but everyone i saw was dressed casually (probably because it was lunch). I started with the tuna and salmon, which was very light and the different flavours really complemented each other. The crunch was also amazing and added a nice texture. 

I also got the chicken malai tikka, which was very good. It was not too creamy and had a very nice kick of spice, however not too spicy that even people who don't eat spice, couldn't eat it. 

My friend got the roast lamb which was very good. It reminded us of Peking duck because of the ability to fold your own serving. 

Overall great experience. High ceilings but it could get a little noisey when it was fully packed. We also finished with the makhan malai which was amazing! Very light.
Outstanding Michelin star quality Indian food with delicate presentation and fantastic service.

Loved everything about this place !!! Attention to detail and very courteous staff. We ordered two 3 courses dinner and everything was spot on ! I m a fan of lamb/goat curry . Extra 0.5 stars for ghee roast lamb which was extremely tender. There are a lot of options for vegetarians . It's a win win place for all except people who are on diet because you would want to keep on eating . I was too full for desserts but would be coming back soon to try them ! Little expensive but then it's exquisite stuff so it's worth the $$$$.

Visited for lunch earlier this week. Things got off to a bad start - I was running late for my reservation and called the restaurant as a courtesy and got a very rude gentlemen on the phone simply recited their 15 min grace period and did not hear anything I had to say. In any case, I decided to show up anyway and was seated. 

I am going to forgive this interaction, as I was completely blown away by the food. Service in the restaurant was outstanding as well and the space is beautiful. We had the short ribs, pork dumplings, chicken malai tikka, and ghee roast lamb. All were beautiful interpretations of Indian cuisine with superb flavors. I strongly recommend the lamb. The stuffed kulchas are also excellent. 

Such fine Indian restaurants are very hard to find in the US. If you like Indian and are visiting NYC, I'd strongly recommend giving Indian Accent a try.

Very interesting take on Indian food. Had brunch with family and friends and really enjoyed the experience. Service was great as they were very patient though we stayed way beyond closing time. We did the shared brunch feast for the table and enjoyed both the first and second courses. Definitely plan to come back and try other meals.

Disappointing to say the least, the keema pao flavors were good but the bread doesn't have any lime leaf aroma or flavor and the portion of the bread doesn't match the portion of the meat unless you're supposed to eat about ten bites of keema without any bread for second the chicken tikka was succulent and flavorful the truffle kinda got lost in the other flavors my friend got the ghee roast lamb, which was good. 
Both the desserts were blah all in all perhaps my expectations were too high for the place

Amazing Indian food!!! We came in here for lunch at 1:59pm and they close at 2pm for lunch but the host was so nice and found us a table quickly. We all had the two course lunch and everyone loved their food. Service was quick and our server recommendations were all great. Highly recommend the below:

From first course:
- soy keema
- sweet pickle ribs

From second course:
- paper roast dosa
- soft shell crab koliwada: love love love this. The rice was so flavorful and was perfectly cooked, the soft shell crab was crunchy yet soft and so delicious 
- chicken malai tikka

I highly recommend this place!

My husband and I just returned from enjoying the 8 course tasting menu at lunchtime. We travel a lot and enjoy eating food from many cultures. He is a meat lover and I am pescatarian with a preference for vegetarian food. What we experienced at Indian Accent, was probably one of  most exceptional dining experiences we have ever had! From the clean, minimalist decor, to the genius serving vessels and plating, to the attentive service of a crew of elegant waitstaff, this restaurant has it all. And the food? Sheer heaven! While it is clearly Indian inspired food, there are elements of surprise, such as tiny  bite sized blue cheese naan or the mustard sauce with a kick of horseradish and lemon served with the overstuffed kulcha. I could write pages about this place, but just GO! I must, recommend trying one of the many creative cocktails. I enjoyed the Pisco Rising, a combination of chamomile pisco, almond liquor and lemongrass bitters so much, that my husband "made " me order a second. Every element of every dish made sense in its way of maximizing the star of the dish and was gorgeously presented. Having had the experience of dining at Indian Accent was an experience we will not forget and hope to repeat!

We went the to celebrate our Anniversary. We tried the tasting menu.
The food is very delicious and beautiful presented. It's true when they say food presentation adds to the taste.
Care is taken to even sett the right spoon, and for certain courses no spoon, to encourage using your fingers.
The portions are small, but you are full by the end of the course.
I loved all the chefs preparations, but stuffed kulcha and 
Malai Makkah was my favorite 

This is the first time we had tried a tasting menu at a up scale restaurant, so cannot really compare the prices.
100$ per person felt steel, but personally it felt worth the price.

Service here is weirdly good. We came here for our anniversary. I ordered a meal that didn't come with enough naan, and they literally heard me complaining and brought more naan. That's some attentive service!

Food here is some of the better Indian food in New York. But I have to say, the New York Location doesn't even compare to the original Indian Accent restaurant in Delhi. Obviously. But still, food was good. I feel like all the Indian restaurants in New York are trying to take a page out of Gaggan's book and add a more gastro twist to the Indian cuisine. I appreciate it, but even then, all the "eclectic" or "modern" indian restauarants in new york are starting to feel the same. They're literally just making portion sizes smaller and presentation better, with some added attention to the taste of the food too. But the cuisine hasn't changed in my opinion, just the style, presentation, and portion size. And that's why no Indian restaurant in new york has been able to truly match Gaggan or Junoon's reputation. Change the food too!! Not just the way it looks. I can see through that.

The most magical meal I've had, probable ever. 

Tasting menu vs a 3 or 4 course meal was the biggest decision for us. 

Ended up going with the 4 course meal since this gave us the option to pick any item on the menu so we got to try 8 different dishes between the two of us. The tasting menu is QUITE a marathon so make sure you work up an appetite beforehand if you choose it. 

Pictures speak louder than words so look below to get a taste of the magic - all dishes labeled although the menu changes regularly. All the dishes were great so you can't go wrong with any choice.

Very good food. Went here for my wife's birthday and we were very happy with the quality of the food and service. We had the weekend brunch and the Malai Makhan dessert was a great way to finish off the meal.

I was skeptical about the place cause of the price and menu options. We tried the 4 course meal. This place twisted Indian food in a way where my palate tasted the simplest of individual flavor and spices. Great ambience and customer service. A must-try place for someone anyone who loves Indian food.

Service here is really good, most importantly I loved the vegetarian options and the dessert. All the food was well seasoned and served to perfection. Cooked very thoroughly and a large amount of options as it's a large number of courses being offered. However the portion control for each course made it manageable to taste a variety of flavors. Make sure to make a reservation online or via phone beforehand.

Amazing!  The most expensive but the best Indian restaurant I have been to in U.S.  The talent of the chef is evident in every dish.  The flavors are perfect, mix of traditional Indian flavors but with a twist.  Honestly the meal was very filling!  The only criticism I have is if have a big party (more than 4) on the phone they try to give you a less desirable time first but you can negotiate and immediately hey will give you a better time.  Maybe they are saving earlier slots in the eve in case the Obamas visit which is understandable.  Regardless the meal was perfect and would return again for sure, but for now time to save up for that visit

I have been to the Indian Accent both in London and India which I will say were amazing!!! I just called the NYC location to make brunch reservations for 9 people for my husband's birthday celebrations and got told they do not accommodate for more than 8 guests!!!! This is ridiculous! So if there is a larger family you discriminate against them and won't allow them into the restaurant?!? I am absolutely appalled at this. I was not allowed to make the reservation in the end. Shame on the management and the "rules" you have in place for who can and cannot dine in this restaurant. Sad.
I have had better experiences here than last night. Came here after a lot of planning however everything took forever. Very disappointed in the food as well as the service.

Ah what a delight! What a delight! I loved everything about Indian Accent! The ambience was wonderful, inviting, modern and functional. The food is beyond! I don't even have an adjective to describe how delicious the food is. We had the non-vegetarian tasting menu (See picture) and it was perfectly executed - every single element was meant to be there, not one thing was out of place. My personal favorites were all the appetizers! They were literally so flavorful that I am craving some again as I write this review. I would go back again, order the tasting menu plus all the appetizers! 
The service is seamless, coordinated and refined. The staff is keen with their details, always checking in and making polite conversation. 
You have to visit Indian Accent (in any three locations around the globe) to really understand what I am trying to convey. Allow yourself to indulge in this restaurant and I promise you it will be nothing like you have experienced with Indian cuisine. It will leave you wanting more.

Took my wife for our anniversary. It was fantastic on all levels, the food was spectacular, the service was perfect. The 5 individuals who served our table were perfectly professional and very knowledgeable about every dish we ordered. 
If I could give 10 stars I would, it was the quintessential dining experience.

I felt like I was dining at Michelin star restaurant. The presentation was so beautiful, but the portion size was ridiculously small. Brunch will set you back $100 per person.

I don't know why everyone raves about the potato chaat, it's hard and doesn't taste like potato. The Pea kofta was very spicy and served with one tablespoon of rice, yes that's correct. The kufta was so small. You have to give vegetarians a larger serving size so we don't leave still hungry. For dessert I got the Makhan Malai (a cream cake) which was larger than my entree! It was incredible, so delicious and fluffy! The metal straw with my drink was hard on my teeth.

The service was very attentive and so professional. The bathroom was beautiful, but too dark to check my teeth and fix my lipstick. Having a toilet lid in a public toilet is just nuisance. The sink was too low.

Underwhelming!

I took my dad today to Indian Accent for his 80th bday. The food was mixed, service good and bad... overall experience worse than I would have ever imagined!

Good: the waiters were attentive. The last dessert was exceptional. Chicken naan one of the better dish, not that I think that requires a 5-star chef skills

Bad: most food was underwhelming. We order the chefs menu. The pani poori - I liked only one out of 5 flavors. Amritsar cod - there was nothing amritsari about it. Chicken kofta - bland and tasteless. Prawns - portion was so small that I felt as if they were serving caviar. I don't remember the rest because it wasn't worth remembering. The food flavors are not any special.  A good chef can do a lot with Indian spices. This is mediocre at best.

Ugly: the wait. This is an overly pretentious place where they are more focused to change ur utensils than to serve you exceptional food. The worse was the wait. The chef prioritized 5 other table around us in the middle of our meal while those folks came well after us.. they made us wait for a good 40'minutes before I had to request twice to the waiters to bring our food. 

My dad who is least demanding was utterly disappointed. Such a special day and such a waste. Spent $800 for a meal for 4. Save your money, go to Chola, their paani poori is fantastic. Tamarind is good service with great flavors. 

I am disgusted I chose this place. Shame on the management
Ok. What a great experience. Not just meat in gravies or a mountain of rice. This was such a delight. So happy to visit and this place makes me want to come back.

What an awesome experience. Was definitely worth the money. The atmosphere & the food definitely worth every praise.
I'd highly recommend the chef's tasting menu. Drinks were pretty good as well.

Wow wow wow, this place was unreal! The service was amazing, Andrew our waiter, went above and beyond! The food was maybe the best Indian I've ever had, it's not traditional, but it's brought it to the next level! Can't say enough nice things about this place!

I had heard mixed reviews about the restaurant from my friends in Delhi and NYC. I went for the Sunday brunch with my family with zero expectations and was pleasantly surprised. The owner Chef Manish Mehrotra was in the kitchen and I requested the manager if my father could say hello to him since my father follows him on TV. To my surprise Chef Mehrotra came up to say hello after we had finished brunch. 
The food was very authentic. I have not had fresher chutneys and accompaniments anywhere else in NYC except Junoon. Their street food was excellent. The papdi chaat and the crab cheese toast evoked memories of Delhi. They tasted exactly as if they were straight out of a very creative and competent Punjabi Aunty's kitchen. The curry with the shrimp omelette was fresher than the butter chicken gravy at most Indian restaurants. The dessert Makhan malai was phenomenal. The restaurant is expensive, but the food quality and experience makes it worth a visit.

Unreal.The food and service here is unreal.We went to celebrate a special day and had the chef's tasting menu.Every plate of food that was kept in front of us was a masterpiece in itself.Everything tasted soo delicious and absolutely amazing.My favorite will definitely be the makhan malai ... i can't explain how good it is...Everyone should try it once
Ahh!! the gola ...reminded me of my childhood.
Being an Indian and have been eating indian food all my life ...I never thought i would be able to appreciate modern indian food to this extent.
Definitely worth visiting.
The absolute most incredible Indian food we have ever eaten. True haute cuisine and the service was the best. Andrew took fantastic care of us and made the evening one to remember forever!!

Me and 2 of my coworkers from out of town wanted to try this restaurant out. We had made a reservation almost 4 weeks in advance. When we got to the place (right on time), we were given a table which was meant for 2 people. We requested the restaurant manager to give us another table and we got a cold response that take this or wait for 1 hour. I go to these kind of exclusive restaurants for the experience and service (apart from the food). The experience & customer service which we received was awful. We left the place and don't think I will come back again.

I and my girl friend had a brunch feast here on Sunday. The food are so delicious. The presentation is very pretty. My friend's brunch drink with fresh pressed ginger is amazing. My pisco is also fantastic. The food came in time. Atmosphere is nice and quiet. Love this place! Will come back again to try different dishes.

Found!
I love Indian Accent. It is a modern take on traditional Northern Indian cuisine. I was recently in Delhi and enjoyed my meal (lunch) here as much as I did there. Much like Indian culture, the dishes are bursting with flavor and personality. Excellent price fixe lunch with standouts dishes including tofu masala with shishito peppers, butter chicken kulcha, and the paper roast dosa with wild mushrooms.
For more great reviews visit TheLoupe!

Don't go expecting a full blown Indian menu, Indian Accent is an Indian Fusion restaurant with great flavors! My favorite was the Malai Dessert as well as their Dumplings! I also liked the fact that their menu of the course 3 or 4 can be all apps or entrees! Some of people in our group of 6 for all entrees as well.  I did feel that the drink menu was good however a little too pricey! It's a one time restaurant and for a special occasion with a small intimate group.  I don't recommend bringing any children as the restaurant will not have any options that are kid friendly.  I also recommend making reservations.  The restaurant only takes a max reservation of 6 people.  But call to confirm they don't accommodate parties larger than 6 to ensure you are able to get the full experience of their menu.  Enjoy!

Don't come here. Big waste of money. First of all, the service is sub par. We complained to the manager because the waiter did not come by to take our order after waiting 20 minutes, and he responded in a very rude tone. Did not make us feel welcome at all. The waitstaff seemed like they hated their jobs there, kind of felt bad for them. The food is pretty good but definitely not worth the steep price. For 3 small courses, it costs $75 a person. My first two courses were very good, but the final course (chicken tikka something) tasted like someone had put cheap Alfredo sauce over chicken salad. Absolutely tasteless. Didn't even want to tip this meal but felt bad for the waiter. Overall, food was good be definitely not worth the price. Quality of service was terrible. I would go to any hole in the wall traditional Indian place over this.

My self and two other ladies had a great lunch experience here! We set at the bar and did two course brunch menu for $38.  One guest of our party is dairy and gluten free and they were able to accommodate her very nicely.  I am vegetarian I had plenty of choices for both courses.  I am glad we visited this place.
