The bar tender was very friendly and he even treated us with a dairy free smoothly like drink!!  Can't wait to be back for dinner here!

Indian cuisine in a modern way. Everything about this place is excellent and exquisite. I can't believe they don't have  Michelin stars yet. Not just food, the cocktails and desserts are too good to be true.

I we outraged to learn this establishment doesn't allow children under 10! At arrival we were told they don't have a kids menu as a poor excuse for this policy. Maybe the food is good but if you have children you won't be able to opine due to this ridiculous policy unless you come without them

Truly an amazing and inventive restaurant. Loved the pre-theater menu where you get to pick any 2 courses and 1 accompaniment. I chose the tandoori lamb chops, the beef tenderloin, and the butter chicken kulcha. Everything had so much flavor and was really delicious. The service was excellent too. Be aware it is pretty pricey. Probably more of a place for a special occasion.

Tried the chef tasting dinner menu with 3 of friends. I am very unhappy about the pace at which the courses arrive. They might have some standards, but they should understand how the customers are moving and deliver stuff faster. There is a 20 minute gap between each course for 10 courses, not kidding we spent 3 hours at this place.

Waiters are knowledgeable about what they are doing. 

Just an advise, don't stick to your standards. Get along with the customers and serve them better. At the end of the day customer satisfaction is important for places like yours.

We had a lovely dinner at Indian Accent. The service was impeccable, the food was delicious, beautiful, and interesting. My partner and I loved our cocktails as well. The space is comfortable, elegant, and accessible. Gender neutral bathrooms, too.

AMAZING food! I totally enjoyed the food! Went for a three course meal plus a drink. It fills you up quite good! Ordered sweet potato as an app, masala tofu, green pease kofta, black dal with garlic naan.. overall, it was a great experience! The service was pretty good too.
If you love Indian food is absolute must. It's a high end nice size restaurant with very unique food and great service. Not easy to get reservations on a weekend but it's worth the wait

Such a disappointment 

The place lacks everything you would except from a fine dining restaurant.  
The ambience is absolutely the worst.  You are repeatedly reminded of crappy airport lounges /  shoddy restaurant.  

The staff, though well meaning, seems untrained and is objectively unkempt. They messed up the service in a number of ways more than once.  

Lastly the food- I kept longing for more.  I wished for More flavor, more innovation, more quality.  
The chefs have done nothing more than a lazy job putting together a modern Indian meal that left me with a lot to desire. The only discernible flavor in the chaats was that of tamarind chutney and most other dishes just did not work together.

Pros: The food was delicious with beautiful presentations. My favorite was the puri appetizer with different fillings, chaat sphere, kofta and lamb entree

Cons: The guy checking in on us during the dinner was very intrusive. Didn't let us enjoy in peace. The 'sabudana' amuse bouche was WAY too hot. Provided there was no plate on my table, I ate it directly from the servers tray. Hot oil poured out as I took a bite and ended up burning my tongue and palate. I was unable to properly enjoy rest of my courses. 

Overall, some delicious apps and entrees, and poorly executed amuse bouche

By far the best restaurant experience in Manhattan- if you are done with the typical Indo- American orange kinda gravies of butter chicken and paneer tikka masala and want to try something different, Indian accent is the place to go. It had been on my wishlist for a long time to visit Chef Manish Malhotra's latest and the most talked about venture. 
I had already tired the one in India and was mighty impressed by it. I was expecting a similar kind of menu here as well but to my utter surprise, the menu was completely different and innovative
We went for the 10 course chef's tasting menu. My husband tried the vegetarian dishes while I tried the non vegetarian ones. Everything was fresh, flavorful , exquisite and delectable 
 PS - as I belong to Lucknow (the birthplace of Makkahan malai), I didn't have high expectations from that particular dish but they have done a great job at recreating that experience in NYC. Loved it!

Impressive.  Innovative. Interesting.  All describe the wonders of IA as a place of truly a fine dining experience.  From the impeccable service, to the offerings even of Pu-Er tea, to the chef's 11 course tasting menu, the flavors and delicacies are a unique combination for even a city renown for excellent gastrointestinal delights.  Our table partook in the tasting menu from the chef, and spent over two hours receiving wondrous offerings and explanations about the types of foods we were fortunate to taste; this was not street cuisine from Mumbai or Pune.  It was, quite frankly, one of the most well orchestrated dining experiences - whether in London, North America, South America or the subcontinent itself; one feels both comfortable and well-taken care of, and feels the details in both the food and the crisp service which attends to the smallest detail.

3 years ago I planned a dinner here with my future father in law. We tried the tasting menu which was exceptional. It was first time meeting him and I remember Indian Accent was newly opened. Service was impeccable. It was definitely a more fine dining experience of Indian cuisine which is great addition to the midtown power lunch/dinner scene.

Fast forward to this year my husband and I celebrated Diwali here with close friends and tried the more casual a la carte menu. Everything we ordered was amazing. The crab leg, tiger prawn (must have), lamb chop(please order this) and the deserts oh so delicious! Some might think certain dishes might be a bit overpowering but I must say we've enjoyed every single bites of that night. Will for sure come back and we plan to make it an annual Diwali dinner celebration.

Spectacular.  Incredible. Fun. Fascinating.  The two of us each ordered the chef's tasting menu. The most innovative dinner we've ever had.  Each dish was inspired by something traditional, but the chef took the familiar in new directions. A series of delicious bites that left us satisfied and full, but not heavy.  Friendly and highly efficient service, understatedly elegant ambiance.
Good and inventive cocktails; eclectic and modern take on Indian fusion; and average size portions. Great for groups or intimate celebrations.

Upscale dining with great service. I lived in Singapore and because of that I'm very picky with Indian food since a lot of places in the US don't measure up. It's impressive that they were able to maintain authenticity even with the deconstructed items on the menu, while also maintaining an elevated experience. We were short on time so we opted for the 4 course menu, but will definitely try the Chef's menu next time.

Highly recommend this place to visitors and locals alike

Worth every penny!! Everything from the food to the cocktails, ambiance and service was exceptional! We ordered the tasting menu which was very generous and absolutely delicious. Loved every single dish from its thorough description, artistic presentation to its unique Indian flavors. Busy place, even on a weeknight so reservations are encouraged! Upscale spot for date night or client lunch/dinner.

Amazing all around. Service impeccable. Everything we tried was creative and delicious. We are pescatarian and it was a beautiful dining experience. Definitely a splurge. Little unexpected things such as Coffee cups warmed before being placed in table. Spice level perfect.

Indian Accent is one of the more upscale restaurants in New York City. Located in Hell's Kitchen, this posh restaurant offers a pre fixed feast. The menu contains fusion Indian food from different Indian cuisines.
We visited Indian Accent on a Saturday and chose the brunch feast. All of us were vegetarians and so we opted for the veg options in the menu. 

Dry fenugreek paapdi chaat: Chaat is a blend of savory and spicy dish with a variety of food assembled together. This wasn't spicy at all. The fenu Greek is finely cooked so that it Melts in your mouth. It contains a crisp thin fried biscuit(paapdi) along with a mint and cilantro chutney. The soft fenugreek with the crunchy paapdi is a good option for the starter

Wild mushroom uttapam, roast onion chutney:
We were apprehensive of how a mushroom uttapam would taste but were pleasantly surprised. Mushroom is extremely soft and fresh. It's finely chopped. Uttapam is a South Indian pancake made from rice and split lentils. At Indian Accent, this pancake is stuffed mushrooms and caramelized onions. It's topped  with mint leaves and what seemed like yogurt  and mint chutney. We absolutely loved this concept 

Chili cheese toast, cucumber pickle, tamarind ketchup:
A classic toasted bread with melted cheese and chillies. The chillies aren't spicy and the tamarind ketchup on top makes it slightly sweet. I would probably avoid this next time. 

Avocado and pomegranate raita:
Raita is yogurt blended so well it's almost semi liquid. This accompanist lent comes with the main course. Adding a pomegranate and avocado to it took away the essence of the raita 

Wild Mushroom kulcha, truffle butter:
Extremely good. We have never had this and were in love with it. The tandoori naan(bread) is stuffed with mushrooms and lid greased with abundant butter. It'll the mushroom taste is not prominent to take away the essence of the main course served with it

Saag paneer kulcha, chill butter :
We could not resist but order one more of this. Paneer is cottage cheese and saag is a kind of green which tastes like spinach. It's a very popular vegetable in Northern India. This bread is filled with excellent saag paneer. Despite it being full of a paste made from saag and cottage cheese, it doesn't get soggy. I could probably eat this bread by itself.

Black dairy dal:
This is the classic dal makhani. A curry made from black lentils cooked with Indian spices in butter. Generally the excessive butter makes your throat dry but not this one. 

Baby Idlis, vegetable, gunpowder:
Idlis is a steamed dumpling made of rice. After cooking, it was sautéed in oil with chili powder and turmeric powder. Instead of just one vegetable, which I believe was radish, I would expect more flavour and veggies on this plate. 

Green pea kofta, cauliflower, coconut curry:
Probably are favourite main course. Fried dumplings consisting of green peas and cauliflower in a coconut-tomato gravy. The dumpling was topped with coconut shavings. Extremely soft and well cooked. The tomato-coconut combination was sweet and little tangy. The dryness of green peas was absorbed by the gravy. The stuffed kulchas along with this curry infuse so many flavours and keep you craving for more!

Herb paneer, soy keema, butter pao:
Keema is generally finely minced meat in butter and spices. Here, it is replaced by soy and paneer. It is slightly spicy, not much. The sly and butter is almost friend in butter. This plate is accompanied with butter pao. Pao is the local name for buns in India. Another excellent choice on the menu!

Makhan malai, saffron milk, rose petal jaggery brilltle,
Almond:
I now understand the hype regarding this dessert and why it was awarded best dessert in NYC in 2018.
This dessert is a moist fluffy sponge cake kind of dessert. Made with saffron milk and light cream, you cannot stop eating it once you start. The dessert is topped with dry fruits like most Indian desserts and you will surely be transported to India with the vet first bite

Carrot halwa crumble; salted pistachio ice cream:
The crumble is like a fried puff pastry. The filling contains figs and fried carrot thins. This is topped with a pistachio ice cream. It is extremely sweet. We would probably give this is miss

All I can say is wow, some of the best Indian food i have ever had. Went to the city with a friend and we decided to do the Tasting menu. Every single course was delicious! The service was top notch as well..very friendly and attentive staff..Will definitely go back again

Went to Indian accent last night and was completely blown away. We did the tasting menu and wine pairing. The service was impeccable and the food was absolutely incredible. The dishes were thoughtful, delicious, and presented beautifully. The sommelier could not have done a better job with the wine pairing and she was also a fantastic person. 
This is now one of my favorite restaurants and I'll make an effort to go back whenever I'm in Manhattan.
Thank you everyone for being so great!
Epically flavorful meals, perfectly executed and filled with spice. The reservationist can be a bit discouraging to talk to so would try booking online.

Probably one of the best Indian restaurants in the city. I have been to the Delhi location and I can say the NYC location is as good if not better. My taste buds were scintillating with every bite of dish. It looks like the food portions are low but at the end of the course you are stuffed! We did the lunch menu and can say it was enough food for both my wife and I to be stuffed.
Has quickly become my go-to, be it for a quick drink and snacks at the bar or the dinner tasting menu. It's excellent but please do bring back the malai chicken.

Had the fenugreek chicken entree (would not order again, kinda dry) and the pickled ribs which were delicious!  Naan wasn't bad.  Butter chicken kulcha was okay as well.  Also, word to the wise, sodas are non-refillable and cost $6.00 each!
Utterly outstanding in everything way. Service. Food. All of it. MidTown location means they charge top Dollar. But it was worth every penny.

Came here on a cold winter weekend after having read about this place online and seeing the reviews. After having too many "Chicken tikka Masalas", I was really looking forward to trying something new, interesting, and different. Overall, the place is good but not worth the price and hype.

The pork spareribs appetizers were good, as were the pancakes (we tried the wild mushroom and the roast duck ones). The fenugreek chicken was a little dry as was the paneer.  I will say the paneer sauce was good, but it tasted like a standard Chicken Tikka sauce, which was what I was trying to avoid. 

If I had to choose, the best dishes were the garlic naan and the black dairy dal. 

Service was fine though a bit slow. Not sure I'd come back but I like the concept.

I went to Indian Accent with my mom and sister to celebrate their birthdays! The decor is really nice especially in Manhattan! We tried their sweet potato shakarkandi , beetroot and peanut butter tikki and the kolhapuri chicken salad to begin with. My favorite was the kolhapuri chicken salad! The other too seemed bland and lacking flavor for my liking. For mains, we did the tandoori trout and it was yum. My mum tried the ghee roast lamb and seemed to enjoy it. The best part of the meal however were the desserts, Makhan Malai is one of the best desserts I've ever come across in my life. Light and fluffy, it packs the goodness of any malai sweet without being too heavy. The service was amazing and everybody knew what they were doing and talking about. Would I go back? Definitely for the deserts.

Ate here once.  Everything at this place is Spot On!

The decor is beautiful and understated.  The ambiance is elegant and with a moderate noise level.

All the food we got was delicious.  The presentation and execution were excellent.

Service impeccable.

Afterwards, I thought to myself 'hmm...I should mention this to the big boss's Assistant..that this might be a good place to have on their list, the next time he's looking for a midtown restaurant for a business dinner.  Turns out, this place was already on their list, and a favorite restaurant of his. (BTW, my boss is a well-travelled business exec who originally hails from the area near to New Delhi.... ;-) )

Delicious, presentation of the food is excellent.
Unique combinations of Indian spices and veggies.
Ambiance is pretty good.

Love love love this spot! There are so many overpriced and underwhelming modern Indian restaurants in NYC that totally disappoint but trust me, you'll walk out amazed and satisfied after your experience at Indian accent. 
When you walk in, the service is so nice from the beginning. They take in your coats for coat check too!
The ambiance inside is simple yet classy. There is a bar area in the front where you can grab a drink and the dining area is relatively big too. 
Our server was ridiculously nice and helpful too! She made our experience memorable. 
We started with compliments from the chef, it was so good. They treated us with blue cheese naan and a pumpkin coconut soup. Sounds like strange ingredients but they all were so tasty and savory. 
We decided to do a two course dinner. It comes with two courses along with an accompaniment (so basically 3 course). 
First we had the Assamese pork dumplings and the duck vadai and they were so good. They put a soup over the dumplings and they complemented the taste so well. There was fried vermicelli on top of the duck and it was amazing. 
Next we had (as accompaniments) corn and spinach - basically saag and corn and it was so good. We also had the butter chicken kulcha and it was creamy and delicious.
For our entrees, we got the ghee roasted lamb and gun pepper scallops. The ghee roasted lamb comes with four chutneys and small roomali rotis (you basically make tacos out of them) and the lamb was so soft and the gravy was very savory and seasoned perfectly. The scallops came with cauliflower in a creamy sauce and they were so good too. 
We lastly got the carrot halwa for dinner and it came with pistachio ice cream and it was the perfect way to end the meal. We even got the jasmine pearl tea after and it was refreshing. 
Overall very happy with my experience here and can't wait to come here again for another special occasion! This place isn't cheap, so make the most of it!

I hate to do this, but I need to share.  Being Indian, I'm exposed to Indian food of all kinds.  This was no better than the average Indian restaurant in curry hill.  It's not bad food, it's just not mind-blowing, especially for the price you pay. 

The service was not good.  It took at least 5 minutes for us to get water and menus.  The waiter didn't have the manners that I'd expect at a fancy restaurant.  He wasn't knowledgeable about the menu and seemed really disinterested in us.  What I found the most odd is that my mother is vegan and they offered to bring out naan without butter and then charged us for it.  ???

Overall very average food and service for above average costs.
I would give this place 7 out of 5 stars. Amazing food. This place easily replaces Junoon on our list of places to eat when in NYC.

We called on Nov 25th and Dec 6 to make reservations for 7 people on Dec 31st. They took the information and confirmed on the phone that they have us on the book. I call to confirm and they tell me they messed up and do not have our reservations. I will NEVER go back to this restaurant again. Incompetent people.

Superb! We were looking for a tasting menu but not then normal options. We had about 10 courses for $125 which is not too bad for the area (Per Se would charge $300).. 

Incredible food and service! Everything was tasty and very creative. Definitely not your average Indian food but more innovative. Pics attached of most courses

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday and it was amazing. I have been wanting to go and I was finally able to. The food was amazing. We did the four course menu and we were sooo full after. Although portions are small, it still stuffs you up. The ambiance, the food, the service and everything about this place is amazing. Although it is pricey, it is definitely worth trying. We had gotten non-alcoholic drinks and those were amazing. The dessert was so good too-the makhan malai. My boyfriend had told them we were there for my birthday and they gave us sorbet which was amazing!

Great place to have a nice dinner. Ambience is perfect, with an upbeat vibe, but not too loud. Our waiter was excellent, and he had the kitchen spice up our food upon our request. The butter chicken naan is a must, but I would skip the truffle naan. We ordered a la carte, mostly everything was tasty, especially the duck pakora. I would pass on the ghee roasted lamb though, as it was a bit underwhelming. The cocktails are superb, I believe I had the smoked old fashion. Definitely recommend trying this place out the next time you want a fancy dinner.

Love this restaurant. From it my passion for Indian cuisine began !!!
Chic design. Very clean place ... 
Helpful staff. 
Large portions and beautiful serving!!!

It was my first experience here and I'm glad that I did try this place, great different options from the Indian cuisine, since I was alone I just ordered 1 main dish and 1 side which is not enough, I didn't expect it will be that good but I liked it, I would come back in my next visit or maybe another location and try more options.

If this review was solely for the food, it would be 5 stars. I am by no means any food/experience critic (I usually feel gratitude to just be in the room), I pride myself on being a fair and rational person, but my oh my was the service abysmal. I flew my mom in from Tennessee to celebrate her retirement. She's crazy for Indian food and I thought this place was just the ticket for her milestone occasion. The juxtaposition of the food and service was wild. Our server never identified himself or herself and we felt lost in the chef's tasting process. At our estimation, the restaurant was only between 30-40% capacity and four of our courses came out of the kitchen before our table had been reset. My husband watched them carry the courses back into the kitchen and sit for 2-3 minutes before the table was re-set and they could be brought back. We ate a lot of warmish food or melted desserts. Half of the dishes were explained, half dropped off with a quick sentence we struggled to hear. My husband ordered a cocktail and it took around 20 minutes to hit our table, *after* food. When the glass was empty, a follow up cocktail wasn't offered and the empty glass sat on the table for the remainder of the tasting until dessert. Even though the restaurant continued to clear out, the time between our courses lengthened to the point where we wondered if our courses had been served to another table. It felt clunky, uncomfortable, and zero mention was made to my mother about her milestone occasion, even though it had been noted in the reservation and in the reservation confirmation. If we were just looking for a tasting menu and didn't care about the atmosphere, this would have been great, but we left beyond puzzled about her very, unmerry, retirement uncelebration.
Probably the best fancy Indian restaurant in NYC. Highly recommend the tasting menu. The experience is great.

Great service clubbed with great food. I was disappointed with a particular chicken dish and they replaced it with a different option which was splendid. The carrot halwa crumble is amazing and so is the makhan malai. Being from Lucknow it brought back memories of makhan malai back home. Mehrotras are the best
Had a great birthday dinner experience. They make sure you like the dish/drink, if not they will get you and ready to change it.

Great choice for a special occasion. Note that kids under 10 are not allowed. Tried the four course option and thoroughly enjoyed every one of them. Had a good selection for vegetarians across all courses.

The ambience is lovely but can be a bit loud so  if you need some aa quieter table, you will need to request the staff beforehand. The food i  called for was the three course dinner  with lamb chops, sea bass with berry rice and makhan malai dessert. I called for two drinks of Rhube which are quite tasty and strong. 
Food was great, lamb chops  were really good, juicy and tender. Sea bass doesnt have much  flavors but goes well with the berry rice. The dessert was really nice. 
The staff service is really slow. Had to wait for about an hour too get our orders in after drinks. All in all the food is good but not worth the price you pay.

I bought my girlfriend here for a post-Valentine's day dinner. Indian Accent exceeded our expectations. The food was phenomenal; the flavors were incredible as well as the presentation. The staff was extremely knowledgeable and courteous. Shoutout to our server, Andrew, for all the recommendations and excellent service. We intend on dining here again in the near future.

This place sucks. Ordered an Arnold Palmer twice and didn't get it. Ended up getting an ice tea. 
Ordered Trout and got salmon. The waiter said the flavoring they use makes the trout like a salmon. Bizarre. It is also crazy expensive for the portions. Jail house portion size or weight loss method.

An expensive disaster!  The restaurant staff from servers to the manager have no sense of hospitality.  Once seated, we waited about 15 minutes for our server.  When she arrived, she was eager to take our dinner order, but we were never asked if we wanted to order a cocktail or drink.  Overall service was or pretty poor.  We ordered the price fixe ($125 pp) chef's tasting but the servers' English was very poor and we could only make out their explanations of the dishes put in front of us about half the time.  The dishes themselves are experiments in some kind of Indian-continental fusion.  I am Indian, and while I think I enjoy a bit of experimentation, several dishes left me wondering why this restaurant is labeled Indian.  So far not a complete disaster, and I would have rated tonight's experience 3 out of 5 stars, but then something totally surprising happened.  We were served our last course (a small dessert) around 9:15pm, which we promptly finished and soon thereafter (around 9:30pm) paid the check - total with tip: $425.  Just as we're finishing our drinks and about to imminently leave, a manager interiors our conversation and loudly offers us a complimentary glass of wine at the bar.  I think he thought just approach clever, but I just  asked him if he wanted the table and he affirmed that he wanted our table to put it together with another one.  We hadn't been lingering, so I thought this request highly improper.  Regardless, told him to give us two minutes, after which we left.  On the way out, the manager tries to direct us to the bar for the free wine.  I told what he could do with his wine and left.  Would never go back to this place.  $425 for two, for mediocre food, Terri le service, and insulting management.
It was good lunch place. Good for groups and the food was innovative and not the usual Indian affair.
Very tasty food. Just remember to wear semi casual clothes or not wear too athletic wear as typical clients here are all wearing suits. Loved it.

We've been here 3 times now and every time have had a great experience. Amazing service and good. In the past we've come with people who had gluten allergies and the servers were always knowledgeable about what they could eat. Really absolutely wonderful! A little pricey for sure but in our opinion worth it!
We loved our meal! It was fancified Indian but  not to the point that was stuffy or irritating.  Everything tasted wonderful.  Their mustard tequila cocktail was THE BOMB

My fiancée and I went here for a date night in the city. We were completely blown away by not only the wonderful staff, but also the fabulous food. The flavor was immaculate. Our server perfectly paired our meals with beautifully noted wine. I would like to specifically note one of the servers Mardek (I hope I'm spelling that correctly) for his tremendous hospitality. He answered all of our questions to the best of his ability and was so kind. Definitely recommend and will most definitely be coming back.

We decided to try Indian accent after having an incredible experience at the location in Delhi last year. Nyc location is just as good and we have been back a few times this year. Food quality is always consistent, service is attentive and very respectable. The drinks, wine and all of the courses have been amazing! This is our favorite Indian restaurant in the city! Absolutely the best compared to every other 'Indian' restaurant you can name in the city.

Indian accent was the last meal we had before COVID and we are so glad they are back. Beautiful outdoor space, mindful precautions. Food and drinks are as delicious as ever. The amuse bouche are back. We had the pepper chicken (one of our fav) and the green pea kofta (loved it). We also really enjoyed the crab claws. Kulchi wise we tried the saag but prefer the butter chicken. Also
Note to self you love the mulgur fornication and the doda dessert which tasted like sticky toffee pudding with vanilla bean ice cream
The food is good but take away service is bad, people want to get desert to go,they ready to pay but they say you can't get desert to go, you can get desert only if you dine in.

My family and I went last night to celebrate my husband's birthday.  We drove from Connecticut, after picking up my daughter from Fordham, and could not have been more pleased with this choice.  The food was incredible, the service was attentive, professional and our waiter's recommendations were fantastic.  This restaurant made our evening celebration the highlight of our last few months since Covid first appeared.  The innovative and delicious meals and dessert, along with the Covid restrictions which gave us plenty of space to dine, made this dinner one of the most enjoyable meals we have ever experienced in New York City.  I will rave about this restaurant to everyone I know.  This dinner inspired us to visit restaurants in New York City more often, but I doubt it will be easy to find one that compares to this.  We also appreciated the birthday candle elegantly displayed on the plate next to our dessert.

This is one of my and my husband's favorite restaurants anywhere, which is why it's hard to write this review. We were worried that this restaurant would not survive the pandemic and were relieved when we realized we could make reservations for in-door or outdoor dining. We made an early 6:45 dinner reservation, arrived 5-10 minutes early and were happy to see hygiene and safety pre-cautions were being observed and it was quite empty inside. We were told we were limited to 90 minutes at the table starting at the time of our reservation,  which we were fine with. What we were not fine with was our waiter who we had to prompt with our readiness to submit our orders, delivered our first round of drinks almost until we were through with our appetizers and who barely visited our table to check on us, and at 15 prior to our time limit ending being told by the manager that we could not receive the dessert we ordered due to their restrictions. I understood, but had to point out to the manager that there were two to three other tables who were seated well before we were that were still sitting at their tables. he checked and informed me one arrived early and were leaving and another I witnessed him remind them of 90 minute policy as well. Would that have happened had I not pointed this out? I understand we're living in a new time and have to observe new instructions so everyone remains safe and businesses continue to operate. I do not, however, like being made to feel like the rules only applied to us and having service staff that could have been more attentive so that we did not feel like were rushed to eat our meals within a short time limit because of timing and service inefficiencies, and one which was not inexpensive at that. Prior to being told this we discussed coming back once a month to support them because we do love their cuisine and cocktails, but after this, we're disappointed with this experience and will support other small businesses where we won't feel uncomfortable the few times we are venturing out to dine out at this time.
Food was great! I liked how they provided little bags for masks, we ate outside. Everything was well curated and very tasty! I especially liked the desert. Would come again!

Incredible, as always! This is our celebration restaurant which we typically visit a few times a year. Tonight was celebratory, we were meeting our neighbor's new girlfriend. The food was outstanding as was the service. 

I had written the restaurant a little note, while booking, of my food restrictions. Chef Vineet took the trouble to come out and ask me what I could/couldn't eat. The hostess said that she had tried to reach me to ask the same during the day but I had missed a call. 

Chef Vineet prepared my meal accordingly. It was delicious! I'm so grateful for his thoughtfulness.

We dined here on a Sunday during COVID. Service was exceptional but I think food could improve a bit. The Indian spice and flavor is def there but some of the dishes lacked in texture. We ordered the aloo chaat which was ok. Crab legs which was good. Tiger prawns, a very basic dish that could be made easily at home. Nothing amazing about it. 

For entree, sea bass and ghee lamb. Ghee lamb was good while it was hot but gave me acid reflux after since it's so heavy with oil.. but sea bass was good. 

Dessert ... malai makhani... although it was delicious the first few spoonful, it lacked texture and you can only have so many spoons of it. 

Drinks were good.
Excellent. I love this place!!! Wish they had some offerings off the tasting menu. My friend and I enjoyed their version of a Moscow Mule- it has rose petals in it and was super delicious.

There isn't enough good things I can say about this place- I've been a few times for dinner and I can say that that it consistently has some of the best food I've ever eaten in my life. Add onto that the incredibly friendly staff and it's one of my top recommendations for a date-night spot to my friends visiting Manhattan.

Great spot for a fancy modern Indian food! They are following all safety protocols for Covid. Outdoor dining is cute and you need to take reservations. 
I had always heard a lot about this place, and I must say it did live upto my expectations. Our server was sweet and the food was served fast and hot. 
They gave us pumpkin coconut soup to start with on the house, and it was one of the best soups ever! 
I have tried stuffed kulcha in other high end Indian restaurants in the city, but Indian accent tops it all. 
Their mushroom and the spinach kulcha are to drool for! 
I wasn't impressed by the pea kofta. It was fried and  dry. We loved their black daal! They serve it as a side, so we ended up ordering two of those.

Overall food and service of the waiters were good. The only huge setback was the manager (bald caucasian) stopping the waiters to serve our table of minorities (funny because its an ethnic restaurant)  because we didn't have our mask on WHILE seated. This did not happen to the other tables and observed the same manager serving others with no hesitation.

So ridiculously good... Every single plate was perfect! Even the dessert! I don't normally like anything sweet that doesn't have chocolate but MAN that was good. 100% recommend and will go back for more.

We went here for the Diwali dinner. I have had Manish Mehrotras cuisine back in Delhi and always wanted to visit this place in NYC, what better occasion than Diwali? Really loved the aesthetics of the place. Also Manish Mehrotra is known for chaat and the Indian fusion food. I particularly loved the Potato sphere chaat. The best items from everything we ordered was soy keema and  green kofta. The daal was perfect! The dash paneer kulcha or the garlic naan were okay and so was the best and paneer tikki. The winner of all was the dessert - makhan malai......a derivative of the famous Delgis Daulat ki chaat. The five star to this review is especially for the daal, koftas and this dessert which truly made our Diwali dinner perfect. I would love to thank the restaurant for the joy of discovering especially the  Daulat ki chaat dessert. Would love a more elaborate chaat menu though, hoping that happens soon! Also recommend the Chilli based cocktail and going by their servers recommendations which are very good. Also very polite staff and great service.

OK, blown away! We ate in India at the original Indian accent and this did not disappoint. It was off the chart. We asked for all the favs and it was really the bomb.

Even the drinks were good and the ribs were so good, that even after all we ordered, and we are a lot we had to get one more.

if you love Indian food, and we do - run don't walk to go there!

The food is ofcourse delicious. Everything that we have ordered was finger licking good. Over that the restaurant was super safe to dine in during the Covid times. The entire staff was wearing mask and keeping the safe distance. 
As you enter you fill a form with all your details so that they can contact you back for any reason. You would be asked to wear a mask every time a server come to your table. I really appreciate the safety and enjoyed our beautiful anniversary dinner.

This is the top restaurant that I hope survives the pandemic. The food is SO GOOD. The lamb entree especially. I've had so much on the menu. The soy keema is delectable as is all their chaats and cocktails.  Let's put it this way, I paid $70 round trip in Uber's so I could pick up a takeout meal from Indian accent once. Cravings. The take out was just as good as dining in. Do it. Give yourself a treat and order, especially right now, from Indian Accent.

A meal that spoke to my culture, roots and background... Growing up I was always around Indian and West Indian cuisine but it was always prepared and served in a old school homestyle sort of way. Truthfully told, I didn't love Indian food as a kid but I've come to grow fond of it and the countless possibilities and recipes that come with it. I love seeing restaurants such as this, spearheaded by Chef Manish Mehrotra, who have sought out to elevate Indian food into a fine dining experience rather than merely relying on the old world ways. Hopefully as time goes on society will become more accepting and receptive of this shift from old school to fine dining in regards to Indian cuisine. Here's a peek at the amazing offerings that Indian Accent NYC has: Sweet Pickled Ribs, Mathri Trio (Crispy Duck Curry, Foie Gras & Tamarind Cones), Vegetable Tart, Ghee Roasted Lamb with Roomali Roti, Khasta Roti with Goat Brains, Naan Bread, Makhan Malai Dessert (Cream Foam with Honey, Saffron, Almonds and Rose Petals), Meethe Chawal (Sweet Rice, Almond Milk and Barberries), Doba Barfi Treacle Tart with Vanilla Bean Ice Cream and  The Proper Copper (Kaffir Lime Leaf Infused Vodka and Honey Rose Blossom Water).

Amazing. Service, cocktails, food all outstanding. I hope they survive COVID. 

The complimentary blue cheese naan appetizer with pumpkin soup is a classy move and delicious.  The cocktails were phenomenal as well.  

We started with the dumplings, garlic butter crab claws, and sweet pickled ribs. Tender and so delicious! We would probably skip the dumplings next time. 

For mains we had a chicken curry dish and a spiced shredded lamb dish that came with a number of chutneys and bread for making little wraps almost like a taco. They were both so flavorful and delicious.  On the side we ordered garlic naan, and a flakey bread stuffed with butter chicken and another stuffed with saag paneer. 

Would come back again for sure. Wonderful experience.

My friend made a reservation here for our annual dinner where we eat Indian food. This restaurant has been on our list to eat for a long time and we finally came here in November. 
It was a pretty cold night, and Indian Accent did not have outdoor heaters at the time we dined. The staff were apologetic about the cold. 
Upon ordering, the staff presented us with a complimentary amuse bouche, a soup served in a shot glass. It was delicious. 
We also ordered an excellent appetizer which we shared. 
My friend had the ghee roast lamb with roti pancakes for a main, while I had the green pea kofta. The lamb was tender and flavoursome. The roti pancakes that it came with were soft and perfectly made. 
I also really enjoyed the green pea kofta. The peas were mashed and made into dumplings, and served in a coconut curry broth. I only wished that the serving had been a little larger. 
We also shared the makhan malai which the staff recommended as their most popular dessert. It was a giant ball of cream flavoured with spices. It was light and airy, and although I enjoyed it, I much prefer classic Indian desserts. 
We had no complaints whatsoever with our dining experience here, and I am looking forward to returning on another occasion.

I ordered takeout for my anniversary (celebrating with the place we ate on our wedding day). It lost some of the polish it would have had in-person. We ordered 14 items, 1 (yellow dal tadka) was missing and immediately refunded by Grubhub, 2 items were dessert. The bebinca Goan cake was not for me, it did not have a pleasant taste or texture at all. The doda barfi treacle tart was not bad, I enjoyed the milk cake bottom. As for the appetizers we had the papad and chutney sampler - solid. The others were sweet potato quinoa chaat (good, but a little too much quinoa, which tends to be dry) and corn and winter fenugreek (dry, wouldn't recommend). The entrees were pretty good - South Indian veg moilee, paneer butter masala, and Punjabi kadhi pakora. The black dairy dal was really weird, tasted entirely like tomato paste and not thoroughly cooked with all ingredients. The bhindi, raita, madras potatoes, and aloo gobhi were all very good. Overall, definitely a higher end for Indian food, but some decline with some items and getting takeout. I was also slightly disappointed that with our order of 14 items (about $150) we didn't receive a complimentary item (blue cheese naan or pumpkin soup) like others before me had posted about.

Having been a repeat customer (both in-person and takeout during the pandemic), this place deserves all 5 stars. Ordering was a great way to make my boyfriend's birthday special while no indoor dining options were available in NYC. 

My favorites remain largely the same: the butter kulcha, the ribs, lamb masala, butter chicken. 
The delivery/takeout menu is a bit different so a great opportunity to try something new.
Menu is reduced from before and so is the service. This used to be my favorite fine dine Indian restaurant but sad to see it's pathetic service and mediocre taste.

We were finally able to return to indoor dining at Indian Accent today and it was as amazing as ever.  Post covid they have done away with their tasting menu, hopefully temporarily, but their a la crate menu was astounding. The service was as attentive, prompt, abs courteous as always and they were extra cautious and took all the expected covid safety measures. For appetizers we had the smoked eggplant and the pickled ribs and both were highlights. The ribs in particular were the perfect combo of sweet and spicy and were cooked to perfection. For our entree we had the ghee roast lamb and desert we had the makhan malai, both of which were also very solid. Overall, I'd highly recommend Indian Accent. It's one of my favorites in NYC and can't wait for them to bring back their tasting and brunch menus

Indian Accent is a solid, higher end Indian food establishment in Midtown with a nice inside. Dined in a few years ago and I remember they also had tasty cocktails. 

This review is geared towards a more recent experience with delivery for dinner. Food came well packaged and food was warm and delicious. I had the Old Delhi butter chicken that came with basmati rice and laccha paratha.  Great flavors but without being too oily or leaving you feel bloated once the meal is over. Would eat here again.

Indian Accent has some of the best food I've ever eaten. Came by with a friend for a birthday dinner. The decor, hostess, bathroom, ambiance, service, COVID measures etc etc everything was great. The real star is the food. We ordered nearly everything on the menu: 

Food- 

Wild mushroom kulcha, truffle butter (bite sized and decadent)
Sweet potato shakarkandi, kohlrabi, crispy okra (very good, but you can pass on these) 
Beet and peanut butter tikki, goat cheese raita (even the most underwhelming of our four appetizers (this) was very good)
Sweet pickle ribs, sundried mango, onion seeds (these are a standout, so good!)
Crab claws, butter-pepper-garlic, cauliflower (absolutely delicious) 
Baked sea bass, patrani butter, barberry pulao (cooked to perfection) 
Ghee roast lamb, roomali roti pancakes (so flavorful. Portion sizes on yelp are misleading, this was a lot of food)
Doda barfi treacle tart, vanilla bean ice cream (AMAZING)
Pumpkin and coconut milk shorba with garam masala and blue cheese naan (so very good, the restaurant manager was kind enough to give me the recipe for the shorba) 

Drinks-

Mughal Fortification (very good) 
Green Chili Sour (good, but doesn't stand out next to others) 
Tiger House Punch (really good, kinda sweet) 
Smoke and Spice (smoky, spicy deliciousness) 

Everything we ate was divine and I cannot wait to go back. Our waitress, Amy, was also a sweetheart as was her trainee. Restaurant manager was also very kind and attentive. Great dinner. 10/10.

This is probably the best food I've ever had. The presentation and portion sizes are perfect, the flavor is PACKED into each bite and nothing overwhelms the senses to the point of standing out over the accompanying flavors. You can't go wrong here.

First time I've been to a restaurant and left saying the dessert was the best part of the meal after paying $250/person. Cocktails were well executed but the service was painfully slow and inattentive for having such few diners. 

The pepper chicken was good for a take out South Indian place but for $30 it should have been moist and succulent instead of dry. The chicken tasted like it may have been cooked in advance. Black daal was delicious and was a stand out dish. 

The mushroom kulcha and spinach kulcha were chewy and poorly executed. The ingredients would have had a harmonious marriage if it was executed properly. Butter chicken kulcha was tasty because it was the only dish that came out piping hot. 

The sticky ribs were delicious and were executed perfectly. At $11/rib eat them slowly and savor every bite. Chili pork phulka was an interesting idea but poorly executed and difficult to share. One bite size taco with a very chewy phulka. 

Crab claws were well done and full or flavor. South Indian flavors were spot on. 

Ghee roast lamb was a tiny dish at $40 and was flavorful but would have been just as good at any good Indian take out spot. The roti was cold and brittle. 

Beef tenderloin was good and cooked to a medium well although we were told it would be medium rare. This dish had enough flavor and the potato side was a nice compliment. 

The makan malai and the dosa bardo treacle were straight from the heavens and worthy of hitting this spot again. Absolutely sublime. Cocktails were also a hit.

The food and drinks at indian accent never disappoints but what makes the experience all the more lux is their impeccable service! Bradley was an absolutely amazing host. Its easy to fall in one of the two categories : either always be on your head (sorry sounds crude) or just being absent ! But he was just absolutely on point! 
The portions are really small but on hind side we can order and try  so many different things because of it. But I kind of missed the chef tasting menu.. 
INDIAN ACCENT IS A MUST GO !

I had a very disappointing Mother's Day  dinner . It was cold and wet and there was no heater for outdoor dinning ; apparently they text guests that it was going to be cold; but the rain was not something that planned for. Worst of all water was leaking from the roof while we were eating  - it was disgusting. Management was uncaring and did not give a damn about trying to accomodate the customers for indoor dining - despite the restaurant being more than half empty (I believe there were two large tables that remained empty from 6:00 pm to 7:30 pm and no where near other tables. 
This was the worst experience at a fine dining restaurant . I would not recommend to anyone under any circumstance.

A very good example of a BAD RESTAURANT!. I would leave zero stars if I could.  The food is mediocre for the price and to make it worse it is not even close to authentic.  Host ( Richard) at the front was rude and arrogant!  Come here if you want an attitude!

Lots of lists, lots of friends and lots of family recommended Indian Accent and became like one our must try places. Overall the experience was good. People raved about the 3 course menu but they are restarting that only end of May so we ended up trying the alacarte menu. 

Cocktails 
- Green Chilli Sour was not worth it. Watered down
- Mughal Mortification was a delicious and would order that again

Appetizers and Sides
Potato sphere Chaat - was outstanding 
Sweet pickle ribs - delicious and a must try
Butter chicken Kulcha - delicious
Black Dairy Dal - not recommended. Their take on dal makhani but too much tomato and not buttery enough


Main Dishes
Crispy jack fruit - very tasty
Ghee Roast Lamb - another not recommended option. My husband lived in mangalore for 5 years and the ghee roast is nothing close to being authentic. It has flavor but I would call it lamb roasted curry 

Dessert
Makkhan Malai - delicious and good for two 
Off menu chocolate old monk cake - delicious and very decadent 

It was a one time experience and we went for the chef. Tips:
- pricey
- small portions mostly 
- difficult to make reservations

I am in love and that's i have to say.but if you need more elaboration its the 
Appetizers- Potato spree chat, white pea mash
Main course--ghee roast lamb with roti pancakes
Deserts - Kheer , crispy seviyan, coconut jagery icecream
Makhan malai , safron milk, rose petal jaggerybrittle, almonds

Just order the above and thank me later.
Amazing service and even better cuisine . Best Indian on all of New York for sure the soy keema is my favorite.
exceptional food and service. felt so full and satisfied after the meal. great place for a date or celebrating an important milestone! 100% recommend
This is the one of the best food we had in NYC. Loved butter chucked naan, pepper chicken, paneer. Thought ghee roast lamb could have little more taste but it was nice.

I really loved the food  in all dimensions with respect to taste , quality and portion. This is a different approach to Indian cuisine and use of veggies. The tofu shistu, chicken tikka naan and finally dodha barfi were the top dishes I liked at this place

Truly a memorable meal.  I have had indian food many times, but never like they serve it at indian accents.  It is the food you think you know, prepared in a totally unique way.  My wife and I chose the 3 course with accompaniments.  The beet, peanut butter and goat cheese raita does not taste like its ingredients would suggest.  There a hints of the above, but the flavor is clean fresh and nicely balanced.  The chili pork phulka looks like a pulled pork taco, but it does not have that heavyness that pulled pork can have.  The texture is crispy, the finish is spicy, and it will leave you wanting for more.

Sweet pickle ribs were perfectly cooked, sweet and served with pickled vegetables.  It is as if an Indian chef married a girl from Nashville and moved to manhattan.  The Crab claws were plentiful, and spiced in a way you have never had before.

The pepper chicken was closer to standard indian fair, but more balanced.  The lamb roomali was superb.  Impossibly thin pancakes served with a choice of chutneys, and sublimely cooked lamb.  Be forewarned, it looks like a small serving but is very rich,  We had to finish the next day.  

Service and ambiance were also excellent, and perfectly complimented the great food.

PLEASE READ!!!

short story: THIS IS THE BEST INDIAN RESTAURANT IN THE WORLD (10/10 would recommend to a stranger)

l o n g  story: When you step inside Indian Accent, one of the first things you see is the decoration. The decoration is DEFINITELY next level! It looks pretty and very mind-friendly. The tables looked sparklingly clean and the servers were friendly and helpful. 

I arrived at the place early, so they offered us a table so we could wait for them to get ready to place orders. One thing I liked is that while we were waiting is that a server politely asked if we wanted water while we waited. We accepted and quickly got water and the glasses looked sanitary! 

When we placed the order, we got to know that THE FOOD COMES IN SMALL PORTIONS. 

Their food was EXTREMELY good, however my favorite foods on the menu were the Tawa Paneer (w/ rumali roti), the Butter Chicken Kulcha, and the Saag Paneer Kulcha. My favorite dessert was ABSOLUTELY the Doda Barfi. It was just perfect, like, you cannot change my mind. I am not joking, it was so good I fell asleep 

All in all, This is my favorite restaurant of all time. 10/10 would recommend to a stranger. One thing I REAAAALLLYY appreciate about Indian Accent is that it's not like your conventional Indian Restaurant that you could find anywhere. Their foods were very experimental, peculiar, and strong (IN A GOOD WAY!!!!!!!!!!). This restaurant is one of the prime reasons I like New York. 

Big props to the chefs btw. 

CONCLUSION: Eat here before you die
