One of my Indian friends recommended this place to me, saying it's his "favorite Indian restaurant in the world outside India" - I can see why.

All the starters were exquisite and flavor was carefully balanced. 

The complimentary pumpkin soup might have been my favorite of the meal. It comes in a little stone cup that keeps it warm, and it was deliciously (but not overly) creamy and spiced just right.

Other highlights: the assam pork dumplings were fragrant, the crab claws and chicken khulcha were satisfying (though the khulcha was on the tougher side), and the treacle tart was very decadent. Would definitely come back.

Pro tip: make your reservation for outdoors so you don't have to get the prix fixe. I would skip the entrees (nothing special) and order a bunch of everything else!
Love this place their dodha barfi was the show stopper  definitely making a visit very soon for another extensive review

Disclaimer- I did not actually eat here. But I did have an undesirable experience attempting to. 

It was a hot and rainy Wednesday night. I had looked at reservations that afternoon but all they had was a 5:30. Based on a review I read it seemed like a pretty big place so we thought we would just try to walk in knowing the risk. This review is not because they couldn't seat us but with how the host spoke to me. The woman called me sweetheart or hunny in a very condescending way more than once and made some comment about how "you should always get reservations when in New York". It was weird and patronizing. I live here and it was a Wednesday night. All you need to say in that situation was sorry we are completely booked and not taking walk ins tonight. Just rubbed me the wrong way, don't call strangers sweetheart.
AMAZING FOOD!!! Go here for your anniversary, birthday, graduation, etc. because it's pricey but amazing. Try the ribs and any of the desserts
Very Good Indian restaurant in NYC. Smell very good inside feel like you not in Indian restaurant and all foods We are order is excellent For sure we will go  back there again.

WOW! This place lives up to the hype. 

Came here for dinner on Tuesday, and reservations (apparently) are not easy to come by. 

Food (5/5): The food was excellent and ranks in my top picks for Indian food in NYC. My girlfriend and I picked the 3 course menu and it was PLENTY to keep us full. I disagree with other reviews claiming the portions are small... I found it to be more than enough and left feeling a bit too full. Here is what we got in order of how tasty it was:
Tandoori Salmon: Cooked perfectly and beautifully spiced. Peas were a nice touch
Chicken: Spicy! and delicious. Came with green beans which were a nice accompaniment 
Soy Keema: very flavorful and comes in a cute clay pot. Was spicy
Desserts were also amazing. We got the malai and the doda which were both delicious. The doda especially! It had a great scoop of vanilla ice cream on top

Service (5/5): The wait staff and host are trained wonderfully. They were incredibly attentive and helpful. Sometime during the meal we realized we couldn't complete our 4-courses (which we ordered initially) and asked if we could switch to 3. They were more than willing to help and were able to make the switch, no fuss about it. I've been to Michelin star restaurants with service much worse than this. 

Ambiance (5/5): What can i say, it's a beautiful interior with various sections to dine. I love the subtle decor and the clean vibes. Great if you're looking for an upscale, but not stuffy, place for a date 

Overall, I would highly recommend this place and I will be back to try the rest of the menu :)

Giving 1 star because couldn't give 0!

Had a birthday in the group. They only just got a candle for us.
No special cocktails. The ones we ordered were especially bad.
Makhan malai dessert - it's just whipped cream!
Mains course ghee roast dosa - no taste at all

Daal was ok. Probably the only thing worth eating.
Service soooo sooooo bad!!

If  you're anything like me - you won't be exactly sure what you're ordering, but you're hoping it's good once it hits the table. 

Have no fear, they are all eater friendly for those who may be fearful of the exotic. The options pulled from traditional Indian dishes with a modern (and western) twist - so I assure your taste buds will be pleased. More so, the servers were very educated on the menu. So do not be afraid to ask for pairings and recommendations.

Damn good. Can't wait to return

Two choices 3 or 4 course. The balance of flavors is just amazing from a simple potato chili to prawns koliwada.

My husband and I made reservations here for 5:30 on a Sunday night, right when they open, thinking it would be an empty restaurant, but right after we were seated, the people came pouring in!! By 6 pm, the place was moderately filled, which I guess is a testament to how absolutely phenomenal the food is. 
We both did the four course option, which came with an accompaniment, and a soft cocktail each.
For the first course, my husband had the Sweet Potato Shakarkandi, and I had the potato sphere chaat. Absolutely. Mind. Blown. I can't say enough about how amazing the textures and flavours were!!!! And the portion sizes were just right! 
Second course, my husband had the soy keema (and they were kind enough to cook the quail egg further than runny because I was pregnant, bonus points for thoughtfulness!! And I had the tofu masala. Admittedly, I had it in my head that the tofu masala wouldn't be as delish bc it's something I've made at home so much, but nope, this one just blew my mind!!!!!
Third/main course, my husband had the pepper chicken, and I had the prawn koliwada, SO GOOD, but honestly we were stuffed by the time the third course came!
Dessert was also really really good but I feel like bc of how stuffed we were we didn't get to enjoy it properly, BUT at no point did the waiters rush us, we were there for 2+ hours and honestly had such a wonderful date night. 
12/10 for food, ambience, and service and would come back again post baby, and I am already so excited!!!

I rank the food 5/5, and the service a 4.5/5. Every dish was well balanced and complete. We  experienced unique flavors and left wanting satisfied yet wanting more. I would 100% return again and again in the future. The price point was accurate for the quality of service and food. If you had any thoughts of making a reservation here, I would just go ahead and book it.

Fabulously inventive menu, great execution, wonderful wine list. This isn't a traditional Indian restaurant. It's an elevated, boutique experience. 

We well be back.
A different take on traditional Indian dishes. Really enjoyed it. We had the 4 course tasting menu. More than enough food. Actually could of done the 3 course. . Great desserts too!

What a great place to have Indian fusion food. Definitely one of the best fine dining Indian restaurant in the City.
We went with 3 course meal and still ended up taking the leftover food.

Complimentary - They started with complimentary pumpkin coconut soup and cheese ball. This soup was just out of the world! We really wanted to ask for one more serving, but we were shy ;)

Appetizer - Who would have imagined red potato chaat would taste sooooo good! Also their tofu shishito pepper was great and filling.

Main course - Loved crispy jackfruit in kerala style curry. Soy boti dish was OK - though loved it's presentation.

Sides - One of the best dal makhani we ever had! Even their stuffed kulchas were great.

Dessert - Makhan malai was amazing! Yes it is like whipped cream, but definitely worth having it. We didn't like meethe chawal at all - the only reason to take off one star - it was a weird combination.

Good food at a price. The tasting menu is pretty good. The Assamese Pork dumpling was very tasty. The crab claws were well made, but difficult to eat, esp. in the setting. 3 chili potatoes was basically fillings from a masala dosa.
The lamb ghee roast was exquisite - Kosha Mangsho, for those of you know what it is. The appetizers, chutneys, accompaniments were all full of intense flavors.
Overall a fine dinning experience for an occasion.

Made a reservation for late Friday night as a post-Diwali celebration with some friends who had come to town. We were seated promptly and our servers were all extremely nice. We took our time ordering our four courses, but never felt rushed despite the lateness of our meal. We were given a pumpkin soup amuse bouche, which was absolutely delicious, and we hope a larger version is one day available on the menu. For drinks, we ordered the proper copper which was delicious, and the Mughal fortification, among others that were more forgettable.

For appetizers, we ordered the beet and peanut butter tikki, the potato sphere chaat and the Assamese pork dumplings. Of these, the Assamese pork dumplings were far and away the favorite of our table. 

For mid courses we ordered the soy kheema, smoked eggplant bharta cornet, tofu masala, sweet pickle ribs, and crab claws. All of these were delicious but again a clear favorite emerged with the sweet pickle ribs.

For the main course, we ordered the beef tenderloin which was spicy and melted in our mouths. The sides accompanying the meat, which included some sort of sweet biscuit and potatoes was surprisingly bland but the beef made up for it. We also ordered the ghee roast lamb with Rumali roti which was honestly a little bit more gimmicky than flavorful. Finally we also ordered the paper dosa which was decent. For accompaniments we had the black dairy dal with naan and the asparagus poriyal, both of which were delicious.

For desserts we had the makhan malai, doda barfi treacle tart and the meethe chawal. As with previous courses, one order was a clear favorite which was the makhan malai.

Overall a great meal but definitely some dishes were more worth the price than others.

Indian Accent just became my favorite Indian food experience in America. The food was 10/10; it was all so flavorful and unique, there wasn't one thing that I wouldn't want to eat again. I especially enjoyed the crab claws appetizer and the prawn entree. 

What sets this place apart, however, is the phenomenal service. If you get a chance, be sure to have dinner at the bar, as James the bartender is beyond knowledgeable and hospitable. Another bright spot was Suresh, who really went above and beyond to make this experience incredible. Everyone was so friendly and welcoming and I already can't wait to go back.

Made a reservation for two people on a Wednesday night without any problem. Despite being filled inside we didn't feel the place was crowded, being seated and served menus immediately.

Decided on the pre fixe menu, which included w choice of three items ($80):
Beef Tenderloin - beautifully cooked, moist.interior and  savory sauce on top
Smoked Eggplant - sweet roasted flavor in a hearty cone
Beer & PB Tikki - rich pb sauce over a hearty veggie disk. Another delicious bite.

Honestly no qualms at all - good service, wonderful.wine list, amazing food. Assuredly expensive but worth the visit at least once.

I have been to many Indian restaurants in the city, but I have to say that for upscale Indian food this is the best the city has to offer. From the drinks, food, service and ambiance, I would give them all 5/5.

I came here for my birthday last night with my girlfriend. The first thing I noticed as soon as I walked in through the door is the decor. It was very chic and modern. Since my date was running a bit late I had a Macallan neat by the bar. This is when I noticed that the staff was excellent. The bartender was very nice and engaged me in a nice conversation about pocket squares. That really started my night off well due to his friendliness.

When my girlfriend finally arrived, we got a excellent table for two towards the back right corner. It was very well lit and had the pleasure of being served by Madak (please excuse my spelling). He was very nice and gave us great recommendations as it came tot the tasting menu. His service was definitely a 5/5. I ordered a dirty martini to start while my girlfriend had the proper copper. My drink was tasty as always and my girlfriend thoroughly enjoyed her drink. Overall another 5/5.

Before we ordered they served us a pumpkin soup and a mini stuffed naan with cheese which was delicious. It was a great way to get our appetites up and was really tasty (5/5). My girlfriend and I both did the four course tasting menu. I had the potato sphere chaat, white pea mash for the appetizer and it was absolutely delicious (5/5). My girlfriend had the beet and peanut butter tikki, goat cheese raita which was even better than mine (6/5) if that was even possible. For our midcourse, I had the tofu masala, shishito peppers (4.5/5) and my girlfriend got the smoked eggplant bharta cornet, goat cheese mousse which was even bette than mine again (5/5).  For the main course I got the paper roast dosa, wild mushrooms, water chestnuts, gunpowder (4.5/5) with the accompaniments of saag paneer kulcha, chilli butter (5/5). The kulcha was absolutely delicious, but my girlfriend's main course once again outshined mine. She got the crispy jackfruit, cauliflower rice, kerala pumpkin curry, which was amazing (5/5), with the black dairy dal with naan (5/5). 

When it came to our final dessert course, I had the doda barfi treacle tart, vanilla bean ice cream which was excellent once again (5/5). My girlfriend had the
kheer, crispy seviyan, coconut and jaggery ice cream (4.5/5). For once I thought my dish was better. I finished it off with a espresso and sambuca which I believe the manager brought over and I had nice chat with.

Overall a (5/5). This restaurant takes Indian dishes and adds a flair and uniqueness to it. I have had a lot of Indian food and some of these flavors I have never had in my life. I highly recommend it that you give it a try.

When it comes to Saturday evening, it should be happening and foodilicious. This upscale Indian restaurant in Manhattan has the all the flavors you want to try. Perfect ambience, good food and excellent cocktails. The bartenders know what you want to drink and make the perfect cocktails. Food menu was limited but whatever you order is perfectly cooked and delicious. Hospitality is amazing and friendly. Thank you for that. Looking forward to visit again soon.

Food was amazing, the ambience was to the point! We visited with our friends and got a table reserved for 6. We had a great time! The servers were polite and walked each of us through every dish served. 
The coconut pumpkin shorba was absolutely yum! My absolute favorite was the "Makhan malai" - I've never had it in India but I'm sure it doesn't get better. 

We will definitely get back once the tasting menu changes.
OMG $$ but so good! Flavors feel like home. Upscale/fine dining. Nice spot for date night

This was such an incredible culinary experience. We love Indian food, and this restaurant blew us away with the ambiance, service, and most importantly cuisine. It's a 3 or 4 course meal per person, so we elected to go with the 3 courses each. We thought we would walk away hungry, however that was not the case although portions deceivingly appear smaller. The dessert makkan malai was the clear cut winner. If we could order that to go we could come back frequently for it.

To start off, the aesthetic of the food & setting of Indian Accent is phenomenal. Each dish was actually beautifully presented + this is a solid fine dining establishment. The restaurant requires you to do the 3/4 course tasting menu, which allowed us to try a few different things on the menu and see the varied presentation. However, when it comes to the actual quality of the food, the restaurant feels lacking. The starter deconstructed samosa I ordered was just so average - while it looked pretty, nothing super interesting food-wise (just smothered in sauce). The Soy Keema was a small portion for a mid-course and nothing too much to note. The Butter Pao alongside were cute, but pretty small + flavorless. The Crispy Jackfruit main was the star of the meal (with their kulchas as an accompaniment, which were great). I didn't actually remember that it was made of jackfruit because that flavor was so subtle, which I can appreciate. My biggest gripe with Indian Accent is that, while their food is solid & presentation is quite good, it did not feel worth the $80 for the tasting menu. With so many other Indian restaurants in the city that are more affordable and taste much better, I would avoid coming here again.

Indian Accent is the pinnacle of Indian restaurants.  I've tried Indian food in different restaurants in the world and none of them would compare to Indian Accent.  
The restaurant has a tasting menu and it's on the pricier side but it's definitely worth.  
  We came here and ordered 2 six entree course meals, everything we ordered was delicious.  Their presentation of the food was amazing too.  However don't leave this place without having the Makhan Malai dessert.  This is an absolute MUST.
Not a good restaurant. They'll try to overcharge you if they think you're an out of towner otherwise food is average nothing special.

This place gets one star from me. An incredibly bland, supremely underwhelming meal. The only Indian accents in this restaurant are the Indian accents of some of the customers. I feel sorry for the crab that lost its life for my overpriced meal. It was an unforgettable experience, in that I will never forget how disappointed I was. One star for the ambience, do not come here, the bodega next door will have better Indian food for 1/10 of the price.

This is one of the best Indian restaurant in New York serving outstanding food and great service.

I definitely recommend doing prior reservations. They have prix fixe menu which offers 3 or 4 course meal with one accompaniment 

Ambience: This restaurant has warm and cozy vibe.

They welcome you with pumpkin soup and cheese naan. The soup is so great and hearty. Loved it. It definitely sets the palate for the further courses. 

Drinks: opted for soft cocktail named mudra punch . It's rose sharbat with almond milk and coconut . It's absolutely superb. Extremely refreshing. 

Appetizer: I opted forward beet peanut  tikki . It was appetizing and beautifully plated.

Mains: opted for prawns koliwada. It was one best prawn koliwada I have ever had outside Mumbai. 
 It's spicy , tangy and so flavorful. Fried shrimps taste really delicious.

Accompaniment: butter chicken kulcha is delicious and such a unique dish. Liked it a lot.

Dessert: Makhan Malai is just outstanding. I strongly recommend it. Don't miss it. It's creamy but light , not too sweet. It's  beautiful presented with almonds and rose petals.

Before we get to my commentary on the food (arguably the most important element), I'll first discuss the other facets of our experience (all positive) - service level and attention to detail, lack of noise, comfort level and drinks.

Service level and attention to detail 
Service was rather expeditious. Our table was ready as soon as we arrived. Waiters were attentive, i.e. filling water quickly and asking how our meal was every 10-15 minutes. Food was brought out at a relatively quick rate and the presentation of food was phenomenal. Though admittedly, at a fine dining establishment of this caliber, this level of impeccable service is expected.

Noise level and crowd
Tables were well spaced out. Noise/background chatter was minimal. On par with Junoon/Tamarind and quite a contrast from the newly opened Sona (see my review on Sona). Crowd was chic and everyone was relatively well dressed.

Chairs and table
Very comfortable. At many restaurants, unless you have a booth, the seating comfort level is questionable (again, see my review of Sona) but at Indian Accent the chairs were plush and roomy. Our table for two was also relatively large, a huge plus when you have multiple drinks and several dishes simultaneously on the table.

Drinks
My wife just had a coke but I had the Mughal Fortification and Smoke and Spice. The Mughal is a bit sweet, but if you are a fan of peaty whiskeys (Ardbeg, Laphroaig, etc.) like me, the Smoke and Spice is phenomenal. Def recommended. 

Now on to the primary attraction of the evening. 

Food
First, you have to choose from either the 3 or 4 course menu. However, unlike many restaurants where you can't deviate away from ordering one item per category, here you can mix and match. This flexibility is great. Between my wife and me, we ordered one 3-course and one 4-course, and chose to forego dessert (neither one of us is a huge fan of ordering desserts at restaurants - we prefer to eat ice cream or cookies at home) in favor of additional main courses. Note that you also get one accompaniment per person.

What we ordered
Appetizers - sphere chaat and pork dumplings.
Mid-courses - sweet pickle ribs and crab claws.
Entrees - pepper chicken, prawn koliwada and ghee roast lamb.
Accompaniments - saag paneer kulcha and butter chicken kulcha.

Amuse-Bouche - pumpkin coconut soup served with a mini cheese naan. The soup was out of this world. Hot and spicy. Absolute heaven. Granted, a small shot-glass sized portion. Wish I could order as an appetizer.

Sphere chaat - small portion yet delicious. We both enjoy chaat in general and this dish did not disappoint.

Pork dumplings - my wife wanted this and loved it. I found the broth to be fantastic but something about the dumplings (think it was cardamom?) turned me off.

Ribs - flavorful, moist and falls right off the bone. Melts in your mouth. Def recommended.

Crab claws - my wife isn't a huge seafood fan like me, but I loved them. As often is the case with ordering crab at a non-seafood fine dining establishment, you don't get a ton of meat, but the little meat provided within the 4 small claws was delicious. As a cauliflower fan, I found the reasonable amount of well seasoned cauliflower in the dish to be a great touch.

Pepper chicken - well seasoned and very spicy. Personally, I loved it though my wife did not. If you are a huge black pepper fan like me, this dish is a win. However, if you are opposed to a heavy dose of black pepper, avoid at all costs. To each their own :) 

Prawn koliwada - the shrimp was beyond delicious. However, the pulao (rice) was just ok. Def recommended if you are a huge shrimp fan like me. Only questionable element pertains to the fact that there was a giant heap of caviar/fish eggs on top of the prawns. If you love caviar, fantastic. However, if you don't, could be a major drawback, granted you can easily push aside the caviar.

Lamb - the shining star of the evening. I saved the best for last. This dish comes with several roti pancakes and a few chutneys. The shredded lamb is rich, flavorful, tender and spicy. Essentially, the idea is to create mini tacos/fajitas with each roti. A must have!

Kulchas - the saag paneer kulcha was decent but the butter chicken kulcha was fantastic. More filling than your standard kulcha but well worth it.

The amount of food we ordered was beyond substantive and filling. We def didn't finish everything, but that's primarily because (as always) we ordered too much!

Overall, a memorable experience. Highly recommended.

Modern Indian deliciousness.

*Blue Cheese Nann comp- simply could be my favorite just because I love blue cheese!

*Pork Dumpling- ordered because all the hooray on Yelp. Unsure what's the hype about it. Felt like regular dumpling with more perfume scent within.

*Potato Chaat- pretty good.

*Tofu Masala- little slimy and more of sweet and sourt Thai sauce in my opinion. Not bad.

*Pickled Rib- very delicious but doesn't feel Indian.

*Pepper Chicken- delish and love the coconut sauce.

*Lamb- pretty good but wasn't sure if the 4 sauce came with it were really thought out.

*Mushroom Truffle Kulcha- pretty good and prob needed the carb to fill a bit.

*Butter Chicken Kulcha- yummy too but had this pita feeling.

*Makhan Malai- first time trying this, like Indian cream. Tried to enjoy it.

Overall was quite nice experience.!

Indian Accent is one of my favorite Indian places to come to in the city. While it's definitely expensive (arguably overpriced), if you're less price conscious and just looking for good and interesting Indian food this is a great option. My major gripe is the menu doesn't really change over time so there's not a lot of value in coming back

**Unless you have a very large appetite the 3 course option should satisfy you.

Food 5/5: Indian accent is a fairly unique restaurant in that they take what's usually homey and traditional (Indian food) and add interesting almost shocking flavors (good example is the blue cheese naan they give in the beginning). Some of their dishes are genuinely wonderful and all of them stand up well. I'd make it a point to get the tikkis, the mushroom kulcha, the dal, and the saag main.

Service and ambience 4/5: Service is prompt and attentive but at this level, nothing particularly special. The restaurant is spacious and comfy.

In simple words Amazing. I'm always apprehensive to have Indian food at a restaurant, lest I get disappointed. Everything here was delicious.
I did the 3 course meal
Drinks:
Smoke and spice
Green chilli sour
Appetizer: pork dumplings
Mid course: ribs
Mains: ghee roast lamb
Accompaniment: wild mushroom kulcha

The quantities were deceptively large and I could barely walk at the end of the meal. The ghee roast was out of this world and the chutneys were simply amazing. This is definitely a place I'm coming many more times

I was in London in 2018 and really wanted to try this place, but we had to cancel our reservations due to the Tube being shutdown and our American phones not being able to hail a Lyft or Uber.  So, I was ecstatic to be able to rectify this at their NYC location.

This place has all of the trappings of a high end restaurant:  great service, creative and well crafted cocktail program, attention to detail.   Our server was great, explained how their menu worked and offered some suggestions.   Everything we had here was a creative take on Indian cuisine that really challenged our notions of what Indian food can be.  Cocktails were well balanced.   The wine list was well suited.   Great selection of teas.   The highlight of the meal was the pickled ribs which where perfectly seasoned and more tender than the kisses of a puppy.   Plus the flow of the meal was so well timed.   We had 4 courses and everything came out like clockwork: not too fast and not too slow.   I believe we were out of there in about 90 minutes and we were not rushed.   Great service execution.

All in all, the great service and great food will have me coming back for more.   Definitely recommend.

We've been regulars here since Indian Accent opened up in New York. Consistently a good experience. the food remains top notch! I sorely miss the paneer w/ roomali roti main and their delivery service but the shakarkandi chaat, ghee roast and dodha barfi will keep bringing me back.

The service is always pleasant, with servers who know the dishes inside out. 

Highly recommend!

Fantastic food! From the moment you walk in, you are treated with excellence. The ambiance is impeccable and the service is superb. We got the 4 course meal and each dish we got was excellent. A great mix of rich Indian flavors and creative presentation. The cocktails are also uniquely made. I will definitely be back again! 

-Sweet Potato Shakarkandi, Kohlrabi, Crispy Okra
-Tofu Masala, Shishito Peppers
-Soy Keema, Quail Egg, Lime Leaf Pao
-jackfruit Phulka 
-Pepper Chicken, Kerala Vegetable Stew
-paper roast dosa, wild mushrooms, water chestnuts, gunpowder
-butter chicken kulcha, sundried fenugreek
-makhan malai, saffron milk, rose petal jaggery brittle, almonds
-doda barfi treacle tart, vanilla bean ice cream

Amazing modern Indian food! They take traditional Indian food and make it very unique in presentation and flavor. From the moment you walk  in the ambiance is great. The service is phenomenal. It's expensive, but it's a great place to come to celebrate special occasions. I highly recommend this restaurant.
Worth the experience once for a special occasion! With so many Indian restaurants in NYC it can sometimes be hard to stand out but through some innovative dishes - Indian Accent does!

One word - WOW! 
We came here for my birthday and had a wonderful experience. Indian accent offers a pre fixe menu from which you can choose a 3 course or 4 course. I went with the 4 course and my husband chose the 3 course so we can share the dessert.
For the appetizers we got the potato sphere chat and Assamese pork dumplings and both were great.
For the mid course we got the crab claws and sweet pickle ribs and both were equally good.
For the mains we got the prawn koliwada and lamb ghee roast, the lamb ghee roast was the clear winner and totally worth the additional 10$. If needed they will always switch the Romali roti with a gluten free sub.
For the accompaniments we got the butter chicken kulcha and three chilli potato, the kulcha was the clear winner again.
For dessert we got the Makhan malai and that was such a treat to wrap up the meal.
Overall for the price range it was such a treat.. they treat you like royalty and the food matches the service.
Innovative approach to Indian food . Everything was exceptional. Food, drinks and service.
Best Indian food in midtown. No question. The flavors in every dish are brilliant. It is expensive but worth it!

Unfortunately not impressed and I'm surprised by my mediocre experience after reading these 5 star reviews.

Service: the man who took our order seemed as if we were inconveniencing him with every question. It was 8:00, so not even close to closing time. Once we ordered, food arrived at a painfully slow pace, making our total meal 3 hours long.

Food: chewy stale naan, bland courses. Best part was the dessert (makhan malai!) we were very impressed with it!

Ambiance: nice classy decor makes you feel like you're at an elite restaurant.

Overall, seems overhyped and the service left much to be desired.

Absolutely amazing dinner and service! We made a 9PM reservation and was one of the last tables of the night, but our waiters were so kind and attentive, treating us as though we were one of the first. 

And of course, the food! The food was on par with the service and we thoroughly enjoyed everything we ordered. The menu is creative and flavorful. I found myself surprised (in the best way!) at how innovative each dish was and how the different spices combined together. 

We ordered quite a bit because we wanted to try as many thing as possible, so we went with more of the small dishes and appetizers: 
- sweet potato shakarkandi
- assamese pork dumplings
- tofu masala
- sweet pickle ribs
- prawns
- tandoori salmon
- butter chicken kulcha
- garlic naan
- three chilli potato
- kheer

If you love Indian food, you'll definitely enjoy dining here - and if you don't love Indian food, I would highly recommend that you give Indian Accent a try because it might just change your mind.

A few hits and misses, overall good experience, but not worth the price tag. 

We stopped by since our hotel was the adjacent Thompson, made a reservation a few weeks in advance. Seated promptly. Clean, modern interior. The staff was solid and attentive all night, but nothing remarkable. 

I enjoyed my Proper Copper cocktail, as I'm a big fan of mules. We each got the 4 course meal, with differing dishes to sample as many plates as possible. The sweet pickle ribs were good, perhaps the standout. The worst thing I had was the fried prawn main dish, as the curry just tasted bland. Seasoned but not tasty if that makes sense. Most other things fell somewhere in between. Spice level is moderate for most dishes, it never got a point of pain. Even the desserts were just OK. 

Coming in at $125 per person after everything, I expected much better. You can see why they're on the Michelin guide, but do not have a star designation. I'd rather go to more casual Indian places that are bursting with flavor without busting the budget.

Food is amazing and service is amazing. This may be my favorite restaurant of all time. I would say it is worth the price - I am a vegetarian.

It feels like a world class experience which is one of the reasons why I adore dining with Indian Accent.

I was here a good long while back with two others, long enough that I don't remember what everyone else had. My photos appear from October 2021 and I presume it was from around then but it could be earlier. The food here is pricey but good. We had the 3 course option which comes with one side dish. For a drink, I went with the Mudra Punch which consisted of, Rose Sharbat , Almond Milk, and Toasted Coconut. This was alright. A bit unbalanced and small for the ingredients list but fine.

The amuse bouche consisted of pumpkin and coconut shorba as well as a blue cheese naan. The pumpkin and coconut shorba was fantastic. Not overly sweet and I would have loved a large portion of this as my appetizer. The blue cheese naan had very strong cheese flavor as expected. A bit unbalanced but it helped with the palate.

My appetizer was the sweet pickled pork ribs with sun-dried mango and onion seeds. It felt odd ordering pork in an Indian spot but it appeared to be the popular appetizer here. This was excellent though it didn't exactly remind me much of Indian food. Perhaps a more sour mango chutney on the side would help with the sweetness or something. Still very good. Another person had the crab claws which were quite tasty and I believe the last person had the chaat which I don't remember trying. 

My main course was the fried soft shell crab Koliwada with Malvani dried shrimp pulao. The crab had a nice light fry and the portion size was adequate. There was a bit of caviar on top for extra flavor and crunch. The dried shrimp pulao, or sode bhaat, had a strong fishy flavor and overall the dish had a strong fish flabor but this was all to be expected with the dish. I would recommend it. Another person had the ghee roast lamb which was a $10 supplement and this was the other strongest dish. Very tasty roti with it. Another person I believe had the chicken.

I believe the accompaniments were the butter chicken kulcha with sundried fenugreek, the black dairy dal with naan, and the saag paneer. The best of the three by a mile was the dal. Very well flavored with an excellent garlic naan. The kulcha I remember being alright and the latter was perfectly fine.

For dessert, we split all of them. The Makhan Malai consisting of saffron milk, rose petal jaggery brittle, and almonds, had a big presentation but it was lighter flavor than I expected. It was good but I would prefer a stronger rose flavor. The doda barfi treacle tart was a bit hard to cut through but the flavors were nice and  much stronger. The dessert made sense being that their original location is in Britain and it was a fun spin on the usual treacle tart. The kheer with crispy seviyan and coconut/jaggery ice cream topped with fresh fruit. was fine but the weakest of the three. The crispy seviyan was essentially like having fried filo dough like in Turkish spots and it was a fun spin but not as well flavored.

Overall the food is good here. The flavors were a mix of alright to excellent. I'm unsure if it was super worth it for the price but a couple dishes in particular were excellent even if some of them were not particularly Indian in terms of flavors. Good spot. Low 4.

Went here for the first time and was the worst restaurant experience. I am Indian and I know what is good and bad. This restaurant gave me heart burn and bad stomach issues. In one hour and 30 min we only got two  appetizers. And for the main entrance we had to pack it up and take it home bc our car lot where we parked the car was going to close . Food was horrible quality.

The food was divine and the service was great.  They were able to seat me a few minutes early, but also accommodate us needing to start 15 minutes late.  They started us off with a pumpkin curry and blue cheese naan amuse bouche.  I really liked how the curry felt on my palate, and that everything was in balance considering we were intended to drink it.  I had the Assamese pork dumplings for my appetizer.  It was a flavorful, savory, and slightly floral dish, that had some similarities to soup dumplings. (but the broth was outside of the dumplings, and flavored differently)  I liked the crunch from the crispy black rice.  Then I had the bharta cornet, which was crispy with a clean, flavorful kick.  I was thinking about how the eggplant texture wasn't discernible to me, maybe because it was chopped into small pieces, but that makes a lot of sense with the goat cheese mousse and the crispy exterior.  Then I had the prawns koliwada, which was nice.  I liked how the cumin came through in the sauce, and the prawns were very crispy, the rice fluffy and aromatic.  The root vegetable saag tart was a great refreshing dish.  My last dish of the night that I ordered was the beef tenderloin dish with the black dairy dal accompaniment.  Here, it was a bit heavy on the starches for me, but I knew what I ordered, and probably should have planned this better.  I ended up not finishing 1 piece of naan bread, but it all tasted very nice and my beef was cooked perfectly.  In the potato and fenugreek cheela, I wonder if I missed the fenugreek because I thought it was spinach.

Then, I forgot that I let them know it was my birthday, and was surprised when they brought out a complimentary birthday dessert!  It took me a second to remember how they knew, and then I remembered the reservation.  That was so thoughtful.  Especially because I mentioned I was considering dessert at the beginning of the meal, but asked which dessert was the least sweet due to needing to regulate sugar levels.  That waiter suggested the makhan malai, which was exactly the dessert they brought out after the meal with a candle and some 24 carat gold flakes.  I had such a wonderful time, and the food was exquisite.

TLDR: Go for the ambience and elevated fare but not for authentic Indian cuisine 

Every dish was beautifully presented and well crafted. Its a properly portioned tasting menu and brings the fine dining aspect to indian food. However, I found some of the items to be on the blander side and found the pairings to be a bit odd. The peanut butter was tasty but didn't mesh with the rest of the bite. The eggplant was under-seasoned and felt more like a lasagna filling. The saving grace however was the lamb main dish and the dessert. The lamb was perfectly cooked and the accompanying kulcha was packed with flavor. The dessert was definitely the most unique and tasty thing they had- it had the lightness of a merengue with the flavor of rose lassi. 

I really struggled between giving this a 3 or 4 star but ultimately decided on a 3 star given the price point of the restaurant.

I may visited this restaurant with high expectations. 

good stuff 
1. food presentation was excellent
2. service is excellent
3. nice clean, decor of the restaurant

stuff that I did not like
1. the food I ate almost was not an Indian food
2. the portions were small and Emil handed for presentation. 
3. not a great food selection
4. expensive and not worth the value 
5. Good descriptions were very bad 

friends kept talking about experience so visited. but would not recommend

PSA: I'm 100% Indian and grew up eating the best home-cooked food so I'm very critical when it comes to Indian food lol. This place was an 1000/10. Every single dish was very unique and tasted amazing. The flavors were all on point and the portions were perfect. There's not a lot of creative Indian food out there & I'm super happy to have finally gotten the chance to eat here. Can't wait to visit again!!

Everything was Excellent from food to service , everything...
I had a great server couldn't remember the name but two african american girls one of them was a back waiter . They were top notch wiping my table after every course, water refilling without me pouring by myself.
Just remember you cannot order a la carte but its 3-4 course menu but you have a great choices even if you are vegetarian or nv person.

Food came out on time, din't have to wait too long neither for drinks !
Amazing creativity on the food, very impressive !!

Very nice experience. I was looking for an elevated Indian restaurant for my husbands bday and this totally fit the bill. Food and service was excellent! Definitely recommend. It's something different from the usual tasting menu experience.

This place is my favorite restaurant in NYC. While it is expensive, it is totally worth it! Their portion sizes are decent for this type of restaurant. I highly recommend splurging and going with the four-course meal. Regardless of what items you pick for this meal, you can't go wrong. My favorites include the pumpkin soup, the beet and peanut butter tikki, the tofu masala, the chicken malai tikka, and the butter chicken kulcha.
Amazing and knowledgeable service. Jaquy was an excellent host. All of the food was incredible and a great value.

We went to this restaurant with our baby and took an Uber there and it was over $40. We were very hungry and want to new  Indian restaurant. So we get out of our Uber and go to the door to try to open it to get in the restaurant and it's locked. We're a little confused because we looked up the restaurant online and looked at all the yelp reviews and it said it was open. Then a lady comes out and says you're not allowed to eat here. And I'm like excuse me what do you mean. And she said kids under 10 are not allowed to come inside the restaurant. And I was very upset we're starving we just ordered up expensive Uber just to come to this restaurant and she doesn't even let us inside. Not only was it the rule that was very weird is that her attitude was very impolite and very hostile. Her tone of voice was very mean and like she was angry and we did nothing wrong.

Indian Accent is one of my favorite restaurants anywhere.  Not just in New York.  It's a bit expensive, to be sure, but it is completely worth it.  It's a culinary experience, one which you won't soon forget.  This is not your typical Indian restaurant- it's not fusion in the sense of everything being too new-fangled and unfamiliar and seemingly unnecessary, but the dishes are slightly different than what you'd find in your usual Indian restaurant.  It is obvious that Chef Mehrotra has put a lot of thought and care and creativity into each dish, and it shows.  Everything you taste or sip here will be special, trust me.

I've been here twice with my brother, and both times he has come away saying "Wow that was the best meal I've had in years!"  And I can't disagree with him. The amouse bouche, the drinks, the appetizers, the main courses, the desserts, even the seemingly innocuous dipping sauces- everything is freaking awesome.

Some of the dishes that have stood out to me over my two visits are the Kerala moilee curry, the spicy crab, the soy keema pav, the sweet potato chaat, the saffron malai dessert, and the coconut jaggery kheer dessert.  But like I said, it's all good.  Come here with an empty stomach and get ready to be wowed.
Quality and taste were top notch! But the portions were tiny. Don't think I have ever spent soooo much $$$$ and still left a restaurant hungry. We had to get a pizza after my dinner here

I was amazed by the flavors and presentation of all the courses. I did choose to do the 3 course and it was a lot of food! The best was the makhan malai dessert which was super airy and light in texture but packed with so much flavor in every bite. I would highly recommend checking out this restaurant. Reservations are a must! 

Service is top notch as well! Richard was amazing and went above and beyond to be hospitable and welcoming! He gave us great recommendations and helped guide us through the three courses.

Outstanding Indian food true to its flavors. We did the chefs tasting menu and tried a couple of cocktails. Everything was fantastic and great experience with the staff. Place can be a little noisy for a fine dining exp but overall ambiance was great.
Love love love it. Great Indian, with a small twist that they successfully added ! Sometimes dishes can be slightly too spicy, make sure to ask for the food the way you like it.

I highly recommend this restaurant. The cuisine is a truly innovative blend of flavors, the presentation is gorgeous, and the service is impeccable. Some of the highlights were the mutton dahi vada, the assamese pork dumplings, the ghee roast lamb, and the asparagus poriyal.  The complimentary pumpkin soup in the tiny earthen beer stein was also a delight. All the dishes were familiar but with intriguing twists that made for a unique and memorable experience.The only caution is the pricing -- the bill is not for the faint of heart so make sure to go for a special occasion! We chose Indian Accent for a college send-off dinner for our daughter, which was a perfect way to mark a life transition.

Made a reservation to celebrate my wife's birthday along with our 4 year old son. Landed up there to be told that "we don't seat children under 10 years of age". Shouldn't this be made clear on the website or the booking app? They pointed to a confirmation email which apparently says this - and its in this small fine print at the bottom of the email. Shouldn't this be made prominent so folks don't have a terrible experience and are left high and dry? They make it clear they require a credit card to make a reservation. So they can make things clear if they want to.
Terrible experience being left without a reservation on Saturday night in NYC.

There are only a handful of places that can take the traditional dishes and flavors of well established staples and transform them into something new and innovative. I typically don't go for fusion style places, but Indian accent is the real deal. Taking from more Northern influences, the chef manages to combine nostalgia with outside influences. I am a big fan of the prix fixe menu as it enables you to experience a wide array of dishes - each uniquely distinct. Everything I ordered was sensational, only matched by world class service that was attentive and almost militant. Would definitely come back!

This place is quite expensive and is more for a date night or special celebration.  They only offer a tasting menu of either 3 of 4 dishes for dinner.  I got a glass of wine for $20 and it was literally half a glass which I found annoying considering I was paying so much for everything.  My husband and I both got the 4 dish tasting menu.  For my first course, I got the potato chaat which was probably my favorite dish of the evening.  The chutney on it was so flavorful and tangy which made the potato pop.  My mid-course was the smoked eggplant which came in cute little cones which I wasn't expecting.  My husband got the prawns which I really liked.  For our mains, we got chicken malai tikka and tandoori salmon.  The salmon was cooked well though on the creamy side.  I loved my side of butter chicken kulcha, which is basically stuffed bread.  I wasn't a huge fan of the dessert and chose the manhandled malai which was basically like eating air.  It didn't taste like any substance which was odd to me.  It came in a huge bowl.  I wish I had chosen something else and thought it would be more like kulfi.

I've been to many nice and fancy restaurants, i value quality and taste first and foremost, followed by service.  This didn't meet any of those.  This was the worst Indian/fusion food I've ever had.  Service was bad too.  The food was over priced for the quality and quantity you get, and tasting like the way it did I wouldn't want more quantity either.  Gives a bad name to Indian food.  I wouldn't even give it 1 star.

I came to Indian Accent five years ago on my Birthday and it was outstanding!!. I could not wait to get back and made it back today. A bit of a disappointment. Five years ago, I was treated like a star: the food and service were excellent! ! Today, while the food held up, the service did not. While the Waiters were well meaning, responsive and nice,  the attempt to call my Tito's and Club Martini's ,with a up charge, and not acknowledging my Birthday as they did , 5 years ago, has reduced my rating .  As a native Washingtonian, it was Rasika's fierce competitor.  No more!!

Indian accent far exceeded all my expectations...and if I could give more stars I would. 
This was one top notch restaurant truly on top of their game .
Stellar service from the minute we walked til we left. Pristine inside, minimalist decor, but just enough. Nice sleek bar area. 
I've heard nothing but amazing things about the food here, and it was the first place I reserved when I knew I was coming to New York . 
You have to be a real foodie to appreciate the menu, and their twist on all things normal. It's not your average Indian restaurant type of menu. 
They offer a 3 course pre fixe  menu, which we went with. Also offer a 4 course if your up for more food!
Drinks are of course extra, and they have a amazing wine list and some really interesting cocktails with Indian ingredients.
My friend and I picked two different items from each course so we could share. 
They start you off with blue cheese stuffed naan with a coconut curry soup. Not a fan of blue cheese I just had the soup, which was awesome, and served in the cutest little cups. Such good coconut flavor and spices. This was a great tease of things to come. 
First course I ordered the potato sphere chaat, with a white pea mash , this  was visually amazing and tasted excellent, crunchy potato and the well spiced pea mash, with the chutneys, it all comes together so well. Definitely get this!
My friend got the chili pork Phulka , comes  out like a taco, the phulka bread was stuffed with veggies and the chili pork, was tender and had great flavor. Filled to the brim this was another excellent choice. 
Second course I went with the prawns, with butter pepper garlic sauce and cauliflower , again wow, on the flavors, and the combination of prawns and cauliflower. Loved this. 
My friend got the sweet pickle ribs and those were so unique and Fantastic. Great thick sauce covered the ribs and presented like a popsicle. Great  presentation again. 
The final course, I was dying for this one! The paper roast dosa, with wild mushrooms water chestnuts, and gunpowder. This was such a pretty dish! And I loved the mushrooms inside the dosa. And you never knew when you'd get a hit of water chestnuts mixed in with the mushrooms. 
Great take on the South Indian classic.
The chicken malai tikka in a green chili cream, with summer truffles, wow. Another twist on a classic chicken tikka masala. Rich dish, loved the cream. The truffles felt very decadent and fancy. 
With the 3 course pre fixe, you get to pick an accompaniment, so I got the green pea and spicy potato kulcha , and my friend got the wild mushroom with truffle butter kulcha . Both of these are like stuffed naan but not as heavy bread. Served nice and hot, I could have made a meal out of the two of these. Great sides, both equally as good. 
This was one of the best food experiences I've had in a restaurant. 
They come out with every course explaining what it is and what's in it. 
Definitely an indulgent culinary adventure. With fantastic service.

If you are in New York City ORR in the area, I highly recommend trying this spot! Note: it is on the expensive end but it is definitely worth the hype and money. You start off with this delicious pumpkin soup shot that was Devine!! Being a vegetarian and a foodie, I was delighted to see Indian food demonstrated in a upscale manner. One point of criticism, I do wish the saag didn't just have raw root veggies at the top. The saffron daulat ki chaat was a perfect way to round up the meal!

Food was very good & each dish was presented in a way that made it fun to eat. Service was also excellent. The only reason I'd give it 4 stars & not 5 is because my boyfriend ended up with terrible heartburn & stomach cramping the next morning.

My absolute favorite fancy Indian restaurant in the city. Very unique dishes and the flavors are just scrumptious. The black dairy dal is what dreams are made off, but every new dish I have tried has been amazing. The only wish now is to see more vegan options (please whoever is listening:)). Impeccable service and lovely ambience!

"Next level Indian"

This is a really unique choice if you want something completely out of the ordinary and to challenge your palette. While not as spicy as some Indian places, the flavors are unusual and intense.

This is a very upscale and high end experience.

Whats to cheer
- Indian food you won't find anywhere else
- Each dish is well crafted 
- good cocktails 
- The lamb ghee was excellent!
- great service 

Whats to jeer
- Had a reservation and still waited for a half an hour for a table. Got comped drinks but still.
- it's pricey

Best Indian hands down in NYC 
Went there two days in row
Excellent drinks, service and dinner 
Esp lamb ! 
Have to make this my one stop everytime I visit NYC

Michelin star rated for a reason!! We all left SO full and content with this place. 

The service is amazing. Patient, kind and they do a nice job of explaining each dish. 

Now, the main part: the food. Absolutely amazing, filled with flavor and solid portions. There were 3 of us, so we ordered different things so we could all try. Highly recommend the beef ribs, the nihari, the pecan pie-esque dessert and the dal. 

It was all SO good!! If you want an upscale experience of flavorful food, head to indian accent.
Food was 5 stars all the way. Service was wonderful. Ambiance fitting of a multi course tasting menu in NYC. Please open one in Seattle.

Fabulous experience. I took my wife there for her birthday. The ambience, service, and food were spectacular

For the appetizer I got the pulkha with jackfruit-awesome 
Wife got chaat-really good 

First course I got soy keema and my wife got smoked eggplant- both really good 

Main course I got the kadai paneer which was excellent and my wife got the vadai which was really good 

For accompaniment we both got dal with garlic naan-awesome. Must get

For dessert I got the pecan pie with ice cream and my wife got the keer. Both were excellent

Worth every penny of the $200 we spent on lunch for 3. And the unbelievably delicious food deserves all the credit. 

First we started with the sphere chaat (not on the lunch menu but kitchen specially made), sweet potato chaat and pork phulka/torta. These were presented beautifully and tasted amazing, especially the rich pork. The 2 chaats were fresh and bursting with tangy flavor. 

Next we had the ghee roast lamb which was absolutely melt in your mouth. The little mini rotis with tamarind chutney were fun to eat and super satisfying. The chicken kofta and kadhi was a little bland so I probably wouldn't order it again. The paper dosa was a fun and interesting combination of flavors. 

Now for dessert - the airy and light makhan malai was daunting in size but not heavy at all. It melts away in your mouth like cotton candy but with pleasant bits of crunchy nuts in between. However the treacle tart stole the show. It was sweet, satisfying, warm and just a perfect end to a memorable meal.
Absolutely amazing!! Can't stop thinking about this meal!! I'm very picky about Indian food and this place lived up to all the hype!! Planning my next trip to NYC right now and I'm coming back again!

Aii y'all let me start off by saying I'm Punjabi right...my boo and I tried this restaurant for his birthday. First things first, I requested a special birthday dessert in my online reservation. Maybe I should've verbally told the staff too, but I thought they would see it in the online reservation as they allow you to specify an option for special occasions! Ultimately, we did not get the special birthday dessert. Anyways... 

We went for the 3-course per person and they give you a complimentary accompaniment as well. Overall, the courses were filling, but for a Michelin star restaurant we weren't super impressed. 

What we liked: 
- The little shot of pumpkin curry was rich and SO delicious. I could've eaten a whole bowl of it and been happy, honestly. 
- Smoked eggplant bharta cornets were really good. Again, super small portions so they were like little bites, but yum and reminded me a lot of my mom's rajma. The cornets tasted like papadum. :) 
- Wild mushroom kebabs with morel pulao were ok. Def not my favorite. 

What we didn't like: 
- Beet and peanut butter tikki as a concept didn't taste successful imo. The peanut butter overpowered any and all other flavor. 
- Green pea & spicy potato kulcha was pretty terrible. The peas were hard. 
- Kadai paneer tasted very odd, almost bitter 
- Makhan Malai dessert. Respected the concept, but it was really Malai ice cream deconstructed into whipped cream 

Just for a quick comparison, we love Tamarind, another Michelin star restaurant in Manhattan. And of course, most if not all of the restaurants (not Michelin star) in Kips Bay/curry hill are pretty darn great, and I have to give a special shout-out to Bhatti Indian Grill. 

Our meal at Indian Accent was all vegetarian, so maybe the meat dishes might've been better. A lot of these restaurants are catered to a certain clientele and that's fine, it is Manhattan, but overall we were not blown away and likely won't be back.

Darling! This was my highlight at a recent trip to the Big Apple. Absolutely delicious food and even better service. My waiter, Jaquy was on point! The meditation cocktail was so yummy. Solid 5 stars. Will definitely be back.

Many told me about how great this place was. I must say, the ambiance is very upscale, as are the prices. The service is outstanding and very attentive and well-timed. This is a great place to have a long meal and conversation, if you have an expense account or disposable income. 

The price of the food matches the upscale feel. While the food was excellent, the serving portions were small and I left hungry. They were also quite skimpy on the spice, even though I asked for my food hotter. 

Overall, it was good and pleasant, but I didn't feel it was worth the price of admission. 

Remember to tip well.

One of the best meals I've had in a long time. Three of us shared the three courses and there was not a false note. The service is impeccable while friendly and the ambience is calm and perfect for a special meal.
Beautiful dinner on an exceptionally cold night in NYC. Many thanks for welcoming us without reservations! Will be back again.
Hands down the best Indian food I've ever had outside of a home cooked meal! Great service, very cordial people. Maybe they could work on getting newer tables but overall an excellent place!!

Loved the tasting menu here! The 3-course is more than enough food. Standouts included the pickled ribs and the stuffed naans. I really loved the pumpkin soup bite at the beginning as well. The food came out very promptly / at a really good pace. I wasn't super wowed by the cocktails and the wine pour was really small, but overall thought this was a really cool high end Indian food experience!

OUTSTANDING food but ... we had dinner at Indian Accent last year for New Year's Eve. We had a wonderful experience, thought we were a bit rushed but overall it was amazing. I think I rated it 5 * then. 

We had such a wonderful experience that this year, we decided to go back for New Year's Eve dinner and it was pretty disappointing. First of all, the menu was the same as a year ago. We were not too keen on going to the same restaurant 2 years in a row at first but we thought it was going to be a new culinary discovery and that I itself was exciting. So we gave it a shot ... i had to say that this time we felt totally rushed, way too rushed. I hadn't touched the amuse bouche and had not had a zip of my cocktail that they served the first course...
Staff is friendly but clearly on a mission, it turned out to be difficult to enjoy the evening.  For the amount of food and the price, it would be nice to give us the time to relax and enjoy. I can't eat that much in that little time !

Excellent dining experience. Great service. 

Not enough vegetarian main options and they ran out of the kadai paneer. Could only get the sweet corn and garlic scapes vadai with quinoa. I really didn't want this, but there were no other vegetarian options. This dish tasted too sweet and like corn soup. 

Black dhal was so good. Desserts are a must here. Drinks were kind of weak.

Great restaurant! We had a wonderful time for our anniversary dinner. Everything was excellent food, drinks, and exceptional service. Our reservation was ready when we arrived and we got a great corner table. Would definitely recommend and plan to return.

Elegant understated interior feels upscale.
We came prepared for a high end dinner experience that would justify the cost.

They didn't disappoint. On the contrary:

Seating was just in time and since it is Midtown New York they correctly assume the early seating are ahead of scheduled performance, and verify the time you want to be out.

You can pick a 3 or 4 Prix fixe menu. We chose the 3, which allowed us to taste 6 great dishes ( see pics).
A very pleasant surprise was complementary mini stuffed naans with 2 shots of red spicy coconut warm drink ( see pic).
The pace of the meal was perfect: lasted about an hour with minimal waits in between courses.
All in all a great gastronomic experience in s very pleasant setting: we plan to come back in our next visit to NYC!

Came back a second time and everything was spot on. The cocktails are amazing and the food was great. The mutton dahi vada appetizer was a bit weird, basically, a dahi vada dish with mutton added to it. But everything else was spot on.

Went here for my anniversary after I had it bookmarked for years. Ordered 2 three course meals, one for me and one for wife. Starters were very average sweet potato and chat both. Main course sweet corn and moilee was good. Kadai paneer was totally unexpected and not good. Deserts were good. Doda burgi was the best item among all items. Overall not worth $80 + tip + tax per person. Nothing extraordinary taste wise.
One of the best meals I've had in NYC in a long time. Great service, a beautiful interior, and some really interesting, flavorful, and well curated dishes. Did not disappoint.

We had a great meal last minute! We had plans for an Indian restaurant across the street but they had a 40 minute wait and we had Carnegie theater tickets!
Indian Accent was full but they seated us at the bar. Super wonderful upscale Indian. Denne at the bar was super helpful, gave us great suggestions
We had a couple appetizers, the shrimp and Cauliflower, and a crispy potato appetizers and a wonderful lamb dish that we shared! All were super flavorful!
They also brought out an amuse bouche of pumpkin coconut soup Called shorba and filled a blue cheese naan bite. The soup was amazing and I loved loved it! Denne had them bring another surprised shot of it and gave me the recipe!!!! I just made it at home and it's so yummy!!!
This is a fun, yum, restaurant!!

Indian Accent offers a fantastic Indian fusion experience that is truly unparalleled. I have visited it a few times by now and continue to be impressed by the quality of the dining experience. Highly recommend!
had a great valentines day meal here!! interior was cute and good for a date night. I enjoyed all of the dishes, definitely the most unique Indian food I've ever had. I'd recommend trying it out!! :)

Indian Accent is a fine-dining restaurant located in the heart of New York City, serving up contemporary Indian cuisine that is both innovative and delicious. From the moment you step inside, you are greeted by a warm and welcoming atmosphere that sets the tone for an exceptional dining experience.

The menu at Indian Accent is a fusion of classic Indian dishes with a modern twist. Each dish is beautifully presented and bursting with flavor, showcasing the chef's creativity and skill. The standout dishes include the duck khurchan, a dish of shredded duck with a spicy tomato sauce and mini uttapams, and the paneer cheesecake, which combines the creamy texture of paneer with the sweetness of cheesecake.

The service at Indian Accent is impeccable, with attentive and knowledgeable waitstaff who are eager to assist with any questions or requests. The wine list is extensive, with a variety of carefully curated options that pair perfectly with the bold flavors of the food.

The ambiance of the restaurant is elegant and refined, with sleek decor and comfortable seating. The lighting is dimmed to create a cozy and intimate atmosphere, perfect for a romantic dinner or a special occasion.

Overall, Indian Accent is a standout restaurant that offers an exceptional dining experience. The innovative cuisine, impeccable service, and elegant ambiance make it a must-visit for anyone looking for a memorable culinary adventure in the heart of New York City.

What a wonderful experience!! Presentation right on point!!
Remember to make reservations or you won't get in and have a good time....

Came to Indian Accent on a Wednesday evening. The food was outstanding: Indian with a lot of creativity and fusion. We ordered the four course and we had:
- Drinks: Mughal Fortification (awesome), Tiger Paw (Good not great)
- Amuse: Blue cheese mulch's and a pumpkin soup - delicious
- Starter: mutton dahi vada/green tomatoes (amazing) and assamese pork dumplings/broth/nettle oil/crispy black rice(so good)
- Second: sweet pickle ribs/sundried mango/onion seeds(amazing), prawns/butter-pepper-garlic/cauliflower (so good)
- Main: tandoori salmon/lemon-butter peas/herb oil (not good) and ghee roast lamb/roomali roti pancakes (amazing)
- Accompaniment: butter chicken kulcha/sundried fenugreek (amazing)
- Dessert: makhan malai/saffron milk/rose petal jaggery brittle/almonds (not good), dada barfi treacle tart/vanilla bean ice cream (so good)

Can't wait to come back here. The service , while friendly and attentive was the greatest at selling items on the menu or describing them well but the recommendations were actually good so not a big deal. The prices were expensive but the quality was high.

I enjoyed the food. 80% of the dishes were really good. My favorites were the dessert and the taco. I found the menu to be kind of confusing but the waiter was super helpful. 
The concept is kind of pretentious. It's not an Indian restaurant like we expected but an American restaurant with an "Indian accent." 
Pretty expensive so probably would not go back but glad I tried it out.

Finally got to try this much talked about Indian restaurant. It is pretty well maintained and staff seems well trained.
They offer three course or four course menu to pick from at an affordable price, as per NewYork standard. They do have a good selection  but the options are limited if you are pescatarian or vegetarian. Meat eaters can have a field day.
We were a party of four so we ordered a  variety of options. 
Beetroot tiki with goat cheese raita and pulled pork tacos were two great appetizer options but if you had to pick one, go for lamb dahi vada; innovative and delicious.
Interestingly they have mid course option. I tried smoked the delicious egg plant bharta cornet with goat cheese mousse. Indeed an aesthetically pleasing dish. My friend tried tofu vada, not the best I would say.

The star of the night was the Prawns kolivada with malvani dried shrimps pulao. This dish awakened all my senses. 
Another great option for mains was ghee roast lamb. Specially calling out that the presentation was mind blowing
They also let you pick accompaniments with mains like pea, mushrooms and other types of kulcha. 
I do think you get a good bank for your buck. I have heard a lot about this restaurant and rightfully so. Dining here is a delight that one must experience at least once.

Excellent service, staff was friendly! I liked most food items I tried and dessert was also amazing. Variety of drink options! The black daal and naan, most appetizers were good. The only item I didn't like was Pao bhaji.

We went to Indian accent because someone gave us a 150 dollar gift certificate. it was my sons birthday and we went with my husband, three kids and elderly parents. The price is $85/pp without drinks for a three course meal. My 91 year old father hardly eats and we requested that he just order a la carte for himself. The manager very rudely answered "absolutely no exceptions" and we were tempted to leave but for the fact that my dad cannot move around easily. The manager then walked back to our table and yelled at us for having our water bottle visible on the table. I made a joke about not getting carded and a very severe response to my joke was made, rather than joining me in my humor. I was told that if I made that remark it would require them to card everyone and if someone didn't have ID then there would be no drinks allowed. If you end up with a bill for 850 dollars for 7 people you want to feel like you were treated with joy and enthusiasm and not like bad schoolchildren. The food was good for the most part, if haute Indian cuisine is your thing. Tiny portions with eclectic tastes. It would have been more palatable for half the price and double the customer service. By the way this is my first review ever. I have never felt so emboldened to write one before but because of the circumstances I felt that it was the responsible thing to do.

My favorite NYC restaurant (and not just because my wife likes it even more). This place redefines the word inventive. The menu is a challenging delight and you may find it a bit daunting, but the staff will guide you. And don't miss the cocktails!

The lamb ghee was excellent. The shrimp was also very good. Portions are somewhat on the small side considering the price point the drinks are excellent. I had this smoky something drink, which was very good and boozy. But I like the tequila drink better the lamb dhai vada was definitely different and interesting. But after eating all of those dishes which we shared, I left a bit hungry... the bartender Danny is a super great guy. I will try it again but this time I would order the blue cheese naan. I love the fact that the chef gave us some items to try the coconut soup was fabulous.

It was a beautiful experience at Indian acent. We were served 3 course meals. Each meal was perfect portion and unique display. The service and ambiance was really good to celebrate our first valentines day.

Best high end Indian restaurant in NYC!!! Absolutely delicious food, every dish is just perfect in terms of flavor, taste and presentation. Coocktails are just amazing!!! It's a great place to celebrate special occasions. Service is amazing!! You really are made to feel special at this restaurant. We went to celebrate our anniversary, and staff was graciously wishing us!! Location is great esp. If you are going for a Broadway show! Love Indian accent and best part is they have maintained the quality of food and the whole vibe of the restaurant for years. Kuddos to consistency!!! Definitely recommend....

This had been my partner's and my third time dining at Indian Accent. All three times we were completely blown away by the food and service. We got the three course tasting menu, and some standouts included the sweet pickle ribs, butter chicken kulcha, potato sphere chaat, the makhan malai, and the smoke and spice cocktail. A seriously perfect 35th birthday celebration.

This was my first time visiting Indian Accent located in NYC as I had previously been to the one in Delhi, India. The ambiance and decor were quite tasteful, and the service was spectacular. We ordered a completely vegetarian spread, and some of the highlights were the beetroot chaat (very unique - must try!), the cheese kulcha (soft cheesy bread bites), the sesame coated kofta (unquie gravy with a crunch to the koftas) and the halwa tart (not too sweet but def on the heavy side). All in all, a great dining experience (although limited to 4 people maximum per table) that I would love to repeat again!

Location, ambiance, service, presentation and food is definitely worth 5 STAR! The server was very attentive and was kind enough to answer all my questions. They serve 3 or 4 course meal for $85 or $98 per person. I would highly recommend this restaurant for perfect date night. Every single course was nicely presented and has lot of flavors. Portions are small but filling. Can't wait to go back!

Amazing food. Highly recommend pretty much anything here; each dish is flavorful and unique. The cocktails are also good -- get the Proper Copper. This place is good for special occasions or slightly fancier meals.

Indian Accent is worth a one-time visit if you enjoy contemporary and inventive Indian food. Although the portion sizes tended to be on the smaller side, my friend and I left pretty full after the three-course tasting menu.

I opted for the lamb dahi vada, chicken malai tikka, butter chicken kulcha, and the makhan malai. The standout dish was definitely the chicken malai tikka- the chicken meatballs were extremely tender, and the addition of truffle to the malai sauce was certainly welcomed. I also enjoyed the butter chicken kulcha, which was a unique take on a popular Indian pairing. The lamb dahi vada dish was good as well but was pretty consistent with most other dahi vada dishes I've had. Unfortunately, the makhan malai didn't live up to the hype for me. I would only recommend getting this dish if you like light and airy desserts. As someone who prefers denser and cakey desserts, I was quite disappointed by this choice.

Overall, Indian Accent is a solid dining option for a special occasion!
Food is very delicious and elegant, service is superior and I think it's more friendly than Japanese restaurant;)
Tasting menu didn't really match high expectations.  Some items required hands and were messy. Service was top notch. Super expensive.

Delicious food. Deplorable front of house 

You can choose between three or four courses.  The food is inventive and delicious. The ambiance is pleasant.  The waitstaff attentive.  However watch out for your bar bill!  My husband ordered a Don Julio tequila, and much to our surprise his shot showed up on the bill for $60.00

We have been to venues before where the waitstaff let us know if a special vintage liquor was being poured or some other reason why a shot might be priced beyond expectations. No one said anything to us when he ordered. When we questioned the bill the server did nothing. 

Disappointed by the disinterest in our upset we paid and as we left the older male at the front of house asked how our meal was. We told him it was delicious but the tequila pricing was a surprise.  He got annoyed with us and said we should have known.  " Don Julio was on the wine list". We pointed out that all of us ordered cocktails made with name brands that were typically priced and this was a surprise. We've ordered Don Julio before and unless it's a special bottle it's never been 60 bucks a pour. He didn't back down. Our friend said" all you have to do is say you're sorry". The response? " I'm not sorry".  

We frequent Indian Accent.  We have introduced many friends to the place. We will not return.  We suggest you don't go.

Modern and luxurious ambiance. Attention to details from start to finish extraordinary service. An utterly lovely Sunday brunch had.

Enlightening all of my senses were my choices made from Indian Accent's 2-course brunch menu of "Sweet Pickle Ribs" and "Uttapam". 

Sublime also were their creative cocktails and an added celebratory dessert of "Spiced Mission Figs".

CHEERS!

My wife and I visited this place to celebrate her Birthday this past Saturday.
I will begin with a positive note. The associates who work there are very nice and trained well to push the prefix menu. If looks matter more than taste then this is the place to go. The presentation of the food is great, but the taste is far from what one can expect from any Indian restaurant. If you are hungry this is not the place for you, the quantity they give for the price you pay is not worth it! My wife is vegetarian and the quantity and quality is not even worth mentioning anything about it!
Last but not least I suffered the night from a mild upset stomach and my wife said she felt uncomfortable as well!
Choose wisely!

Indian Accent's fine dining take on Indian food is worthwhile but not spectacular. The place has an understated look comparable to an upscale American restaurant with low lighting and minimalist decor. We got the four course option and enjoyed it. I'd recommend the lamb entree, which has a $10 supplemental but was delicious. I would avoid the tofu appetizer though as I found it rather bland even with the sauce.

Truly an experience. The ambiance is very relaxing and romantic, and the service was impeccable. Note that you must order a 3 or 4 course pre-fixe menu and cannot order a-la-carte, though I personally liked this as we got to try a bunch of dishes.

In general, everything was flavored really well. The portion sizes varied, though. Apps like the aloo sphere chaat were tiny whereas the lamb dahi vada was pretty filling. The mid courses and entrees were a decent size. The dessert was phenomenal - we loved the makhan malai as it was so different, and the banana cake was a treat!

The price is up there but it's worth it. I highly recommending coming here for any kind of celebration, or just to enjoy a delicious meal and great service!

By far the innovative and delicious Indian food I have ever tasted. I had the 4 course chef's dinner. Each course was even more impressive than the first. Any fears of the spice being overwhelming were quickly abated. The food exhibited a depth of flavor unlike I have ever experienced. My scallops were seared to perfection and the accompanying sea beans were delicious. Every dish was light and satisfying.

Indian accent is excellent in terms of quality but I must state not that they are listening - the quantity of food for the vegetarians versus meat eaters is disparate. For example my sweet potato shakarkandi was a good portion size but my next course tofu vadai should have had 3 pieces instead of the 2 tiny pieces. The last course palak tart was sufficient size but lesser than everyone else on my table who ordered meat. You guys can do better -

Indian Accent was a restaurant that we checked out while checking New York as we had seen recommendations for it online. The inside is decorated very well, with lots of cultural elements portrayed in a modern way. We had a reservation so we were seated instantly and the service was great. For the menu the way they structure it is interesting, as you can choose either 3 or 4 courses from the different sections on the menu (although some sections only allow one)

 For the food we decided to go with the Assamese Pork Dumplings, the Pao Bhaji, the sweet pickle ribs, the prawn koliwada, and the makhan malai for dessert. All of these tasted fantastic, although we really enjoyed the Pao Bhaji and the Prawn Koliwada a lot! The Pao Bhaji was warm and fluffy, which went well with the provided savory sauce.
