The Makhan Malai was also very unique, as the texture and taste is definitely memorable. The saffron and rose petal brittle add a lot of character to the flavors, which I enjoyed a lot!

 Overall, this restaurant was a great experience and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys Indian food!

The reason I gave it a low rating is due to service. Last min reservation. We had heard great things and were really excited.  We arrived early. Had some good drinks at the bar. Then when seated we found out that there was nothing on the menu that didn't have the one item that my colleague was allergic to. We asked them to accommodate and perhaps make something fresh. We were told no. Everything is "premade" (hence buyer beware) and there was nothing they could do. Disappointing! We left after paying for our drinks. Should have seen the red flag when the hostess even said she hadn't eaten there before. While I was excited it's lost its luster.

The food and service here is really impressive, but for me it felt a bit on the stuffy side. Almost too attentive service and too much focus on visuals. I wanted to hold on to the menu just to be reminded of what i ordered as the dishes arrived but they wouldn't let me. It seemed like it would look too messy? So no I don't think I'll return.

If you have money to burn without much interest in the quality of food or service this may be your place. Had Thanksgiving tasting menu without advance notice that there were only 3 options for each course, that included only two options for the main course because one was not even available leaving turkey that tasted like cardboard or a pumpkin main -don't believe this is an Indian staple - as the other options or a replacement dish of prawns that were actually slightly stunted shrimp and cold rice that took forever to arrive. Ah, but management pointed out that you could have seen the actual menu in advance if you scrolled through the reservation notice on Open Table and then espying a throwaway line at the bottom directing you to their web site to click on the Thanksgiving menu. Oops forgot to mention that clicking on the Thanksgiving menu directs you to a Spam site. This was before a fire alarm was followed by 15 minutes of a flashing light and a carrot dessert that , yes tasted like cardboard - and yes, this is a recurring theme. Conversation with management pointing out that notification about the limited cardboard menu was not provided in advance was met with , oh I don't know (yes I do) , complete disinterest.  So many great Indian restaurants in New York, why come here?

Came on a chilly Tuesday night with my sister to celebrate her engagement just as sisters. We chose Indian Accent because we both love Indian food and heard good things which it did not disappoint! The servers here are so kind and the aesthetic is nice! 

We did the prefix course and started with the pulka chili pork and pork dumplings. i was so surprised with how delicious and juicy the chili pork was - a very nice indo mexican fusion with it being in a taco. my sisters dumplings were delicious too

next we did the bone marrow kabob and sweet pickle rib. the bone marrow was so good as well and paired nicely with some naan as its fatty and juicy. the rib was _____ 

for mains we did chicken malai and beef tenderloin with butter chicken kulcha and black daal. the black daal they make here might be the best daal ive ever had!

dessert was banana sticky cake and makhan malai - the makan malai was so airy and light but had all the flavors listed. really loved this - probably my favorite and would recommend. the banana sticky cake was also so so so delish but i was so full by the end felt like i couldnt enjoy it as much since it was heavier

10/10 recommend and would come back

We enjoyed our 3 course meal at Indian accent. Some dishes hit the mark and some were near misses! 

Hits
- jackfruit in phulka. Amazing flavors in jackfruit. I wish the quantity was a bit more. It was the best appetizer and the smallest portion! 
- sweet potato and star fruit was innovative 
- beetroot tikki was rather bland. 
- sweet corn kofta was nice
- tofu Vadai was awesome especially the sauces with it 
- don't miss daal and naan. Daal reminded me of daal Bukhara from Delhi. 
- saag paneer in a tart was unexpected but met the mark. 
- makhan malai dessert was very good

Misses
- eggplant and bhujiya raita was a disappointment. No flavors at all 
- asparagus poriyal missed flavors
- mushroom kebabs were dry and I somehow didn't like it. 

The shorba at the start of the meal was very nice. I wish they had it on the menu!

The food was great with unique twists to Indian dishes. Everything was well prepared with plenty of effort put into the presentation of the dish. Each one had a unique combination of flavors to enjoy. 

The service was also commendable as the staff was informative and attentive. The entire experience from reception to the billing was extremely pleasant. 

As for the ambiance, it was in one word, classy. The interior was reminiscent of a restaurant in London. The location in the city was also in an appropriate area. 

My one concern is that the price did not reflect the amount of food given per serving. As it was a sit down per person, the entire course felt a bit lacking. 

Overall, it was a great restaurant that I would recommend.

Worst hospitality experienced at a restaurant!
I reserved a table for me, my husband and my 1 year old daughter, took an uber on a chilly evening to reach the restaurant which is around 5 miles from my place. 
When i made the reservation, it nowhere mentioned that kids are not allowed at the restaurant. When we reached the restaurant, the receptionist was so rude and was not ready to accommodate us. They agreed that the reservation application does not say no kids policy but no-one at the restaurant had a realization that this caused so much hassle for our family.
No kids basically means NO FAMILIES ALLOWED !! which is so weird. 
So this so called high end restaurant was very low on service, ethics , humanity and hospitality!!

An amazing restaurant.
Before covid-19 I ate in their London restaurant. However, it was shut down.
This is great as it was in London.
Very delicate, sophisticate and delicious food.
Great service and a nice selection of wine and drinks.
Hands down, the best upscale Indian restaurant.

Our experience at Indian Accent was absolutely delightful. Nearly every dish we tried was very different from any other indian restaurants we've dined at. Their cocktails were all very smooth and well crafted too. For the amount they charge for the tasting menu you definitely get your money's worth. The ghee lamb entree was a very interesting take on the traditional chinese peking duck dish. I highly recommend that. 

The accompaniments which reminded me of a stuffed naan were very delicious and fresh - i really enjoyed the butter chicken one. The one with the mushroom also went really well with the chicken malai tikka. 

The saffron milk dessert was sooooo yummy and light! It was definitely my favorite indian dessert. This was the highlight of my meal lol.

I would give this place six stars if I could! This place is an absolute steal - on par with many Michelin-starred restaurants I've been to. 

My sister made a reservation for us here for dinner on Christmas Eve, and it was an utter delight from start to finish. The space itself is sleek and refined. The three of us each opted for the $85 three-course tasting menu, which allows you to make four selections (the entree comes with an accompaniment) each from an expansive menu. It can be hard to decipher what all the dishes on the menu are, and our server was incredibly helpful in giving us recommendations. I would suggest ordering different things if you're in a group and splitting everything so you can try as many dishes as possible. The flavors here are delicate, innovative, and so delicious! 

For our appetizers, we ordered the sweet potato shakarkandi, potato sphere chaat, and assamese pork dumplings. They were all flavorful, but the potato sphere chaat was a standout: crispy, well-textured, and so good. For our mid-courses, we ordered the sweet pickle ribs, which was also stunning: it has the thinnest, crispiest glaze, and the meat just falls off the bone. (I didn't even remember to get a picture until I'd already bitten into it.) For mains, we ordered the chicken malai tikka (juicy, truffly meatballs), the prawn koliwada (delicately breaded), and the baked paneer (not our favorite but still good). For accompaniments, we got two black daals with black garlic and butter naans (so richly flavored) and stuffed pastrami naan (fusion-y and wonderful). And for dessert, we got the makhan malai (unbelievably soft and cloud-like) and banana sticky cake (caramel-y and delicious). 

The $85 price point might seem steep to some, but it is an absolute steal for the amount and quality of the food you get - especially in New York. We were stuffed by the end, and we have pretty hearty appetites! The service is also incredible: they changed out our plates three times, and our water glasses were never empty. As an added bonus, they threw in two complimentary small bites in between some of the dishes. Overall: this was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. I can't wait to be back!
Quite possibly the single, best meal I've ever had. I wish I travelled to NYC more often, just so I could eat here.

We had a beautiful meal here on New Year's Eve 2023. The tasting menu is exquisitely prepared to showcase a variety of dishes. They had a special menu for New Year's Eve so I'm not sure if these dishes are available on the regular menu but the third course - crab and caviar - was heavenly. I would definitely come back here and try the broader menu again. Our servers were also incredibly nice and helpful.
Amazing and very unique experience, elevated Indian food. Tried a lot of new things, the tasting menu is well worth the money!
Spectacular, inventive Indian cuisine. My second time solo dining here, both times at the bar. The bar staff has gone above and beyond to make me feel welcome. The cocktails are fantastic.

An incredible high-end Indian restaurant with an incredible tasting menu. Every bite we had was amazing, the service was prompt despite us coming in at 10pm, and the general vibe of the restaurant is a cozy/calm. The food was inventive, eclectic, and still super balanced. I still think about the beet/peanut butter little bites as one of the most interestingly delicious bites I've had in a long time. I'm shocked they don't have a Michelin star, but I would NOT be surprised if it's coming.

A delicious experience coupled with great service and beautiful ambiance.

I tried the brunch tasting menu which was recently introduced by the restaurant. The restaurant came recommended by friends who had tried their dinner tasting menu and found it delicious. The brunch menu consisted of 2 courses with a choice of accompaniment and additional cost for dessert and drinks. Since I came with a group of friends, we got to try almost all the dishes on the menu. 

Ironically, the amuse bouche was one of the most flavorful dish of the meal. They served the most delicious pumpkin shorba with blue cheese naan. 

First course: Tried the burrata chaat, dried fenugreek papdi chaat, herb potato sago pancake, pao bhaji. My personal favorite was the burrata chaat. I loved the crispy lotus stem and the mustard-tomato jam/chutney in the dish. The jam was extremely delicious. 

Second course: Tried the egg ghee roast, uttapam, baked saffron cauliflower, shrimp and herb omlette. For me, the star of the second course was the saffron cauliflower baked dish. I had never had cauliflower with this flavor profile before. I would recommend giving it a try as it's something unique. 

Accompaniment: Tried the black dairy daal with naan, smoked eggplant and bujia raita, traditional black garlic naan, wild mushroom kulcha. Everything was delicious especially the kulcha and the black daal. 

Dessert: For dessert we could only try the makhan malai. It was pillowy, light, not overly sweet. 

I found the brunch tasting absolutely worth it's cost and would recommend it to anyone looking for fushion Indian fine dine.

Really enjoyed my recent dinner here. The starter of blue cheese stuffed naan and shorba was great, but I'm sure those who don't like blue cheese will be looking forward to the other options. The chaat and vada were really tasty. I wish the bhaaji was spicier, but the mini pavs were unique. The paneer with soy cube was very heavy, but paired well with the naan and daal. We were actually too stuffed to get dessert, which wasn't what we expected, so will have to return to check out their dessert options! Overall a great place to try a fixed menu of Indian food. Reservations needed.

The service and ambiance were excellent! I enjoyed certain dishes more than others even given the large menu selection. If you sit at the bar you can order a la cart, but if you sit down at a table you have to choose between a 3 or 4 course prix fix menu. 

The tenderloin came out a little tough for the main course and they swapped it out for us with the prawns very quickly. The mid courses were my favorites actually, especially the prawns and how they were seasoned, but still very crunchy. The bone marrow was also fantastic and the greatest way to add cholesterol to your diet. The pork ribs, though super tender, didn't stand out beyond just falling off the bones in terms of flavor. The kukcha was absolutely delicious for both the duck and butter chicken, but they didn't have very much filling. I really liked the prawn main course also, but it needed a couple more prawns to round it out. The rice was a nice addition, but even with its color, it didn't add anything taste wise to the dish beyond being visually appealing carbs. 

The desserts were ok, the giant whipped cream was probably the most interesting and felt like barely eating anything. The pecan pie like dessert had great texture, but this was a bonus on the house which I wouldn't have paid for after tasting it. The sago pear was mildly interesting, but wasn't particularly sweet or unique beyond the oversized sago texture. 

I might go back to try the menu another time, but fantastic to try at least once. The experience was great overall even though I wasn't blown away by every dish.

Lovely place, amazing food, and great staff. Maybe it was my party's preference for more traditional Indian cuisine, but this takes a venture to high end Indian cuisine and away from what you come to expect in the States. Only choice was a 3 or 4 course set menu, which wasn't bad for under $100 for each, but it was very heard to decide what was what. At the end, the server helped us out and we were experienced some amazing flavors and exotic dishes. Honestly, this was a great business dinner with my colleagues, but perhaps if I would have been more aware of the high scale offering, I might have chose a bit differently. Regardless, we ultimately truly enjoyed everything and most importantly didn't walk away with any stomach issues afterwards which is a major win for any Indian cuisine. I would be happy to return again someday, now with the necessary expectations.

My boyfriend is Indian so we eat at a lot of Indian restaurants. He had eaten at this restaurant in Delhi so he wanted to try the NYC location. Wow one of the two best Indian restaurants we've eaten at in NYC. I put pictures of everything below. We each had the 4 course and we loved that they let u mix and match. The eggplant "cone" was my absolute favorite but everything was top notch. The restaurant was fancy but still comfortable. It was busy but yet we still felt like we were in a private date. Our server was soooooo attentive and had a great dry sense of humor. Really great expe overall.

My friend and I wanted to definitely try a good fine dine Indian restaurant as NYC has so many of them. We decided to go ahead with Indian Accent which has been recognized by Mindy Kaling and BJ Novak.

We selected a fixed 3 course dinner menu. They start off my offering a complimentary pumpkin soup and blue cheese balls before the dishes arrive. For appetizers we got beetroot kababs, jackfruit phulka (tacos), tofu medhu vada and pav bhaji. Out of all the appetizers, jackfruit phukla was our favorite. This was a modernized Mexican touch to a chapatti which we really liked. My second favorite was tofu vada. I don't think I ever imagined this combination of having silken tofu with a crispy vada covering. The gunpowder even though was less but very tasty. The pav bhaji was OK in terms of taste but it has to be the tiniest pav I have ever seen!
For main course, we got black dal with garlic naan, saag paneer with makhani sauce, wild mushroom kebabs with truffle and mushroom kulcha. I think we liked our apps more than the main dishes. The saag paneer with makhani was our favorite out of the lot! The dal makhani surprisingly was the least favorite as it just did not have any salt. We skipped desert as we'd selected 2 apps each in our 3 course menu as both of us aren't desert people.
The service was a bit average. We were a bit pissed when they offered sparkling water bottle without the lid. What's the point of ordering Sparkling water if the fizz can be easily evaporated? 
Overall, nice sophisticated ambiance. My expectations were slightly higher as this is NYC, taste could be more authentic but at the same time creative.  

P.S. Indian Accent also has it's branches in New Delhi and Mumbai. I visit Mumbai and Delhi very frequently but had never heard about this place before however they have glorious reviews at both of these places and it is very difficult to get a reservation in India!
Great experience!  Food and service were spot on!  We had the 4 course meal and left very happy and full.
This restaurant is pricey, but totally worth it! Each course was delicious, as were the mocktails. And the desserts were phenomenal. Will definitely be back.

Incredibly delicious menu. Phenomenal service. Delicious by-the-glass wine options as well. We took the four tastings ... and found every option to be a magically delicious treat. The desserts were out of this world fabulous -- and I am not a sweets person!  Pricy. Highly recommend.

There was two of us and we had the $85 3-course pre-fixe. THIS MEAL IS MADE FOR SHARING. Come with friends and nibble on everyone's choices, good or bad. There is plenty to go around. There are at least 6 choices in every section. You will have plenty variety. 

Everything we got was kind of amazing (except the khichdi, which was ok). I am a firm believer that appetizers are significantly better than mains at fine dining places. This restaurant did not prove me wrong.

One service-related comment: not saying he was racist, but our server was more interested in taking the order from my white friend than from me (I'm Asian).

appetizers:
1. lamb dahi vada, baked masala beet
2. beet and peanut butter tikki, goat cheese raita

mid-courses:
3. smoked eggplant bharta cornet, goat cheese mousse
4. sweet pickle pork ribs, sundried mango, onion seeds

mains:
5. branzino, patrani butter, berry pulao
6. khichdi, crispy sunchokes with achari mutton

accompaniments:
7. hoisin duck kulcha
8. black dairy dal with naan: butter, plain, garlic or black garlic

I ate at this restaurant a year before COVID and had an amazing experience. I went back to them during my recent visit because I again wanted to eat their ghee roast lamb which was AMAZING last time I was here. However I have to say that their quality has gone down.  Servers and staff still amazing , I sat at the bar and staff there were soooo nice. Ordered a scotch drink called Smokin on server recommendation and it was great. Ordered lamb with yogurt a new dish and it was just wow (everyone should try). Then I ordered the dish I came here for ghee roast lamb. Sorry but very disappointed as it was very bland and had so much tomato sauce that there was no flavor. Server was gracious to change the dish and I ordered for chicken malai tikka. Sorry to say but please don't call this dish chicken malai tikka. This was chicken meat ball and even then chicken was not minced. I didn't want to send the dish back and hence said it's ok. But very disappointed and won't recommend this dish. Also ordered dal and naan. Dal was good and naan just ok (same as any other restaurant). Being at Michelin star restaurant the expectations are high. But a BIG disappointment this time. Not sure if they have changed the chef. Also what surprised me was speed with which dishes were coming out. It seems like everything was premade and they were just pouring on plates. Sorry to say but restaurant need to increase their standard and come back to quality it had pre COVID. Thanks to the staff and bar whose service was great and reason I gave an additional star.

Had been looking for an Indian restaurant with actually really good and authentic Indian food (really hard to come by in New York) and the food here did not disappoint. I had the three course menu and the portion sizes were just the right size. Not pictured here was the complimentary amuse bouche they brought at the start which was honestly the highlight of the meal, I could have had 5 more. I didn't quite hear what it was but my friend and I LOVED it. Some kind of bread thing and chai flavored soup? Anyway it was delicious. The shrimp and crab were cooked perfectly and very flavorsome. I wasn't too sold on the desserts or the ambience but overall a great dining experience.
The best food and service ever!!! It's an incredible team and all very attentive. Highly recommend if you're in NYC!!!

Indian accent is phenomenal! From the presentation, ambience, and staff it was an amazing experience. My friends and I opted for the 4 course meal and it was plenty of food. We were full by the time the main course came out! The server was very thoughtful and assisted my party while we decided between the different dishes. We decided to try different dishes and share our meals.

My favorite dish of the night was the warm Doda Barfi tart with vanilla ice cream. The tart was rich and decadent and on the sweeter side but paired remarkably well with the ice cream.

Excellent restaurant. Went for brunch and my favorites were the chicken salad, beef chili dubba gosht and the kulcha butter chicken (favorite).

Admittedly, the dried fenugreek papdi chaat was not for me.

It's a bit hard to write this review, but I felt like this place had no soul or passion. The decor lacked an elegant ambiance, could use some art on the walls, and a more modern feel to accompany the fine dining. It's in the middle of tourist central, so it really needs to be an escape from that to fully immerse you. 

The service was not in line with the prices. Our waiter never checked in after taking our order. The service was fast. They should have explained the dishes better to us.  They source fresh products from the market, but they never talked about it. We learned about it by accident, when one of the ingredients on the menu was different. This is poor training and execution of the dining experience. 

The food was good, but it could be better, take more risks and without the overall experience and service it doesn't quite give you a feeling of wow.  

I would skip this for a more neighborhood spot.

I went in for brunch on a Sunday with two friends. Food was a solid 4, dessert was a 5 and the service was out of the world! It was the best service on our trip and the team looked like they were all working really well together and happy to be there. I'm definitely coming back when I'm in the city again. Kudos to the service team!

Sophisticated atmosphere, attentive service and every dish was stunning, I will defiantly add this place to my roster. Brought my mom here who is vegetarian. I wanted to take her to a place where there was more then one option to choose from and this place did not disappoint. Very delicious cocktails, I tried 2 and really enjoyed them both. We had one 3 course and one 4 course and shared the appetizers. The waiter let us know we could mix and match any 3 or 4 except the entrees, can only choose one. He said we can even just order all desserts if we want and after trying 2 of their desserts, I might take them up on that one day, hahahaha! The names are long, it's faster just to take a look at my photos for exact dishes. I honesty think anything you order here, it would be delicious, except the entrees were a little disappointing.
Delicious food, one of the best Indian eateries in the US. The drinks are lovely and we enjoyed this space for a special occasion

We went there for a birthday celebration and we're so glad we did. The ambiance, the staff, the food everything was top notch. 
You can choose between a 3 or a 4 course option. The best part is, they let you choose and customize your options such that you can pick all 3 courses as appetizers or even all 3 deserts if you wanted. 
We opted for the vegetarian options. 
It started with amuse-bouche, which was pumpkin soup and stuffed naan, served in the cutest possible way! They even gave us a second round of the soup when we said we liked it so much.
For appetizers,  we got potato sphere chaat and the shakarkandi chaat. Both were nice, but I liked the potato sphere chaat better.
For mid course, we opted for pao bhaji and tofu medu vadai. They had their own versions of the dishes but the authenticity of the taste was not lost. The pav bhaji was surprisingly light.
For main course, we went with baked paneer and soy keema, along with arbi shaami. The arbi shaami kabab was just melting in the mouth. For accompaniments we took stuffed mushroom truffle kulcha , and naan with daal.
I was stuffed by the end of this, and decided to change my preference to stick with the three course menu instead. My husband took the Aamras with fresh cut mangoes. 
The staff was just too nice, they still got me a smaller version of makhan malai to celebrate my birthday. Both the desserts were amazing! 
All in all, if you are in NY, please visit this place. I know I am going back!

Flavorful and delicious food - more American / international forward taste with indian-inspired flavors. 

Portion sizes were on the smaller side but service was great and ambiance is perfect for a romantic date night or a work meeting.

My post-birthday dinner spent with husband and daughter, was lovely.  At 7:00 p.m. Tuesday, the dining room was quiet. By 9:00 the place was jumpin'.

The menu is described as "inventive Indian cuisine using global ingredients and techniques."  One can choose the three or four course prix fixe.  We shared dishes, enabling us to sample so much more!  It's important to savor each bite, and even with small portions we had leftovers.  Everything, starting with the amuse bouche, was perfect.  The only dish not as well-received, was the tenderloin.  If vacillating about your main, go with the branzino.

Indian Accent's wine list is 20+ pages.  The sommelier, a lovely woman respectful of our budget, recommended a wonderful red.  I'll add that everyone in the restaurant was gracious and helpful.  

Indian Accent isn't necessarily the best restaurant I've gone to, but a smidge under five stars, it's worthy of excellent reviews.

This place deserves a 10 star, everything was curated and so flavour full, service was phenomenal. I went with a 4- course meal
1. Aloo sphere chat
2. Prawn appetiser 
3. Rumali roti+ghee roast lamb with butter chicken kulcha
4. Banana sticky cake 
I was impressed by the quantity of the food and presentation, menu had decent vegetarian options as well. I would recommend this place and it's a must visit

Can I get a HOLY SHIT in here?!! One of the best meals I've had in my LIFE.

My friends and I were celebrating a birthday and heard they take the CEO of our company to the India location of this restaurant when he visits so of course we gotta try it for ourselves. A reservation for 4 for a Monday night was easy to get a few weeks ahead of time. 

They offer a 3 or 4 course tasting menu (I'm not sure if they offer a la carte items). Definitely go for the 4 course because it's only $10 more than the three course. My friends and I coordinated and ordered something different for each course and then ate the dishes family style to try more options - definitely recommend! 

I forgot exactly what we ordered but every dish was an incredible fusion of classic Indian flavors with a few East Asian and california fresh inspiration. The highlights were the shrimp mid course, the brazino (sea bass) main, and everything in the dessert course. 

I also ordered the bourbon, apricot, and sage cocktail and was impressed that it was flavorful but not too sweet or watery. 

I will be dreaming of this meal for a while and scheming how to get back to New York to eat again.

Logistics:
- there's indoor and outdoor seating but avoid the outdoor because it was basically on the sidewalk and not the vibe for the tasting menu 
- reservations recommend
- it's Manhattan so there isn't really any parking but close to subways and Central Park
- you can create two different vegetarian or pescatarian tasting courses

Absolutely loved Indian Accent. 2 course meal with a variety of options. The chaat was delicious! The doda barfi and malai desserts were out of this world amazing!! Would return just for the dessert. Great and fast service. Restaurant is clean and great for photos. Paid garage parking adjacent.

Food has been a bit oily and tiering compared to the one I experienced last year around the same time. IA - you can do better and I expect a better whiskey list. I.e., include Jameson and JD which commoners like me prefer.

$800 for 3 ppl 
Only 2 drinks but boy it's expensive 
Love the fantastic food and ambiance 
That's a steep price not sure we will be doing it much often
Great food and service. Everything tasted amazing and was so unique. Server was very helpful. Overall a great experience.
Amazing food, service & Ambiance too. I like the chef tasting menu option here. We have visited here few times and the food is consistent and delicious always.

The food is a joke. Serving sizes are tiny (not small) you barely taste the food and it's finished. Ambiance is nothing. It doesn't feel like a classy place at all. With so many choices in the City, I would avoid this place and find any other Indian restaurant. Their servings are made for a doll house.

I would honestly give this a place a 3.8 if I could on here.
The food was decent however not upto the mark like other nice Indian places in New York or like the Indian Accent in Delhi.

The service was good and they did offer us an anniversary cake which was very sweet of them and that doodha cake was great :) 

The ghee roast was good. The dal was average. Also felt the paneer dish was average and hard. 
The butter chicken naan was really good!!!

First.  I can provide receipts with credit card statements.  

I was there yesterday with some friends from Pittsburg.  This place is a con and a trap.   Let me explain.  For anyone who knows Indian food even a bit, any mediocre resturant or a house cook can make better tasting food.  I think this place is geared for diners who are new to the taste of Indian food.   And cannot make out the difference between good and mediocre.   Absolutely bad food. Some dishes were also unhealthy in addition to below average, sub par taste.  

Let me talk about the "trap".   As soon as I entered, was given a firm statement. You have until 8 pm.  From then on, you are constantly looking at your watch.  I ordered the 4 course meal.   Had to gobble it up.  Have been to 100's of nice restaurants in NY over the last 30 years.  Never been forced to gobble up my food.  

I would rate it a 2 out of 10.  10 being the highest.   

Service was good.  Left a $100 tip.   Not the fault of the guys serving.  Fault lies with the ownership and management.   

There are many other high end Indian Resturant's in town.  Skip this one please.
Excellent food and service! Loved the Burrata chat and the dal. Garlic naan and paratha were excellent as well.

Can't rave enough about this place. We tried several other India  fine dining restaurants in NYC. This place was the best by far. Excellent service. I can't think of anything negative to say about this place. We got the prefix 3 course. Start to finish it was just delicious. My favorite dessert was the tart. Do me a favor and get it. Skip the sticky banana dessert  IMO.

Potato sphere chaat and tofu medu vada were decent but soy keema, baked paneer very disappointing. Service was fine except one of new waiter was little bit nervous in explaining which is understandable! Good for one time but def not again. Overall less than average compared to other fine dining places in city for food and service.

Fantastic restaurant, my wife and i went here before the theatre and had a wonderful time.    My vegetarian wife found lots to eat here and i found the food to be wonderful and authentic.   

The potato chat, the tikka malai, and the eggplant barrata were all fantastic.   

Highly recommend

Fantastic place for an upscale, vegetarian-friendly pre fixe. I've been here twice and loved it both times! Attentive service, spacious restaurant, and great flavor combinations. My favorites were the mushroom kulcha, pumpkin soup, and malai dessert. Would love to visit again!

This was an interesting chance to try some fusion Indian food that's more aligned with western fine dining. My friends and I each had the three course lunch. All the dishes were tasty and beautifully presented.

- First Course -
Pao bhaji - incredible. The bread was fluffy and buttery with subtle herbal flavor, and the curry was warm and spicy. The ricotta vada added nice textural contrast.

Shakarkhandi - subtle sweet and sour flavors with a starchy sweet potato, and nice crunch from the okra. I wasn't expecting this dish to be cold, but it was otherwise fine.

Tofu vadai - a bit soft for my taste, but great presentation. Probably the best looking dish in my opinion.

- Main Course -
Potato kofta - the kofta have a breadcrumb coating which gives it a crispier texture than what you'd see at a typical Indian restaurant. The choice to serve it over khadi (sour yogurt based curry) instead of the standard cashew and cream based gravy was unexpected, but good.

Uttapam - I'm vegetarian, so I didn't try this.

- Side Dishes -
Chana masala kulcha - probably my favorite part of the meal, even though it was just a side. The bread is fluffy and stuffed with a spicy, rich chana masala. The bread is hearty and can basically be eaten on its own. Don't miss it!

Raita - more or less standard, though I've never seen avocado in raita before. Not bad, but not special.

Sesame vegetables - a nice side dish, but nothing special. It's stir fried vegetables with a sesame paste based sauce.

- Dessert -
Doda barfi - absolutely delicious warm tart with heavy toffee like flavor, paired with a light ice cream and crunchy bits on top. This was a top contender for my favorite part of the meal as well and definitely stepped up the whole experience. 

Cheesecake and kheer - this was the dairy free dessert option. The flavors are nice and light, and nothing is too sweet.

Banana sticky cake - a nice warm banana bread. The ice cream has a unique flavor from the jaggery, and I really enjoyed it.

The restaurant was fantastic about handling dietary restrictions. After tax and tip, the meal worked out to about $68, which is worth it for the experience.

I can always appreciate good Indian food and can say we enjoyed our dinner here. We had reservation for a weekend dinner and service was overall friendly and helpful. 

We liked the food and the fine dining Indian cuisine. Lots of different flavors that came through the spices with each meal uniquely special and separate from another.

Intimate spot that's dimly lit and definitely has that upscale restaurant energy. If you like Indian food, I'd say this place is worth a try for sure.
Excellent take on Indian food done at a very high level of quality and flavor and sophistication. The service was excellent and the ambiance very pleasant.

Came here for Diwali and even though there were minor mishaps with the service, I would come back here for the ghee roast lamb! It honestly was such a phenomenal dish!! Especially with the sauces and roomali rotis (sort of like small versions of the pancakes you get with Peking duck). Ambiance is nice, but like the service, not anything special. Would return for the food! If you go, get the lamb!

Definitely one of my new favorite NYC spots. This place struck a perfect balance of Indian flavors while being creative with other fusions. The dal, the lamb, the tikka masala, the chaat, absolutely everything was perfect. Hugely recommended!

Indian Accent is a culinary masterpiece! The innovative fusion of traditional Indian flavors with modern techniques is truly impressive. Every dish is a work of art, both visually and taste-wise. The service is impeccable, and the ambiance is elegant and sophisticated.

We came here to celebrate my husband's birthday and picked the 3 course option, which was more than enough food. The ambience is nice and the service superb. I enjoyed the food as well, but noticed that I'm not the biggest fan of fusion dishes in general. They did have some fun options though!

I highly recommend this place! We came here for dinner and the three course menu was AMAZING. Truly worth the price - the concept was an interesting take on Indian food and just so decadent and rich. Definitely come here for a great meal and beautiful interior

Such an experience. Probably the best service/most attention from dining staff that I have ever received during a dining experience in New York City. The food was incredible, one of the few places I've been to that has done Indian fusion right. If my mom knew how much I spent on medhu vadai and khichdi she would probably kill me but personally it was well worth it. Some of my favorite items were the pulled jackfruit phulka (unique and tasted incredible), the tofu medhu vadai (to my South Indian friends pls don't make fun of me it was really good), the baked paneer with soy kheema, the khichdi (pls don't make fun of me for this either it was incredible) and the makhan malai.

Excellent Spot.  Very interesting take on the Indian cuisine.  Although some dishes left me scratching my head a little bit.  

We came here for a business lunch.  The 3 course tasting is second to none.  The atmosphere is very posh with coat check at the door and quiet service with all the servers doing everything quietly and precisely as if the well choreographed military operation. :)  The dishes are very tasty but Sweet Pickle Pork Ribs although excellent puzzles me still.

Had a 3 course:

Sweet Pickle Pork Ribs,
Baked Barramundi with side of Kashmiri Morel Pulao
Barfi Treacle Tart.

All melting on your tongue like the best dishes should.

I left a review already but I think it deleted. We went for dinner on January 6, I got food poisoning the morning of January 7 and my mom got food poisoning the night of January 8. I have recovered enough to type this but my mom is still going through it. We shared the chicken malai tika. To add insult to injury, the service was overall rude. PLEASE don't go here.

Had a lovely experience here with my family. The tasting menu had several vegetarian options and everything we ordered was both unique and tested phenomenal. Even though the courses were smaller, by the end of our meal we were all stuffed and didn't even have room for dessert. The service was excellent and attentive.

This is my favorite midtown 
* upscale restaurant (it feels like upscale French, Italian, steak)
* Indian restaurant (the food is thoughtfully prepared and ventures into the "fusion" world)
* chill restaurant (you don't feel it's upscale or Indian, just relaxing)
Maybe one of these days they'll give me a seat as a walk-in! 
;)
